   670	**Singleflight LANE identity is NARROWER than the reuse oracle.** The coalescing-lane identity is `StoreViewCompatToken`, whose `validity_fingerprint` is the `lane_fingerprint` — delegating to `external_supersession_fingerprint`, the SAME oracle the promotion fence `is_stable` applies. The fingerprint folds ONLY the external-supersession dimensions: `store_view_epoch` + `project_generation` + workspace `content_generation` (file-set mutations — watcher recovery / dependency appearance — advance it without any host-side epoch; a snapshot's edge-currency gates evaluate against it at build time, so a cached snapshot MUST miss once it moves; a cold compute's own loads never advance it, so it cannot self-fence) + folded env hashes (`env_hash_fold`) + `project_identity` + frozen overlay identity. The additive generations (`artifact_generation` / `load_generation`) are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the lane identity: a cold compute advances them through its OWN work (materialising content-addressed caches gated by `store_view_epoch`, loading its dependencies, admitting its own routes), so two identical concurrent requests snapshot at slightly different points in the load sweep — folding those generations would split them across separate lanes and spawn multiple cold winners instead of one leader + N-1 dedup-joining followers. Because the lane oracle IS the promotion oracle, a follower that joins a lane shares exactly the external dimensions the leader's promotion was gated on, so the leader's dedup-joined result is validation-equivalent for it; and a request whose snapshot externally-supersedes the leader's (an epoch / project / env / identity / overlay change, even at an equal `store_view_epoch`) gets a different lane key and forks its own lane — it never receives a result computed under a different external view. The complete `StoreViewValidationToken` (including the additive generations) REMAINS the store-view reuse/validity oracle — the `StoreViewManager` rebuilds its base snapshot on any additive-generation change; only the LANE identity was narrowed (reuse-oracle = full token; lane-identity = external fingerprint).
   671	
   672	**Base-view build:** no-torn-return (a coherent capture or `Superseded`, never a torn publishable view) and SINGLEFLIGHTED — on a token miss exactly one caller sweeps while concurrent token-miss callers wait on a condvar and clone the winner's `Arc<StoreViewSnapshot>` (no N-way parallel sweeps). The component-meta cold publish fence rechecks the computed-under token against the live host before promotion (mismatch → return-only, no shared-cache warm), keying off `externally_superseded_by` so the compute's OWN artifact publications do not self-fence.
   673	
   674	**Captured resolution root (C5a).** The snapshot also stamps the workspace's immutable published resolution world (`Option<Arc<verter_workspace::CapturedResolutionWorld>>`, captured O(1) in the same `PreBuildTokenInputs` read window via `WorkspaceRead::capture_resolution_world`: the current base root plus, for a session population, that session's overlay root). It is the SOLE authority for the `ResolveImportsFactRef::Resolution` arm — `HostStoreView::validates_resolution_fact` (shared by `validates_resolve_imports_domain` and its overlay-aware `_for_content_hash` sibling; `RequestStoreView` routes resolution facts straight to the base view because the completion overlay carries no resolver observations). A view with NO captured world validates no resolution fact. It stays OUT of the token because validity is fact-precise (world IDENTITY is barred from being a cross-root warm-validity oracle) and because a cold compute publishes replacement worlds through its OWN work (a first observation of any path records an evidence baseline), which would self-fence exactly like the additive generations. Residual, owned by C4/C5b: a view captured between a content mutation and the reader-driven evidence refresh holds a root that has not yet observed the change, so it keeps validating the pre-mutation witness until the refresh advances the fact.
   675	
   676	**Handle-backed dimensions stay out of the token for DIFFERENT reasons:** `ResolvedImportFactsDb` is content-addressed — its key carries `content_hash`, so a new version is a new key and a fixed handle reads correctly (immutable-by-key). `RouteDb` is NOT content-addressed (its keys carry no content hash, and evict/clear/replace reuse the same key) — it stays out because every value it hands out is validated per candidate against the reading view through the candidate's own recorded `fact_dep_signature`, so an evict/replace yields a conservative fail-closed MISS, never a stale positive. The per-candidate signature comparison IS the validity rail, so the token needs no `RouteDb` generation. The route-surface FACT domain does not read `RouteDb` at all: its sole arm (`StoreView::validates_route_surface_domain`) compares the recorded `expected_hash` against the augmentation-index fingerprint snapshot captured on the view's artifact root.
   677	
   678	### Non-Current Store-View Contract — Capability Split (CRITICAL)
   679	
   680	The general store-view accessor `VerterHost::resolver_store_view()` returns the capability-split `StoreViewRead`, never a raw `HostStoreView`. The raw unwrap that erased the non-current proof is gone: every caller must compile-choose one of two capabilities, so no caller can validate (warm) or return (query) against a known-stale snapshot by accident.
   681	
   682	- `StoreViewRead::current()` → `CurrentHostStoreView` — the `StoreViewManager` proved this view current at handoff. Allowed for warm-cache fact validation AND for returning a normal query result.
   683	- `StoreViewRead::into_cold_seed_view()` → `ColdSeedHostStoreView` — usable ONLY for a fenced cold builder. It exposes NO `validates*` surface, so a stale seed cannot reach a fact validator by construction. It carries the read's currentness so a derived context fails closed.
   684	
   685	Concrete contract:
   686	
   687	- **Warm validators require `&CurrentHostStoreView`.** The top-level warm-validation entry points with no outer publish fence (`try_get_cached_meta_payload`, `ComponentMetaResultDb::get_with_view`, the imported-root / owner-import-surface warm reads) accept ONLY a proven-current view. A `ReturnOnly` read is a cache MISS, not a validation — the caller falls to the cold path whose own `is_stable` / publish fence gates promotion.
   688	- **typeinfo query-returners do bounded-retry-then-supersede.** `resolve_named_symbol`, `evaluate_type_expression`, `project_node_to_type_expr_json_bytes` (the session-owned bytes FFI facade that mints the `OutputProjector` capability + materializes + serializes internally), `resolve_shallow_surface`, `resolve_vue_macro_surface`, `resolve_vue_public_type`, and `resolve_type_with_audit` build a request-bound dispatch context and RETURN the resolved node with NO outer fence. They acquire a `CurrentHostStoreView` via `typeinfo::current_store_view_for_query` (bounded retry, default 3); on sustained churn they surface a typed non-current MISS (`None`, or `QueryError::UnstableState`) rather than resolving against a superseded snapshot and returning a stale node. `None` is the established FFI miss signal (`typeExpr: null`). The retry is bounded — it terminates, never spins. A non-current evaluation must NOT warm the `scratch_cache`.
   689	- **Every branch of a cache-presence-selected lane binds a REQUEST-BOUND context.** `VerterHost::build_template_class_semantic_facts` (`host_manage/analysis_io.rs`) picks its resolver context from artifact presence: the base-publishable + `IndexedReady`-present branch builds a `HostResolverContext::from_cold_seed`, the other composes a `SessionResolverContext::from_cold_seed`. The resolver-tier builder takes `&dyn RequestBoundResolverContext` — the sealed marker implemented for those two contexts and NEVER for `VerterHost` — so a bare-host binding is a COMPILE error, not a cache-presence-dependent runtime abort. The rail matters because `classify_binding` demands `prepared_value_decl` for every template `:class` script binding, and only a request-bound context can serve a prepared declaration. Regression: `template_class_lane_context_tests.rs` (indexed-present assertion + cold-seed control).
   690	- **Cold contexts carry `Current` vs `ColdSeed`.** `HostResolverContext::from_current(&CurrentHostStoreView)` vs `HostResolverContext::from_cold_seed(&ColdSeedHostStoreView)` — and the session-bound counterpart `SessionResolverContext::from_cold_seed(&ColdSeedHostStoreView)`. The cold-seed constructor marks the request-bound `RequestStoreView` non-current iff the seed was `ReturnOnly`; its `validates*` family then fails CLOSED, so every nested warm-cache probe inside the dispatch MISSES rather than validating against the stale seed. This is the single-chokepoint enforcement — no individual nested validator knows about currentness.
   691	- **Cold-seed currentness is INTRINSIC to its read — never a separately-sourced flag.** A cold-seed view's `is_current` comes from the SAME read that produced its raw view: `StoreViewRead::into_cold_seed_view()` derives it from the read's arm (`Current` vs `ReturnOnly`). There is no constructor that pairs a raw view with a caller-supplied bool — the retired `ColdSeedHostStoreView::from_raw_for_compute(view, separate_flag)` was exactly such a footgun, letting a view from one read be re-bound with a currentness flag from ANOTHER read (a stale second read marked current). Two valid sources of a cold-seed in a validating cold compute:
   692	  - **A helper that does its OWN fresh read** takes the cold-seed straight from that read: `self.resolver_store_view_read().into_cold_seed_view()` (then `.with_session_overlay(..)` for the session path). The view-bound component-meta cold compute (`VerterHost::view_bound_cold_seed` → `compute_component_meta_state_with_view` / `_from_captured_with_view`) and the bare-host overlay entries (`compute_component_meta_state_with_overlay` / `_from_captured_with_overlay`) use this — currentness and view come from one read, no flag to mismatch.
   693	  - **A helper that holds the EXECUTOR's single-read `(view, is_current)` pair** re-binds it via the SOLE pairing constructor `StoreViewRead::from_executor_snapshot(view, is_current)` (returns the intrinsic-currentness enum, consumed via `.into_cold_seed_view()`), confined to the executor boundary where the pair provably came from one read. The fallthrough cold compute (`compute_fallthrough_surface_uncached`) and the component-meta `*_with_view_arg` entries use this — the executor's `snapshot_view` destructured one `StoreViewRead` and threaded both into `compute`. The executors (`ComponentMetaRequestExecutor`, `FallthroughRequestExecutor`) track `snapshot_view_current` and thread it into `compute(.., base_is_current)`.
   694	- **The cold-seed escape hatch (`ColdSeedHostStoreView::into_inner`) never feeds a validating context (INDIRECT-validation seam).** The raw unwrap `.into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` DROPS the `is_current` flag. It is confined to NON-validating consumers: the request-driver `snapshot_store_view()` accessors, the overlay-priority `capture_component_meta_inputs_with_view` (builds `CapturedComponentMetaInputs` only), and `#[cfg(test)]` direct-`host` wrappers. The fallthrough resolver validates its per-element / per-child / per-root node-cache entries through the request-bound `ctx.store_view()` (currentness-gated), not a separately-rebuilt raw `HostStoreView`.
   695	- **Fenced cold seeds remain correct.** A real fenced cold builder (`cold_seed_view_and_fence` + `ColdSeedFence`, the request-driver `compute` path) may compute from a `ReturnOnly` coherent seed to avoid blocking, but re-checks currentness before publishing: a non-current seed's result is non-cacheable and surfaces as superseded/degraded, never warmed into the shared cache. Cold builders are NOT forced to `Current` (that would needlessly block cold progress under churn).
   696	- **The raw-view escape hatch is allowlisted.** `StoreViewRead::into_owned_view()` yields a raw `HostStoreView` ONLY for the bare-host owned-view rail (`ResolverContext::resolver_store_view`, reachable when no request-bound context was installed), the request-driver owned-view snapshot accessors (currentness gated by `snapshot_view_is_current`), and `.into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` fenced cold seeds.

   698	Pinned by the static guards in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs`: `resolver_store_view_returns_store_view_read` (return type is `StoreViewRead`), `cold_seed_store_view_exposes_no_validation_surface` (no `validates*` on `ColdSeedHostStoreView`), `warm_validation_entry_points_require_current_store_view` (warm validators keep `&CurrentHostStoreView`), `resolver_store_view_into_owned_view_is_allowlisted` (raw-view escape hatch confined to the allowlist), `cold_seed_into_inner_confined_to_non_validating_allowlist` (the `into_cold_seed_view().into_inner()` raw-unwrap that drops currentness is confined to non-validating consumers — the INDIRECT-validation seam), `cold_compute_context_constructors_carry_currentness` (cold-compute context constructors are the currentness-carrying `from_cold_seed` form rooted on `RequestStoreView::new_cold_seed`; the footgun `from_raw_for_compute` stays retired; `from_executor_snapshot` is the sole executor-boundary re-bind), and `cold_seed_currentness_is_intrinsic_to_the_read` (the `(view, flag)` re-bind `from_executor_snapshot` is confined to the executor-boundary allowlist, and a fresh `resolver_store_view_read()` may never feed it — closing the view+flag divergence the constructor-shape guards missed), plus the discriminating regressions in `crates/verter_session/src/store_view_non_current_contract_tests.rs` (`session_cold_seed_context_fails_warm_probes_closed`, `view_bound_cold_seed_currentness_comes_from_its_own_read`, `fallthrough_cold_compute_node_cache_validation_fails_closed_under_churn`).

   725	### Template class fact lanes
   726	
   727	Normal compile, content override, and lazy raw-template conversion must all
   728	build `TemplateClassSemanticFacts` from the exact source `whole_hash` and the
   729	same script snapshot used by conversion. `CompileInput` and
   730	`VueTemplateInputs` carry that hash. Base-current computations may retain
   731	complete facts only with their validated dependency `ReadSetSignature`;
   732	overlay, missing/cyclic, or otherwise `ReturnOnly` computations never populate
   733	base-only caches. Content publication is owner-only, so dependency-derived
   734	class facts are served fresh without entering the pure-content store.
   735	
   736	`template_converter_inputs` is linkage-only. Semantic class domains flow
   737	through the opaque, revision-checked `TemplateClassDomainIndex`; callers must
   738	not manufacture raw class-domain tuples or recover domains from display text.

   113	consistent with how `C1.md`'s Context section treated `program.md:191-197` — effort and
   114	breadth are not reasons to shrink a charter (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning).
   115	
   116	**What D1 does NOT do**, stated up front because it is easy to over-read the paragraph:
   117	it does not delete `flow_return.rs`/`flow_return_callee.rs`/`flow_slice_content.rs` (that
   118	is `D2`'s one atomic cutover, per `ADR-014` decision 2); it does not touch any product
   119	entry point; it does not implement nominal-identity extension (`D3`), the full
   120	narrowing/structural-return algebra (`D4`), closure/capture join semantics (`D5`), the
   121	completion graph that closes debt `FR-D8`/`G10` (`D6` — still explicitly open per ruling
   122	R-11), `this`/sequence/call-context surfaces (`D7`), or the final U6 admission proof
   123	(`D8`). D1 builds the foundation those six blocks extend.

   157	## Intent Contract
   158	
   159	**Actor / problem.** Effective-flow answers (function return-type inference feeding
   160	`defineProps`/`defineEmits`/component-meta and any other consumer of
   161	`SemanticQueryKey::FlowReturn`) are produced today by a private evaluator that resolves
   162	local values through its own `read_local(&mut self, name: &str)` map
   163	(`flow_return.rs:4353`) and its own ad hoc reaching-definition bookkeeping — not by
   164	walking the typed-edge `FunctionFlowGraph` dependence structure
   165	(`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs:155`,
   166	`build_function_flow_graph` at `:243`) that already exists beside it, built for demand
   167	SLICING only (`peeker.rs`, `hashing.rs`, `lower.rs`). `A3` (accepted) proved specific
   168	rows of this evaluator wrong-and-warm and retracted them behind typed `FlowGap` markers,
   169	but was explicitly forbidden to replace the evaluator: "adding `FlowSolveOutcome`, proof
   170	tokens, or an obligation ledger in A3 is prohibited scope expansion... belongs to
   171	D1/D2's final typestate cutover" (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md`
   172	§12.1, and its Verdict paragraph). `D3`-`D8` each need a graph-native binding/relation
   173	authority to extend — nominal identity, narrowing, closure, loops, completion — without
   174	re-deriving name-keyed state per block. That authority does not exist. D1 is the block
   175	that builds it, privately, so `D2` can perform ADR-014's one atomic cutover without ever
   176	exposing two selectable production semantics engines at once.
   177	
   178	**Required observable outcomes** (all inside the private hermetic boundary; none are
   179	reachable in a release build):
   180	
   181	- Every value/effect fact the new solver produces is derived by walking
   182	  `FunctionFlowGraph` edges (`FlowEdgeKind::ValueDef` / `PathWrite` / `EvalEffect` /
   183	  `ControlRegion`) keyed by stable `SkeletonBindingId`/`FlowNodeId` slots — never a
   184	  `&str`-keyed lookup into a locally built map, and never a re-walk of the OXC AST for a
   185	  fact the graph already encodes.
   186	- A `FlowDemandPlan` (`architecture.md` §9.3) is computed once per cold logical demand
   187	  by taking the transitive closure of named obligations through one closed static domain
   188	  registry; naming an unregistered domain produces a typed unsupported obligation at
   189	  plan time, never a silent skip and never a partial plan the solver evaluates anyway.
   190	- A private obligation ledger (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §4 — modelled, not
   191	  necessarily named, on `ObligationState { Pending, Running, Discharged(evidence),
   192	  Gap(FlowGap), Failed(reason) }`) discharges every required/expanded obligation before
   193	  a private finalizer can construct a `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped value; that
   194	  constructor is unreachable from outside its owning module (no public `new`, no
   195	  `Default` that yields a "complete" discriminant, no test-only escape left reachable
   196	  outside `#[cfg(test)]`).
   197	- Every `G1`-`G11` case `A3` already typed as a gap
   198	  (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md` §5's per-gap table) is answered by
   199	  the new solver with an equal-or-more-precise typed gap — never silently "solved" where
   200	  production still honestly refuses.
   201	- Authored/legitimately-inferred semantic `any` stays a distinct value from "Verter has
   202	  no model" (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §5: "An authored `any` is a semantic
   203	  value. 'Verter has no model' is a gap and cannot become `any`"), mirroring the closed
   204	  split `A3` already installed (`SliceExpr::SemanticAny` vs. `SliceExpr::Gap(FlowGap)`,
   205	  `flow_slice_content.rs`) or D1's own graph-native equivalent of it.
   206	- Relation/inference decisions — nominal comparability, union/intersection membership,
   207	  coinductive SCC discharge — route exclusively through the existing shared authority:
   208	  `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`/`execute_relate` plus the `ObligationRuntime`/
   209	  `ObligationReentryStack` tagged-identity space
   210	  (`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:879,396`,
   211	  physically relocating into `verter_semantic` under `C1` per its convergence map) —
   212	  never a second copy of that machinery.
   213	- The entire private tree is unreachable from any product entry point (LSP, NAPI, WASM,
   214	  MCP, unplugin) **in a release build** — absent from the compiled artifact, not merely
   215	  undocumented or unlinked-by-convention.
   216	
   217	**Forbidden observable outcomes:**
   218	
   219	- A second name-keyed value-resolution map inside the new solver (any
   220	  `FxHashMap<&str, _>`- or `read_local`-shaped local-binding lookup that competes with
   221	  graph-edge traversal).
   222	- A second relation classifier: a new `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/
   223	  `SessionAdmissionLedger`-shaped type, or any `SemanticNodeId` comparison that does not
   224	  route through `execute_relate`.
   225	- A second `FunctionFlowGraph`-shaped structure, a second CFG, or a derived projection
   226	  (dominators / loop forest / def-use overlay) that stores a semantic fact instead of
   227	  being deterministically reconstructible from `(graph identity, profile)` alone — the
   228	  exact prohibition `ADR-001` states.
   229	- Any product/runtime-selectable flag, config value, or code path — in any crate — that
   230	  can reach the new solver before `D2`'s cutover lands.
   231	- A `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped value constructed anywhere outside its private
   232	  finalizer.
   233	- Porting `D3`-`D6`'s future algorithms (full nominal-identity comparability, full
   234	  narrowing/closure/loop/completion semantics) into the private tree early merely to
   235	  make a parity test pass. D1 owns re-deriving, graph-natively, whatever slice of
   236	  today's behavior is ratified Supported/Stable (or already a typed `A3` gap); it does
   237	  not pre-implement work `program.md` assigns to later blocks by name.
   238	
   239	**Authority/fallback order.** New-solver value/effect resolution → `FunctionFlowGraph`
   240	edges (sole structural authority per `ADR-001`, `architecture.md` §9.1) → stable binding
   241	slots. Relation/inference decisions → `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`/`execute_relate`
   242	(unchanged; `C1`-preserved, not `C1`-converged in the sense of new semantics). Anything
   243	the closed domain registry does not recognize → typed unsupported obligation, never
   244	silent success. There is **no** fallback from the new private solver to the old
   245	production evaluator or vice versa inside D1's scope — they are two independent
   246	implementations that happen to coexist pre-`D2`, never composed.
   247	
   248	**Acceptance IDs.**
   249	
   250	| ID | Requirement | Planned test/gate |
   251	|---|---|---|
   252	| D1-AC-1 | Value/effect resolution is graph-edge-native, never name-keyed | Type-level: the new solver's hot evaluation path takes no `&str`-keyed lookup type in its signature (reviewed at the module boundary, not grep-detected); behavioral: a private-boundary corpus reusing `A3`'s pinned `FIXED_CELLS`/G1-G11/154-row fixtures asserts the same observable result class (`Complete` / `Partial+FlowGap` / `NoValue`) as production for every fixture the new solver claims to cover |
   253	| D1-AC-2 | Private hermetic boundary — unreachable from any release build | `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`-gated module reusing the crate's EXISTING `test-support` feature (`crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml:22`, already documented as "never on the default/production closure"); a Cargo-metadata closure test proves no production `[dependencies]` edge (LSP/NAPI/WASM/MCP/unplugin binaries and their production dependency graphs) enables `test-support`, mirroring the existing dependency-firewall pattern `C1`/`B1` already use |
   254	| D1-AC-3 | Obligation ledger + private finalizer | Compile-fail (`trybuild`) proof that the `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped type has no publicly reachable constructor; a mutation test that removes one discharge call makes the finalizer return the `ReturnOnly`/gap shape instead of `Complete` (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §7: "mutation test dropping one obligation cannot yield `Complete`") |
   255	| D1-AC-4 | Closed static domain registry; unregistered domain fails typed, not silently | Every dispatch site over the domain enum is an exhaustive `match` with no `_` wildcard (compile-time proof: adding a domain variant without handling it is `E0004`); a fixture that requests an intentionally-unregistered domain asserts a typed unsupported-obligation result, never a partial evaluation |
   256	| D1-AC-5 | No second relation/inference authority | The new solver module holds no `pub(crate)`-or-broader path to construct `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/`SessionAdmissionLedger` directly (those stay `pub(crate)` to their defining module; the new solver only calls the public dispatch entry) — a `trybuild` compile-fail fixture proves a type outside that defining module cannot construct them, mirroring `C1-AC-7`'s method |
   257	| D1-AC-6 | Deterministic derived projections carry no semantic fact | Any dominator/loop-forest/def-use overlay the new solver builds is rebuilt twice from the same `(graph identity, profile)` and asserted byte-identical; a fixture proves it is never given its own persisted cache identity or treated as a second graph |
   258	| D1-AC-7 | Typed-gap parity with `A3`'s already-shipped G1-G11 taxonomy | For every G1-G11 fixture in `u6_flow_a3_retraction_tests.rs`/successor, the private solver's result class matches production's (both `Partial+FlowGap` of at least as precise a reason, or both `NoValue`) — never a silent "solved" answer where production still typed-refuses |
   259	| D1-AC-8 | Ratified capability-row coverage | For whatever row set the maintainer ratifies Supported/Stable before D1's candidate is dispatched (see Open Questions §1), every corpus fixture tagged to that row returns the same observable result class production gives today, via the new mechanism; every other row stays a typed gap. **Until ratification, this acceptance ID has an empty covered set and D1-AC-7 is the operative coverage floor** |
   260	| D1-AC-9 | Exact parse reacquisition — at most one reborrow per cold demand | The new solver reborrows the retained parse snapshot through the same lease-only pattern the existing flow substrate already documents (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/mod.rs:1-18`: "borrows no OXC node... performs NO type lowering"; `decl_body_memo.rs`'s scheduler-retained-snapshot pattern), never a second ad hoc re-parse; a counter-instrumented fixture asserts exactly one reborrow per cold function-body demand regardless of how many domains that demand touches |
   261	| D1-AC-10 | No product entry point reaches the private tree | A source/dependency-graph test (the kind `contracts/flow-completeness.md` §7 requires of `D2`, run here as a D1-scoped negative control) proves zero non-test, non-`test-support` call graph edge from `verter_lsp`/`verter_napi`/`verter_wasm`/`verter_mcp`/`unplugin` reaches the new module |
   262	
   263	**Cold/warm/allocation/fan-out/latency bounds.** D1's private tree is, by its own
   264	required outcome, unreachable from any product entry point — it therefore touches **no
   265	existing locked performance-gate cell**, and this charter does not add one.
   266	`A6_META_COMPILE_40_COLD_RUST` (the sole currently-locked cell) must show **zero**
   267	measured delta from a D1 candidate, because nothing it exercises can compile into a
   268	release artifact's hot path; that null result is itself part of D1-AC-2's proof, not a
   269	separate performance obligation. D1 may **not** request a new locked cell for
   270	production-facing flow performance — that is `D2`'s (and later `L2`'s) obligation, once
   271	the solver is actually reachable. The one in-charter resource requirement is
   272	`contracts/flow-completeness.md`'s own "no-flow path allocates no graph/plan" and
   273	"exact parse reacquisition" properties (D1-AC-9 above), proven by the private-boundary
   274	test suite itself, not by a gated SLO cell.

   330	# D1 — Private sole-flow-solver foundation
   331	
   332	**Status:** DRAFT pending maintainer ratification. **Class:** Foundational
   333	(`governance.md` §2.3 names "flow/effective typing" explicitly as a Foundational
   334	example area; `program-dag.toml` / `program.md:225-233`). **Predecessors:** `A3`, `B1`,
   335	`B2` — all three `ACCEPTED` (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:157-176,245-264,465-484`)
   336	— and `C1`, currently `status = "READY"` but its own charter is **DRAFT, unratified**
   337	(`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:619-638`; `charters/C1.md:3`).
   338	D1 cannot be `BLOCK_READY` while a predecessor's charter is unratified; see Sequencing.
   339	
   340	## Context — why this is far bigger than program.md's nine lines
   341	
   342	`program.md:225-233` gives D1 one paragraph: build canonical graph adapters, derived
   343	projections, a domain registry, a demand plan, binding slots, relation-authority
   344	integration, an obligation ledger, a private finalizer, parse reacquisition, and typed
   345	gaps — all behind a hermetic non-production boundary — so that it "preserves every
   346	ratified supported capability" before `D2`'s cutover. Read literally that sounds like a
   347	scaffolding exercise. **It is not**, for the same reason this program has repeatedly
   348	found blocks larger than their summary: the paragraph describes architecture.md §9's
   349	full target shape (§9.1-9.9), and the code it must functionally match today is real,
   350	large, and already characterized by ~20,000 lines of pinned regression tests.
   351	
   352	**The thing being replaced is not small.** The current effective-flow ("`FlowReturn`")
   353	answer is produced by a private, syntax-shaped, name-keyed evaluator:
   354	
   355	- `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs` — 8,416 lines
   356	- `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs` — 733 lines
   357	- `crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs` — 5,407 lines
   358	
   359	— roughly 14,500 production lines — pinned by roughly 20,000 lines of characterization
   360	tests (`flow_return_coverage_tests.rs` 3,154; `flow_return_lexical_tests.rs` 6,683;
   361	`flow_return_tests.rs` 4,531; `flow_return_positional_tests.rs` 463;
   362	`flow_return_root_gate_tests.rs` 680; `flow_return_frame_seal_tests.rs` 409;
   363	`flow_gap_retraction_tests.rs` 672; `u6_flow_shape_corpus_tests.rs` 4,084). D1 must
   364	reproduce, through a wholly different graph-native mechanism, whatever slice of that
   365	14,500-line surface the (currently unratified — see Open Questions) A6 capability
   366	matrix calls Supported/Stable, and must answer everything else with a typed gap at
   367	least as precise as the eleven (`G1`-`G11`) gap classes `A3` already shipped
   368	(`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md` §5). That is not "scaffolding
   369	behind a flag"; it is standing up a second, competing, complete-enough analysis engine
   370	under the same hermetic roof.
   371	
   372	**The target is already normatively specified, in more detail than program.md itself.**
   373	Four documents bind D1 more precisely than the block's own paragraph:
   374	[`contracts/flow-completeness.md`](../contracts/flow-completeness.md) (the "Flow Domain
   375	Closure, Obligation Ledger, and Completeness Contract" — normative), `architecture.md`
   376	§9 ("Effective typing and flow", §9.1-9.9), `decisions/ADR-001-semantic-authority-and-derived-projections.md`,
   377	and `decisions/ADR-014-atomic-flow-cutover-and-obligation-proof.md`. This charter treats
   378	those four as the binding shape and program.md's paragraph as their one-line summary,
   379	consistent with how `C1.md`'s Context section treated `program.md:191-197` — effort and
   380	breadth are not reasons to shrink a charter (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning).

   423	## Intent Contract
   424	
   425	**Actor / problem.** Effective-flow answers (function return-type inference feeding
   426	`defineProps`/`defineEmits`/component-meta and any other consumer of
   427	`SemanticQueryKey::FlowReturn`) are produced today by a private evaluator that resolves
   428	local values through its own `read_local(&mut self, name: &str)` map
   429	(`flow_return.rs:4353`) and its own ad hoc reaching-definition bookkeeping — not by
   430	walking the typed-edge `FunctionFlowGraph` dependence structure
   431	(`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs:155`,
   432	`build_function_flow_graph` at `:243`) that already exists beside it, built for demand
   433	SLICING only (`peeker.rs`, `hashing.rs`, `lower.rs`). `A3` (accepted) proved specific
   434	rows of this evaluator wrong-and-warm and retracted them behind typed `FlowGap` markers,
   435	but was explicitly forbidden to replace the evaluator: "adding `FlowSolveOutcome`, proof
   436	tokens, or an obligation ledger in A3 is prohibited scope expansion... belongs to
   437	D1/D2's final typestate cutover" (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md`
   438	§12.1, and its Verdict paragraph). `D3`-`D8` each need a graph-native binding/relation
   439	authority to extend — nominal identity, narrowing, closure, loops, completion — without
   440	re-deriving name-keyed state per block. That authority does not exist. D1 is the block
   441	that builds it, privately, so `D2` can perform ADR-014's one atomic cutover without ever
   442	exposing two selectable production semantics engines at once.
   443	
   444	**Required observable outcomes** (all inside the private hermetic boundary; none are
   445	reachable in a release build):
   446	
   447	- Every value/effect fact the new solver produces is derived by walking
   448	  `FunctionFlowGraph` edges (`FlowEdgeKind::ValueDef` / `PathWrite` / `EvalEffect` /
   449	  `ControlRegion`) keyed by stable `SkeletonBindingId`/`FlowNodeId` slots — never a
   450	  `&str`-keyed lookup into a locally built map, and never a re-walk of the OXC AST for a
   451	  fact the graph already encodes.
   452	- A `FlowDemandPlan` (`architecture.md` §9.3) is computed once per cold logical demand
   453	  by taking the transitive closure of named obligations through one closed static domain
   454	  registry; naming an unregistered domain produces a typed unsupported obligation at
   455	  plan time, never a silent skip and never a partial plan the solver evaluates anyway.
   456	- A private obligation ledger (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §4 — modelled, not
   457	  necessarily named, on `ObligationState { Pending, Running, Discharged(evidence),
   458	  Gap(FlowGap), Failed(reason) }`) discharges every required/expanded obligation before
   459	  a private finalizer can construct a `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped value; that
   460	  constructor is unreachable from outside its owning module (no public `new`, no
   461	  `Default` that yields a "complete" discriminant, no test-only escape left reachable
   462	  outside `#[cfg(test)]`).
   463	- Every `G1`-`G11` case `A3` already typed as a gap
   464	  (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md` §5's per-gap table) is answered by
   465	  the new solver with an equal-or-more-precise typed gap — never silently "solved" where
   466	  production still honestly refuses.
   467	- Authored/legitimately-inferred semantic `any` stays a distinct value from "Verter has
   468	  no model" (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §5: "An authored `any` is a semantic
   469	  value. 'Verter has no model' is a gap and cannot become `any`"), mirroring the closed
   470	  split `A3` already installed (`SliceExpr::SemanticAny` vs. `SliceExpr::Gap(FlowGap)`,
   471	  `flow_slice_content.rs`) or D1's own graph-native equivalent of it.
   472	- Relation/inference decisions — nominal comparability, union/intersection membership,
   473	  coinductive SCC discharge — route exclusively through the existing shared authority:
   474	  `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`/`execute_relate` plus the `ObligationRuntime`/
   475	  `ObligationReentryStack` tagged-identity space
   476	  (`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:879,396`,
   477	  physically relocating into `verter_semantic` under `C1` per its convergence map) —
   478	  never a second copy of that machinery.
   479	- The entire private tree is unreachable from any product entry point (LSP, NAPI, WASM,
   480	  MCP, unplugin) **in a release build** — absent from the compiled artifact, not merely
   481	  undocumented or unlinked-by-convention.
   482	
   483	**Forbidden observable outcomes:**
   484	
   485	- A second name-keyed value-resolution map inside the new solver (any
   486	  `FxHashMap<&str, _>`- or `read_local`-shaped local-binding lookup that competes with
   487	  graph-edge traversal).
   488	- A second relation classifier: a new `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/
   489	  `SessionAdmissionLedger`-shaped type, or any `SemanticNodeId` comparison that does not
   490	  route through `execute_relate`.
   491	- A second `FunctionFlowGraph`-shaped structure, a second CFG, or a derived projection
   492	  (dominators / loop forest / def-use overlay) that stores a semantic fact instead of
   493	  being deterministically reconstructible from `(graph identity, profile)` alone — the
   494	  exact prohibition `ADR-001` states.
   495	- Any product/runtime-selectable flag, config value, or code path — in any crate — that
   496	  can reach the new solver before `D2`'s cutover lands.
   497	- A `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped value constructed anywhere outside its private
   498	  finalizer.
   499	- Porting `D3`-`D6`'s future algorithms (full nominal-identity comparability, full
   500	  narrowing/closure/loop/completion semantics) into the private tree early merely to
   501	  make a parity test pass. D1 owns re-deriving, graph-natively, whatever slice of
   502	  today's behavior is ratified Supported/Stable (or already a typed `A3` gap); it does
   503	  not pre-implement work `program.md` assigns to later blocks by name.
   504	
   505	**Authority/fallback order.** New-solver value/effect resolution → `FunctionFlowGraph`
   506	edges (sole structural authority per `ADR-001`, `architecture.md` §9.1) → stable binding
   507	slots. Relation/inference decisions → `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`/`execute_relate`
   508	(unchanged; `C1`-preserved, not `C1`-converged in the sense of new semantics). Anything
   509	the closed domain registry does not recognize → typed unsupported obligation, never
   510	silent success. There is **no** fallback from the new private solver to the old
   511	production evaluator or vice versa inside D1's scope — they are two independent
   512	implementations that happen to coexist pre-`D2`, never composed.
   513	
   514	**Acceptance IDs.**
   515	
   516	| ID | Requirement | Planned test/gate |
   517	|---|---|---|
   518	| D1-AC-1 | Value/effect resolution is graph-edge-native, never name-keyed | Type-level: the new solver's hot evaluation path takes no `&str`-keyed lookup type in its signature (reviewed at the module boundary, not grep-detected); behavioral: a private-boundary corpus reusing `A3`'s pinned `FIXED_CELLS`/G1-G11/154-row fixtures asserts the same observable result class (`Complete` / `Partial+FlowGap` / `NoValue`) as production for every fixture the new solver claims to cover |
   519	| D1-AC-2 | Private hermetic boundary — unreachable from any release build | `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`-gated module reusing the crate's EXISTING `test-support` feature (`crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml:22`, already documented as "never on the default/production closure"); a Cargo-metadata closure test proves no production `[dependencies]` edge (LSP/NAPI/WASM/MCP/unplugin binaries and their production dependency graphs) enables `test-support`, mirroring the existing dependency-firewall pattern `C1`/`B1` already use |
   520	| D1-AC-3 | Obligation ledger + private finalizer | Compile-fail (`trybuild`) proof that the `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped type has no publicly reachable constructor; a mutation test that removes one discharge call makes the finalizer return the `ReturnOnly`/gap shape instead of `Complete` (`contracts/flow-completeness.md` §7: "mutation test dropping one obligation cannot yield `Complete`") |
   521	| D1-AC-4 | Closed static domain registry; unregistered domain fails typed, not silently | Every dispatch site over the domain enum is an exhaustive `match` with no `_` wildcard (compile-time proof: adding a domain variant without handling it is `E0004`); a fixture that requests an intentionally-unregistered domain asserts a typed unsupported-obligation result, never a partial evaluation |
   522	| D1-AC-5 | No second relation/inference authority | The new solver module holds no `pub(crate)`-or-broader path to construct `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/`SessionAdmissionLedger` directly (those stay `pub(crate)` to their defining module; the new solver only calls the public dispatch entry) — a `trybuild` compile-fail fixture proves a type outside that defining module cannot construct them, mirroring `C1-AC-7`'s method |
   523	| D1-AC-6 | Deterministic derived projections carry no semantic fact | Any dominator/loop-forest/def-use overlay the new solver builds is rebuilt twice from the same `(graph identity, profile)` and asserted byte-identical; a fixture proves it is never given its own persisted cache identity or treated as a second graph |

   526	| D1-AC-9 | Exact parse reacquisition — at most one reborrow per cold demand | The new solver reborrows the retained parse snapshot through the same lease-only pattern the existing flow substrate already documents (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/mod.rs:1-18`: "borrows no OXC node... performs NO type lowering"; `decl_body_memo.rs`'s scheduler-retained-snapshot pattern), never a second ad hoc re-parse; a counter-instrumented fixture asserts exactly one reborrow per cold function-body demand regardless of how many domains that demand touches |

   528	
   529	**Cold/warm/allocation/fan-out/latency bounds.** D1's private tree is, by its own
   530	required outcome, unreachable from any product entry point — it therefore touches **no
   531	existing locked performance-gate cell**, and this charter does not add one.

   553	## Legacy deletions

   555	**D1 deletes nothing in production.** This is a deliberate, explicit statement, not an
   556	omission: `ADR-014` decision 2 and `contracts/flow-completeness.md` §6 both make the old
   557	evaluator's deletion `D2`'s ONE atomic act ("In one public cutover... delete the old
   558	syntax-shaped evaluator and its state, caches, tasks, flags, compatibility shims, and
   559	migration guards"). A D1 candidate that deletes or even behaviorally alters
   560	`flow_return.rs`/`flow_return_callee.rs`/`flow_slice_content.rs` — or any of their
   561	production call sites — is out of scope and should be treated as a design violation, not
   562	merely an aggressive interpretation. A reviewer should expect **zero diff** in those
   563	three files (and in `dispatch_txn.rs`'s existing `FlowReturn`-domain arms) from a

   593	## Structural confinement
   594	
   595	Every invariant above is enforced structurally where the codebase already has the
   596	mechanism, and named honestly as a convention where it does not:
   597	
   598	- **Hermetic boundary — genuinely structural.** `#[cfg(any(test, feature =
   599	  "test-support"))]`, reusing the `test-support` feature `verter_semantic` (and
   600	  `verter_session`) already declare (`crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml:12-22`,
   601	  already documented: "never on the default/production closure, so release builds
   602	  compile... without" the gated code). A module gated this way does not exist in a
   603	  release compilation unit at all — not merely undocumented or unlinked by convention.
   604	  The existing Cargo-metadata dependency-firewall guard pattern (`C1.md`'s "crate
   605	  dependency firewall is the primary proof, not a marker" — `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs`)
   606	  extends naturally to prove no production `[dependencies]` edge enables
   607	  `test-support` transitively; this is the SAME proof shape already landed for a
   608	  different invariant, not a new mechanism.
   609	- **Private finalizer — genuinely structural, existing pattern.** A `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped
   610	  type with a private constructor, buildable only inside its own module by its own
   611	  finalizer function, is the same shape this codebase already uses elsewhere
   612	  (`MaterializeStructureDb`'s sink-private constructors, the `RequestBoundResolverContext`
   613	  sealed-marker pattern `C1.md` cites). A `trybuild` compile-fail fixture is the
   614	  existing proof idiom (`C1-AC-7`).
   615	- **Closed-enum domain registry and typed gaps — genuinely structural, WITH a caveat.**
   616	  An exhaustive `match` with no `_` arm over the domain enum turns "someone adds a
   617	  domain and forgets a call site" into `E0004` at compile time — real, and consistent
   618	  with this program's existing "EXHAUSTIVE match, no wildcard" rule
   619	  (`framework-adapters` skill: `ExecutorResolveCtx`). The caveat: this protects against
   620	  an **omitted** domain, not a domain handled **wrong** — a match arm that silently
   621	  returns a plausible-looking default instead of the correct discharge still compiles
   622	  and still passes an exhaustiveness check. That half is a test-coverage obligation
   623	  (D1-AC-1/D1-AC-7's behavioral parity corpus), not a structural one; this charter does
   624	  not claim otherwise.
   625	- **No-second-relation-authority — structural via VISIBILITY, not via "nothing calls
   626	  it."** Per this task's own falsification warning: an "exhaustive test double" or "no
   627	  current call site" claim is not proof — a contributor adding a method next year could
   628	  satisfy either trivially. The actual mechanism here is narrower and load-bearing:
   629	  `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/`SessionAdmissionLedger` stay `pub(crate)`
   630	  to their OWN defining module (today `project_semantic_dispatch`; post-`C1`, whichever
   631	  module inside `verter_semantic` inherits that scope). D1's new solver module must be
   632	  placed OUTSIDE that visibility boundary, so it physically cannot name a constructor
   633	  for those types — the same enforcement `HostStoreView`'s immutability already gets
   634	  from holding no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<_>>` field (`C1.md`'s "already structural, not
   635	  a convention" bullet). A contributor who wants to bypass this would have to WIDEN the
   636	  visibility modifier on the shared type — a one-line diff any reviewer sees, not a
   637	  silent addition.
   638	- **Graph-edge-native value resolution — NOT fully structural; named as such.** Nothing
   639	  in Rust's type system stops a contributor from adding a `&str`-keyed `HashMap` inside
   640	  the new solver next to graph-edge traversal; there is no marker type that makes
   641	  "resolves via graph edges" a compile-time property the way `NoTypeExpr` makes
   642	  "content-free" one. This is a **design/review discipline**, proven by the behavioral
   643	  parity corpus (D1-AC-1) and caught at review, not by the compiler. Calling it
   644	  structural would repeat the exact failure mode this task warned against (a trait
   645	  default method silently satisfied); this charter does not make that claim.
   646	
   647	## Boundary against predecessors and successors
   648	
   649	**Against `C1`.** D1 depends on `C1`'s converged `ProjectSemanticDispatch`/relation
   650	authority being physically resident where D1 will build against it. D1 does not
   651	re-litigate `C1`'s crate-placement ruling (`ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md`) and treats its
   652	outcome as given, whichever module boundary it lands with — see Open Questions §2 for
   653	the one genuine gap C1's own charter left unaddressed (whether `flow_return.rs` et al.
   654	physically relocate under `C1` at all).
   655	
   656	**Against `A3`.** D1 preserves `A3`'s typed-gap taxonomy (`FlowGap` and its eleven
   657	classes) and the 154-row checker-correct clean/warm preservation cohort as its own
   658	private-boundary oracle. D1 must not weaken any `A3` guarantee — in particular, D1's
   659	private tree answering a case `A3` retracted must retract it too, never "solve" it back
   660	to a guessed value without that becoming a maintainer-ratified capability decision
   661	(`flow-completeness.md` §6: "unless a separate reviewed breaking product decision
   662	changes that row").
   663	
   664	**Against `D2`.** D1 explicitly does not perform the atomic cutover, does not delete
   665	`flow_return.rs`/`flow_return_callee.rs`/`flow_slice_content.rs`, does not touch any

   911	    98	`SemanticQueryKey::FlowReturn`) are produced today by a private evaluator that resolves

   917	   104	SLICING only (`peeker.rs`, `hashing.rs`, `lower.rs`). `A3` (accepted) proved specific
   918	   105	rows of this evaluator wrong-and-warm and retracted them behind typed `FlowGap` markers,

  1077	   264	## Structural confinement
  1078	   265	
  1079	   266	Every invariant above is enforced structurally where the codebase already has the
  1080	   267	mechanism, and named honestly as a convention where it does not:
  1081	   268	
  1082	   269	- **Hermetic boundary — genuinely structural.** `#[cfg(any(test, feature =
  1083	   270	  "test-support"))]`, reusing the `test-support` feature `verter_semantic` (and
  1084	   271	  `verter_session`) already declare (`crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml:12-22`,
  1085	   272	  already documented: "never on the default/production closure, so release builds
  1086	   273	  compile... without" the gated code). A module gated this way does not exist in a
  1087	   274	  release compilation unit at all — not merely undocumented or unlinked by convention.
  1088	   275	  The existing Cargo-metadata dependency-firewall guard pattern (`C1.md`'s "crate
  1089	   276	  dependency firewall is the primary proof, not a marker" — `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs`)
  1090	   277	  extends naturally to prove no production `[dependencies]` edge enables
  1091	   278	  `test-support` transitively; this is the SAME proof shape already landed for a
  1092	   279	  different invariant, not a new mechanism.
  1093	   280	- **Private finalizer — genuinely structural, existing pattern.** A `CompleteFlowResult`-shaped
  1094	   281	  type with a private constructor, buildable only inside its own module by its own
  1095	   282	  finalizer function, is the same shape this codebase already uses elsewhere
  1096	   283	  (`MaterializeStructureDb`'s sink-private constructors, the `RequestBoundResolverContext`
  1097	   284	  sealed-marker pattern `C1.md` cites). A `trybuild` compile-fail fixture is the
  1098	   285	  existing proof idiom (`C1-AC-7`).
  1099	   286	- **Closed-enum domain registry and typed gaps — genuinely structural, WITH a caveat.**
  1100	   287	  An exhaustive `match` with no `_` arm over the domain enum turns "someone adds a
  1101	   288	  domain and forgets a call site" into `E0004` at compile time — real, and consistent
  1102	   289	  with this program's existing "EXHAUSTIVE match, no wildcard" rule
  1103	   290	  (`framework-adapters` skill: `ExecutorResolveCtx`). The caveat: this protects against
  1104	   291	  an **omitted** domain, not a domain handled **wrong** — a match arm that silently
  1105	   292	  returns a plausible-looking default instead of the correct discharge still compiles
  1106	   293	  and still passes an exhaustiveness check. That half is a test-coverage obligation
  1107	   294	  (D1-AC-1/D1-AC-7's behavioral parity corpus), not a structural one; this charter does
  1108	   295	  not claim otherwise.
  1109	   296	- **No-second-relation-authority — structural via VISIBILITY, not via "nothing calls
  1110	   297	  it."** Per this task's own falsification warning: an "exhaustive test double" or "no
  1111	   298	  current call site" claim is not proof — a contributor adding a method next year could
  1112	   299	  satisfy either trivially. The actual mechanism here is narrower and load-bearing:
  1113	   300	  `RelationDomainRuntime`/`InferenceSession`/`SessionAdmissionLedger` stay `pub(crate)`
  1114	   301	  to their OWN defining module (today `project_semantic_dispatch`; post-`C1`, whichever
  1115	   302	  module inside `verter_semantic` inherits that scope). D1's new solver module must be
  1116	   303	  placed OUTSIDE that visibility boundary, so it physically cannot name a constructor
  1117	   304	  for those types — the same enforcement `HostStoreView`'s immutability already gets
  1118	   305	  from holding no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<_>>` field (`C1.md`'s "already structural, not
  1119	   306	  a convention" bullet). A contributor who wants to bypass this would have to WIDEN the
  1120	   307	  visibility modifier on the shared type — a one-line diff any reviewer sees, not a
  1121	   308	  silent addition.
  1122	   309	- **Graph-edge-native value resolution — NOT fully structural; named as such.** Nothing
  1123	   310	  in Rust's type system stops a contributor from adding a `&str`-keyed `HashMap` inside
  1124	   311	  the new solver next to graph-edge traversal; there is no marker type that makes
  1125	   312	  "resolves via graph edges" a compile-time property the way `NoTypeExpr` makes
  1126	   313	  "content-free" one. This is a **design/review discipline**, proven by the behavioral
  1127	   314	  parity corpus (D1-AC-1) and caught at review, not by the compiler. Calling it
  1128	   315	  structural would repeat the exact failure mode this task warned against (a trait
  1129	   316	  default method silently satisfied); this charter does not make that claim.

  1377	
  1378	Verter = a Vue compiler + Language Server Protocol (LSP) implementation. Converts Vue Single File Components (SFCs) to valid TSX (TypeScript type-checks them) and compiles templates to optimized render functions. Unlike Volar, Verter generates real valid TSX, not virtual files.
  1379	
  1380	Hybrid Rust + TypeScript monorepo: Rust crates own carrier parsing, runtime and IDE code generation, the shared semantic session, and the LSP server (`verter_lsp` binary, stdio); TypeScript packages provide editor integration, TypeScript-provider adapters, protocol bindings, and bundler orchestration.
  1381	
  1382	## Architecture
  1383	
  1384	Detailed module reference, key files, and implementation specifics live in domain skills: `/type-resolution`, `/type-cache-architecture`, `/component-meta`, `/compiler-codegen`, `/host-session`, `/architecture`.
  1385	
  1386	### Shared Optimized Codebase (CRITICAL)
  1387	
  1388	Verter is one shared optimized codebase, not separate semantic implementations per consumer.
  1389	
  1390	- Improvements land in the lowest reusable owner crate that can correctly serve all consumers.
  1391	- `verter_session` + shared workspace/VFS integration are the authority for host-backed loading, invalidation, dependency tracking, cache reuse.
  1392	- `verter_semantic` + `verter_compiler` own reusable semantics, lowering, codegen.
  1393	- `verter_session::resolver_core` owns the host-backed resolver stack + type-resolution orchestration.
  1394	- `verter_audit` is the leaf observability substrate (depends only on `verter_span`, no back-edge; lower crates emit through `current_observer()` (TLS) without knowing whether a `HostAuditRuntime` is installed); the concrete host runtime lives in `verter_session` — full ownership inventory in `/audit-infrastructure`.
  1395	- `verter_protocol` owns transport-facing schema DTOs; `verter_ffi` remains the thin native/WASM adapter layer.
  1396	- Consumer packages (`@verter/component-meta`, LSP, MCP, unplugin, playground) consume the shared substrate, not their own semantic forks.
  1397	
  1398	Architectural consequence:
  1399	
  1400	- A perf/correctness fix found in one surface is implemented in the shared owner layer whenever the behavior is reusable.
  1401	- Consumer-local wrappers stay thin and do not bypass shared parsing, analysis, resolution, or cache ownership.
  1402	
  1403	**Exactly one type-resolution engine.** `SemanticQueryKey` → `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute` → `SemanticGraphStore`, five query modes (`Identity`/`Navigate`/`Shallow`/`Expanded`/`Skeleton`) — the SOLE query-time type resolver. OXC is the syntax/lowering front-end ONLY (declaration bodies lower to `TypeExpr` lazily on first semantic demand through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot — the `DeclBodyMemo` owned by `IndexedReady`); OXC must never resolve types at query time. Any second query-time resolution path — a parallel `resolve_type` engine, a per-surface walker, a re-parse-and-resolve, an OXC element/frontier resolver — is a rule violation: delete it, route through the shared resolver. Two engines diverge; divergence is the bug/hang class.
  1404	
  1405	**Audit infrastructure:** Rust-first deterministic per-request observability for every audited `VerterHost` entry-point (component-meta, type-resolution, compile, analyze, workspace ops, LSP handlers, MCP tools, bundler batches). TS bindings in `packages/types/audit.generated.ts`; opt-in via `HostConfig::audit_enabled + footprint_capture`. See `/audit-infrastructure` and [`docs/audit-footprint/`](docs/audit-footprint/).
  1406	
  1407	Guards: `verter_audit_no_upward_deps`, `audit_substrate_isolation`, `audit_observer_single_accessor`. The former single-engine `no_new_*` shrinking-ledger scanners retired with the deleted parser-owned `type_surface` engine; the single-engine invariant is now held structurally (the compiler consumes only the dependency-neutral macro DTO) plus the Vue macro boundary suite registered under "Vue Macro Semantic Boundary" in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`.
  1408	
  1409	### Build Philosophy (CRITICAL)
  1410	
  1411	Same end-state philosophy as `binary-exploring-lamport.md`. Core rules:
  1412	
  1413	1. Read, parse, shallow-process, cache each canonical file once per content hash through one shared host path.
  1414	2. Store the full shallow symbol inventory up front, then process only requested items on demand.
  1415	3. Same-file closure stays local to the owning file.
  1416	4. Cross-file deepening happens in one place only, one import level at a time.
  1417	5. The builder/solver reads only from cached lookup state; it does not reopen file loading or routing.
  1418	6. The design is demand-driven and query-scoped.
  1419	7. The final implementation lands as one clean cutover, not a merged dual-path transition.
  1420	8. Component-meta, LSP, MCP, and other host-backed consumers share the same file-ready/read/parse/shallow-process lifecycle.
  1421	
  1422	These are architecture rules, not optimization hints. On conflict, fix the owner layer or delete the legacy path rather than preserve a second read/parse/resolution flow.
  1423	
  1424	Guards: `no_thread_local_oxc_caches`, `no_direct_oxc_parser_calls_outside_scheduler_path`, `recursion_budget_invariant_across_module_boundary`.
  1425	
  1426	### Shallow File Processing Core Invariant (CRITICAL)
  1427	
  1428	The shallow file process is a core architectural invariant and must be preserved. When a canonical file is processed, the host stores its shallow symbol inventory once; that inventory is the authoritative index later stages query.
  1429	
  1430	Shallow state must classify and retain at minimum: imports; exports and reexports; type declarations; interfaces; enums; classes; variables/constants; functions/method signatures; `typeof`-relevant value declarations; local symbol dependency edges; cross-file dependency edges.
  1431	
  1432	Design rule: processing a file means collecting and indexing its symbols, not eagerly evaluating them; later stages look up the indexed items they need and process only those on demand; no stage rescans the raw file to rediscover symbols shallow processing already captured. Performance: very high performance comes from targeted demand after broad shallow indexing, not repeated partial reparsing.
  1433	
  1434	Core invariants (full architectural-target detail: `/type-resolution` → IndexedReady Target Contract + Cache Population Target Contract):
  1435	
  1436	- Canonical post-parse artifact = `IndexedReady`: a shallow declaration INDEX plus body locators, NOT a body store. Eagerly it carries canonical imports/exports, top-level symbol names/kinds, declaration spans, source-order contributor grouping, type-parameter names, syntactic member headers, and augmentation inventory — all safe for host-owned `Send + Sync` caches. Declaration BODIES lower only on first semantic demand through the shared lazy body service (the content-addressed `DeclBodyMemo` + scheduler-side `DeclLoweringService` retained-parse workers); publishing an artifact lowers ZERO declaration bodies. Component-meta and later analysis layers both build from it; symbol expansion populates and reuses the same shared resolver caches — no separate expansion paths.
  1437	- Parse each live file version once; the lazy lowering service RETAINS the parse snapshot on its worker shard (keyed `(canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash)`) so body demands reuse it instead of re-parsing per touch. Transient OXC parse arenas stay per-file/per-version and never leak into host-owned shared caches — jobs borrow the retained AST on the worker and return owned typed IR.
  1438	- The declaration-body **hot READ path is handle-native at the one migrated graph-backed site** (`lower_decl_body_to_node`) through `decl_body_hot_ref`; prepared declarations and `LoweredValueDecl` are fact+locator `NoTypeExpr`, and `LoweredTypeDecl.body` is content-free. The two former stored type-parameter `TypeExpr` pockets are CLOSED (the type-parameter-bound confinement block): `LoweredTypeDecl` is wholly `NoTypeExpr` — the stored full `type_parameters: Vec<TypeParam>` is gone; the `narrow_type_parameters` mirror (name + ordinal + content-free bound locators) is the sole stored authority, consumed by the prepared-decl builder and the external frontier (which content-free re-anchors the mirror's bound slots to the frontier symbol, preserving `export default`), while the locator/binder deref uses the mirror for ordinal/name/bound-presence authority and re-borrows bound CONTENT + the full sibling frame lease-only from the retained snapshot (`transient_type_parts`). `TypeParamBinding` is likewise shrunk to the content-free `(name, ordinal)` fact pair (`NoTypeExpr`): its `<script setup generic="…">` bounds are re-borrowed at query time through ONE artifact-local transient producer over the pinned `IndexedReady` and lowered by ONE dispatch helper shared by both content readers, with a missing/stale re-borrow failing as a typed cache-suppressed miss, never a bound-free fabricated binder. The residual-reader ledger is not a terminal-zero mechanism: `ProducerLowering` is permanent transient ingress, the five `GraphFreeDto` rows remain named until the separate producer-boundary-confinement cutover, and a hot consumer must never take `HotTypeRef → TypeExpr → semantic decision`.
  1439	- Navigation stays narrower than expansion: walking `A['c']['full']['bar']` navigates intermediate hops and expands only the terminal requested projection unless limited normalization is required to continue.
  1440	- Generic substitutions are semantic meaning: navigation/expansion operate on instantiated types; cache keys include the relevant substitutions/type arguments.
  1441	- Navigators stay non-owning (choose the next hop, non-owning normalization only); reusable semantic work enters through the shared query API, not a private drill-down path. The shared semantic layer is keyed by semantic query identity and stores immutable semantic data or ids — never borrowed AST pointers or retained parser arenas.
  1442	- Completion fence: top-level live-host results record touched dependency facts, revalidate before publish, retry at most 3 times on mid-flight changes; never warm shared caches with torn provisional results; cancelled, superseded, interrupted, budget-exceeded, or partial results are never promoted warm.
  1443	- Waiters on in-flight work block cooperatively, never busy-spin; same-path recursion never self-awaits.
  1444	- Cache population is path-independent (same result from different entry points → same shared entry); broader successful results may backfill only the narrower entries they actually satisfied; narrower results must not pretend broader work is cached.
  1445	- Final payload caches hand out immutable `Arc` values; any backend preserving concurrency, size bounds, validation semantics is fine.

  1451	### Canonical Dependency Cache Rule (CRITICAL)
  1452	
  1453	Host-backed type/import resolution treats the canonical file ID as the cache identity. Load and parse each dependency at most once per canonical ID per workspace content generation. Cache the parsed state, the shallow declaration index plus lazy declaration-body memo, symbol/export tables, and prepared declarations together. Later lookups hit cached maps — never rewalk the AST. VFS is the authority for file-change invalidation. Concurrent cold requests to the same file collapse onto one materialization path. Changes land as one clean cutover, no dual-path shims.
  1454

  1459	### Cache Architecture (CRITICAL)
  1460	
  1461	The fact-based cache architecture splits cache keys across five orthogonal env-hash dimensions (`parse_env_hash`, `resolve_env_hash`, `type_env_hash`, `lib_env_hash`, `project_identity`). Each cache layer keys only on the dimensions it actually depends on (R21 scoping rule — a single bundled `project_config_hash` is forbidden). `lib_env_hash` enters a key only when the value depends on lib data: `ResolvedImportFacts` does NOT include it; `RouteDb`, typed-IR resolve, `MaterializeStructureDb`, `SemanticGraphStore`, `ComponentMetaResultDb` DO.
  1462	
  1463	Two cache families: **content-addressed artifact caches** (`FileArtifactStore`, `ResolvedImportFacts`, typed-IR resolve, `MemberSemanticFactStore`, `MemberDisplayFactStore`, `ModuleAugmentationIndex`) carry `content_hash` or `parse_stable_hash` in the key; **query-identity caches** (`RouteDb`, `MaterializeStructureDb`, `SemanticGraphStore` query nodes, `ComponentMetaResultDb`) exclude version hashes from the key — concurrent variants coexist as candidates in one slot, with version rooting on the cached value (the structural + semantic-graph caches — `MaterializeStructureDb`, `SemanticGraphStore` memo, `ShapeCacheDb` — root via `ReadSetSignature.facts` + `self_root_canonicals`; `RouteDb` via its value-side `ValidatedFactCache` fact signature; `ComponentMetaResultDb` via the owner whole-hash candidate discriminant + `ReadSetSignature.facts`). Cache keys never include `fact_dep_signature`. The `MaterializeStructureDb` subject is the content-free `MaterializationCacheKey` (a `ResolvedDeclSlotIdentity` slot + projection/policy/mode axes + `resolve_env_hash`), NOT a graph-instance `SemanticNodeId` — the per-thread recursion identity `MaterializeRuntimeKey` is a separate, non-cache key; a root-less anonymous subject keys no slot (uncached). The materialization cycle gate is the sealed `SemanticQueryKey::ClassifyMaterializationCycleGate` family (`MaterializationCycleGateKey`: `ResolvedDeclSlotIdentity` root slot + `parse_env_hash` + `resolve_env_hash`, fixed `StructuralTransit`/`Skeleton`/empty-args axes) — the SOLE authority for "does this declaration transitively reach a cycle through a complex helper surface"; only its `Decided` outcome admits (`LegacyFallback` always suppresses), and consumers branch on the carried `Stop | Continue` verdict from both arms.
  1464	
  1465	Family-memo slots (`SemanticQueryKey::Instantiate.base` / `ResolveMacroPayload.owner`, mirrored on `FamilyKey`) are the env-bearing, content-free `ResolvedDeclSlotIdentity` (R6 — content/version hashes and the versioned `DeclIdentity` are forbidden in any derived-`Hash` query-identity key; the live whole-hash is re-sourced at value-compute time, never carried in the key). A warm hit requires TWO independent gates (§3.4): `cached_satisfies` over a RECORDED materialised `(path, point)` the candidate's compute actually produced — never the candidate's nominal slot/mode, never enum rank — AND per-candidate `ReadSetSignature.validate_with_self_roots` against the caller's live view. Backfill clones only recorded materialised points, directionally gated (the `Shallow → Navigate` clone is lattice-unsound). `validated_at_generation` is recency metadata only, never a validity oracle. Family-slot retention is bounded PER FAMILY (`U3.ADAPTIVE_FAMILY_RETENTION`): each `FamilyKey` declares an exhaustive `candidate_cap()` (floor 4; the inference/substitution-heavy live families `Instantiate` / `TypeOf` / `Conditional` / `MappedType` hold 8); at the cap a publish evicts a candidate INVALID against the publishing caller's stable store view FIRST (snapshot/validate/reacquire OUTSIDE the `entries` mutex, `admission_seq` identity recheck under it), then the least-recently validated-hit candidate (a valid hit promotes to the back); a new cacheable candidate is ALWAYS admitted after local eviction, and same-discriminant re-publish replaces in place as freshest. The process-wide candidate-memory ceiling + typed non-admission are deferred full-`U3.CACHE_FACT_MODEL` work, NOT live. See `/type-cache-architecture` for the full key/context composition (`InstantiateContext`/`MacroPayloadContext` per-key contexts, per-family `candidate_cap()` candidate semantics, non-file-base rooting).
  1466	
  1467	`FileArtifactStore` is the authoritative per-file storage layer, keyed by `(canonical, content_hash, parse_env_hash, parse_key, build_toolchain_fingerprint, file_language_id)` — `parse_key` is the stable exact source-bytes/language/compatibility-domain/syntax-profile identity (there is no separate parser-version counter dimension), and `file_language_id` is the file's `FileLanguage` row (the per-file classification dimension of artifact identity, so a framework-capability flip misses exactly the affected files' artifact slots without touching the global `parse_env_hash`). The overlay-aware `augmentation_index` (module-augmentation inverse lookup) lives on the same store. See `/type-cache-architecture` for the full key composition, `file_language_id` producer wiring, `AugmentationTargetKey`/`AugmentationPopulation` semantics, and the `parse_stable_hash` definition.
  1468	
  1469	Cache runtime hard rules — three always in force: cache correctness is read-side authoritative; `ReturnOnly` (overflow, budget exhaustion, cancellation, generation supersession, incomplete self-rooting, unresolved provenance) never publishes entries, reverse-index metadata, or persistent artifacts; overlay/session results never populate base-only or persistent caches. Full 20-rule list: `/type-cache-architecture` → Cache Runtime Hard Rules.
  1470	
  1471	Guards: `cache_satisfaction_is_materialized_point_not_nominal_demand`, `cache_satisfaction_requires_path_exact_not_prefix`, `backfill_writes_only_recorded_materialized_points`, `no_off_store_host_caches`, the `r6_*` cluster, plus the four migrated-query-identity-key guards in `tests/cases/g_cache/r6_r21_query_identity_keys.rs` (`component_meta_result_key_*`, `route_name_key_*`/`barrel_surface_key_*`, `materialization_cycle_gate_key_*`, `materialization_cache_key_*`) — full list in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`.

  1474	
  1475	### Macro Type Traversal Rule (CRITICAL)
  1476	
  1477	When resolving cross-file macro types (`defineProps<T>()`, `defineEmits<T>()`, component-meta deep expansion, etc.), only follow the import graph reachable from the requested type's declaration graph. There is one shared cross-file type resolver with five query modes: `Identity`, `Navigate`, `Shallow`, `Expanded`, `Skeleton` (see `/type-resolution` → Query Mode Contract).
  1478	
  1479	**Macro resolution is one shared path, not a per-macro engine.** Every macro (`defineProps` / `defineEmits` / `defineOptions` / `defineSlots` / `withDefaults`) and every imported `.vue` component surface resolves through exactly TWO steps: (1) resolve ONE type via the shared typed-IR five-mode dispatch — the generic-parameter type (`define*<T>()`) OR the object-argument type (`define*({ ... })`); `withDefaults` resolves the props payload type plus the defaults-object type and merges; `.vue`-component imports resolve the synthesized `$props` / `$emit` / `$slots` / expose surface recursively through the same dispatch (the hardest case — apply EXTRA caution: it is exactly where rule violations cause the worst hangs); no macro-specific engine, no per-surface walker, no eager element resolver. (2) Normalise per kind — a thin transform, NOT a resolver (per-kind field rules: `/type-resolution` → Macro Type Traversal Rule). A macro/import that resolves through anything else, or flattens a full surface eagerly before the consumer demands it, is a rule violation — collapse it into `shared_resolve(type) + normalise`.
  1480	
  1481	`Skeleton` is the BFS / generic-helper traversal mode: unbound type parameters stay `TypeParam` shells so Conditional branches do not collapse to `never`. Path projection is path-precise: intermediate hops run in `Navigate`, the terminal hop runs in the caller's mode; non-contributing intersection arms are ignored (not rewritten to `never`); open conditionals distribute the remaining path into both branches; closed conditionals reduce immediately. Do not walk unrelated imports. Do not treat plain imports as implicit exports. Cache discovered symbol mappings and barrel hops.
  1482	
  1483	**TS-first resolution priority:** TypeScript types always take priority over JavaScript files. Use `effective_target()`: `.d.ts` > `.d.cts` > `.d.mts` > `.ts` > `.tsx` > `.js` > `.jsx` > `.cjs` > `.mjs`.
  1484	
  1485	**Owned resolution is bounded by `workspace_root`:** `node_modules` and package `#imports` ancestor walks stop at `IdeProjectConfig.workspace_root`.
  1486	
  1487	Guards: `root_conditional_still_distributes`, `no_macro_string_heuristics_in_resolver_core`, `no_text_based_macro_surface_projection_helpers`, `no_role_inference_from_name_suffix`, `no_pick_or_omit_string_prefix_check` — full list in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS` (the retired `no_new_*` shrinking-ledger scanners left with the deleted `type_surface` engine; the compile-boundary half of the invariant is guarded under "Vue Macro Semantic Boundary").
  1488

  1490	
  1491	### Declaration Merging (CRITICAL)
  1492	
  1493	Same-name declaration merge is produced ONLY by `verter_semantic::type_eval` ordered declaration groups: `EvalEnv` appends contributors in source/binder order (`add_type`/`add_value` push onto an ordered `TypeDeclGroup`/`ValueDeclGroup` — no last-wins `FxHashMap<String, TypeDeclInfo>`/`…ValueDeclInfo>` map, no overwrite `insert` for mergeable kinds). Same-name `interface` declarations lower to the explicit `TypeDeclBody::Merged` carrier (on the memo-owned `LoweredTypeDecl.body` read through `ShallowFileState::type_decl(name)` → `PreparedTypeDecl.merged_contributors`), interned as a distinct `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl { contributors }` node.
  1494	
  1495	A merged declaration MUST reach the project-semantic reducer as that distinct carrier — a bare `TypeExpr::Intersection` / `SemanticNodeData::Intersection` is FORBIDDEN as the merged-decl representation, because the intersection reducer applies **heritage-shadow** member precedence and cannot accumulate method overload groups. The `MergedDecl` peer-merge reducer (`reduce_merged_decl_with_graph` + `merge_declaration_surfaces`): (a) same-name methods/call-signatures ACCUMULATE into one ordered overload group across contributors in source order; (b) conflicting non-method properties take deterministic first-contributor precedence (never `never`); (c) distinct members union.
  1496	
  1497	Functions accumulate into an ordered `Vec<FunctionSignature>` (`ValueDeclGroup::merged_signatures`), each carrying `has_implementation_body`; overload visibility is a PROJECTION-time rule (`build_typeof`): a lone signature is visible (even if bodied), a multi-signature group surfaces every bodiless overload in source order and hides the trailing implementation. Same-file merged values version-root on the owner's single `FileWholeHash` self-root under a content-free query-identity key (R6). `verter_session` MUST NOT synthesise the merge as `raw_body = TypeExpr::intersection(...)`. Cross-file ambient augmentation (`declare module`/`declare global`) reuses this same `MergedDecl` peer-merge path — see Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL).
  1498	
  1499	Guards: `eval_env_type_symbols_are_grouped_not_last_wins_map`, `eval_env_add_decl_appends_not_overwrites`, `no_intersection_merge_synthesis_in_verter_session`, `merged_decl_lowers_to_distinct_carrier_not_intersection`, `declaration_merge_facts`.
  1500

  1503	### Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL)
  1504	
  1505	Ambient declaration augmentation (`declare module "X" { ... }` / `declare global { ... }`) is a RETAINED, addressable scoped inventory — never fingerprint-only facts, never file-scope pollution. `EvalEnv.augmentation_scopes` / `EvalEnv.augmentation_value_scopes` key `(AugmentationScopeKind {Global, Module(specifier)}, name)` → ordered `TypeDeclGroup`/`ValueDeclGroup`, mirrored on `ShallowFileState`; inner decls NEVER enter file-scope `type_symbols`/`value_symbols`. Parse-domain `ModuleAugmentationFact`s are DERIVED from this typed inventory (`fact_emission::collect_augmentations`) — NO raw-source byte-scan.
  1506	
  1507	Cross-file augmentation merge is the SAME `MergedDecl` peer-merge path as same-file merging — NOT a second merge engine: `stitch_module_augmentations` finds every augmenter via `FileArtifactStore::ensure_augmentation_index_populated`, lowers each augmenter's RETAINED inner body in its own file context, and folds base ∪ augmenter contributions into ONE `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl` carrier; augmenter order is the stable `(canonical, parse_stable_hash)` key — discovery-order-independent.
  1508	
  1509	Facts rail: the cold stitch observes one `FactKey::ModuleAugmentationIndexShape` fingerprint plus one `FileWholeHash` per contributing file and records `self_root_canonicals = {base} ∪ {augmenters}` — a content edit to ANY contributor misses the warm read; torn/partial routes through `ReturnOnly`. Query keys stay content-free (R6). The index is OVERLAY-AWARE (`AugmentationPopulation {Base, Session(overlay-set fingerprint)}`): overlay augmenters NEVER poison the base index and NEVER cross sessions, and there is NO base-only session assert on the augmentation-index surface — a session view is accepted under `Session` scope.
  1510	
  1511	Guards: `session_overlay_augmenter_isolated_from_base_index`, `session_overlay_augmentation_isolated_from_base_meta`.
