  1805	### Documentation Updates
  1806	
  1807	After adding, changing, or removing features, update the **owning** documentation:
  1808	
  1809	- **Domain skills** (`.claude/skills/`) — update the skill that owns the affected module or API
  1810	- **`CLAUDE.md`** — only if summaries or skill pointers change
  1811	- **`AGENTS.md`** — if skill routing or shared sources change
  1812	- **`docs/`** — API docs, guide pages, contributing guides
  1813	- **Inline doc comments** — Public API rustdoc (`///`) and JSDoc (`/** */`) on changed signatures
  1814	
  1815	Skip for purely internal refactors that don't change public behavior, module paths, or APIs.
  1816	
  1817	### Testing Requirements
  1818	
  1819	**MANDATORY: TDD must be followed for EVERY code change. Non-negotiable.**
  1820	
  1821	1. Write failing tests FIRST — verify they fail before implementing
  1822	2. Implement minimum code to pass
  1823	3. Run tests, verify green
  1824	4. Refactor while keeping tests green
  1825	
  1826	Coverage: new features need tests, bug fixes need regression tests, refactors must keep existing tests passing.
  1827	
  1828	**Always include negative assertions**: verify both what SHOULD and should NOT be present. Codegen tests must check removed syntax is absent. Type tests must include `@ts-expect-error` guards against `any`/`never`.
  1829	
  1830	**Public-boundary acceptance**: for every changed user-visible IDE, API, or compiler outcome, each affected acceptance ID has an automated public-boundary test asserting the required result AND the relevant forbidden or fail-closed result. Provider-selection, status, unit, and architecture tests supplement but do not substitute for that boundary test. A substrate block may inherit a parent boundary test only by recording the acceptance-ID mapping and executing that test in its gate. Enforcement is judgment — reviewers assess the actual invocation path and assertions, not the filename; §1a proves discrimination; confirm reruns the mapped test.
  1831	
  1832	**Architecture guards for critical rules**: every new `CRITICAL` architecture rule lands with a static architecture guard or a discriminating regression test in the same change (subject to the landed-scanner bar below — a "static guard" is never a new name-keyed file scanner); if a guard cannot be automated yet, the rule text names the planned guard/test and the gap is tracked in the owning skill/doc. The R6 meta-guard at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc0/critical_rules_have_guards.rs` (`every_critical_rule_in_docs_has_registered_guard`) walks `CLAUDE.md` plus every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and asserts every `(CRITICAL)` heading has a `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS` registry row with at least one named guard — a prose-only `(CRITICAL)` section fails the gate.
  1833	
  1834	**Landed guards are structural, never name-keyed file scanners (forward-only)**: a heuristic file-scanner guard/test that keys on a specific tool, function, or identifier name (any spelled source name/path/token — type, module, import/path-segment, and string identities included; `syn`/AST-based scanning included) is a transient plan artifact — WIP-only (scratch branches, squashed out before landing), never a full-fledged landed guard. LANDED enforcement of an invariant is structural — compiler/type-system/tool-based (privacy/visibility/`E0603`, type-state, sealed traits, marker-trait derives, a real used tool or function) — never a name/text/grep scanner over the source tree. This strengthens Structural-Confinement-First (`.claude/skills/mom-cto-orchestration/reference/PROTOCOL.md` → Structural-Confinement-First → Landed-scanner bar): even a residual scanner that rule would permit (justified, recorded, supplement to a structural primary) does not land — keep it WIP, replace it structurally, or accept the residue uncovered by any landed scanner. Review/governance-enforced by design, NOT guard-enforced — a guard that detects "name-keyed scanner guards" would itself be a name-scanner. Forward-only: pre-existing landed scanners are grandfathered as a class — by temporal status (already landed at rule adoption), not by list membership — and retained as-is; the explicitly disclosed high-risk example (illustrative, not an exhaustive inventory) is the hot-materialize syntactic tripwire (`hot_materialize_syntactic_tripwire_residual_backstop` + its `HOT_TERMINAL_SINKS`/`HOT_DECIDE_TAINTED_GATE_IDENTS`/`HOT_EXTRACTING_GATE_IDENTS`/`HOT_MAT_DIRECT_IDENTS` name-lists in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/output_projector_residual_guards.rs`), retained as-is with no removal planned or required — its STRUCTURAL rail (the `NoTypeExpr` marker + the sealed `OutputProjector` capabilities) remains the durable primary.
  1835	
  1836	**Rust test file organization**: When inline `#[cfg(test)]` exceeds ~400 lines, extract to a sibling `*_tests.rs` file.
  1837	
  1838	### Verification Must Prove Execution (MANDATORY)
  1839	
  1840	A required gate passes only on fresh, input-bound evidence that: every applicable required job was eligible and ran; the intended tree-derived surface was owned and independently discovered; selectors matched non-zero work; required source, build, and fixture prerequisites matched the tested tree; executed work was non-zero; unexpected prerequisite skips were zero; child deadlines were strictly below their parent killer; and a terminal summary completed. **Exit status 0 alone, a self-declared test universe, or a missing required-job result is FAIL.** Every tracked test or guard has exactly one declared primary gate; a hand-maintained filename list may not define the primary universe unless generated from independent discovery and parity-checked.
  1841	
  1842	Attestation alone is insufficient — a receipt faithfully attests whatever incomplete universe the runner defines for itself. The durable design needs all three: fresh execution attestation; independently tree-derived inventory/discovery parity; and per-surface negative-control mutation through the exact canonical entry point. A single global canary cannot detect an omitted unrelated spec.
  1843	
  1844	**The negative control must itself be proven to have applied.** A plant that fails to apply reports a pass: `perl`/`sed`/`grep` exit 0 on a non-match, so a mutation's exit code is never proof it landed, and a verification search hitting a PRE-EXISTING occurrence of the planted string is a false positive. Prove the mutation is present, unique, and new in the source before trusting the run; a green planted run means the plant failed until proven otherwise. A discrimination check that cannot distinguish "the plant did not apply" from "the code is correct" is not a discrimination check.
  1845	
  1846	Planned guard: `gate_contract_integrity` — one registered suite exercising the canonical entry point against independent inventory plus per-surface negative controls covering missing summary, disabled or missing job, invalid timeout nesting, zero selection, stale or missing build, missing fixture or unexpected skip, omitted or unowned test, and a mutation that silently fails to apply. Until that guard, its attesting driver, and the required-job aggregator land, this rule is held only by §1a and confirm judgment.
  1847	
  1848	**This rule currently fails its own test, and says so.** It ships `(MANDATORY)` — precisely the tier the R6 meta-guard (`every_critical_rule_in_docs_has_registered_guard`) does not check, because that guard scans `(CRITICAL)` headings only. A rule whose thesis is "a gate that cannot prove it ran is a failure" is therefore, today, a gate that cannot prove it ran. `(CRITICAL)` is not available as a shortcut: an unguarded `(CRITICAL)` heading FAILS the meta-guard. So the gap is named rather than hidden — the deferral, its owner (the gate-integrity block), its resolution gate (that block's landing), and the live in-tree instances are recorded in [`docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md`](docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md). Promotion to `(CRITICAL)` with its own `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS` row, in the same change that lands the guard, is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION of that block (ledger row GI-4). It is never folded into `Stub Prevention` — a related but distinct invariant whose guards do not enforce these semantics.
  1849	
  1850	### Testing-Hermeticity (MANDATORY)
  1851	
  1852	Unit tests must only depend on locally-vendored fixtures. They must compile and run without any third-party repository (e.g., `nuxt-ui`, `element-plus`) checked out alongside this repository. Tests that need external corpora must be feature-gated (e.g., `#[cfg(feature = "external-corpus")]`) and excluded from the default canonical run (`node scripts/gate.mjs`, i.e. its two underlying surfaces `cargo nextest run --workspace` + `cargo test -p verter_session --tests`).
  1853	
  1854	A test that references `.integration-tests/repos/<third-party>/...` from a non-gated test file is a violation. The architecture guard `external_corpus_paths_not_present_outside_gated_tests` enforces this.
  1855	
  1856	### No phase archaeology in production code (MANDATORY)
  1857	
  1858	Source comments must not reference plan phases (`phase 5d`, `phase 11`, `post-cutover`, `pre-Phase`), cutover stages (`d-cutover`, `cutover`), deletion history (`deleted in 5g`, `retired in`), or any project-management vocabulary. Once a plan is over, the code reads as final-state.
  1859	
  1860	Durable architecture insights belong in `.claude/skills/*` or `docs/arch/`, not in source comments. Test files named after retired phases must be renamed to describe the invariant they characterize, not the phase that produced them.
  1861	
  1862	The architecture guard `no_phase_archaeology_in_production_code` enforces this on `crates/*/src/**`.
  1863	
  1864	See `/testing` skill for full TS/Rust test patterns, sourcemap testing, and server cleanup.
  1865	
  1866	### VS Code Extension Testing (MANDATORY)
  1867	
  1868	Changes to the VS Code extension or the LSP server MUST be verified with automated tests, NOT manual testing. Unit tests (Vitest) for pure logic, E2E tests (Mocha) for LSP integration features.
  1869	
  1870	See `/testing` and `/e2e-vscode-testing` skills for commands, fixture design, and helpers API.
  1871	
  1872	## Agent Implementation Rules
  1873	
  1874	### Codebase Navigation
  1875	
  1876	Use semantic code-navigation tools (Serena or equivalent MCP: symbol overviews, symbol/reference lookup, rename/refactor ops) before broad source reads. Read full source files only when symbolic context is insufficient or the file is small enough that a full read is clearly the most direct path.
  1877	
  1878	### Planning
  1879	
  1880	Prefer architecturally correct, long-term solutions; evaluate by correctness and durability, not implementation speed. Time constraints, implementation size, migration breadth, anticipated breaking changes, or "a lot of work" are not valid reasons to weaken the design, preserve a compromised path, or diverge from the approved plan — if the correct implementation is larger or breaking, plan for it explicitly or raise it before execution; never silently ship an architectural deviation. Do not provide time estimates unless explicitly asked, and never use estimated effort/duration/perceived time cost as a factor for doing, not doing, or partially doing planned work.
  1881	
  1882	Plans must include these sections:
  1883	1. **Context** — why this change is being made
  1884	---
  1885	name: architecture
  1886	description: "Verter codebase architecture: high-level module map, TypeScript packages, plugin system, CSS analysis, MCP server, static analysis types"
  1887	---
  1888	
  1889	# Verter Architecture Reference
  1890	
  1891	For domain-specific detail, see: `/type-resolution`, `/type-cache-architecture`, `/component-meta`, `/compiler-codegen`, `/host-session`.
  1892	
  1893	## Shared Substrate Principle
  1894	
  1895	Verter is one shared optimized codebase. Consumers reuse lower-level crates instead of separate semantic pipelines.
  1896	
  1897	- Put reusable parsing, analysis, type-resolution, caching, and import-following behavior in the shared owner crate.
  1898	- `verter_language` is the zero-dependency leaf routing authority: `FileLanguage`, `FrameworkAdapterId`, `LanguageId`, `CapabilityId`, and the pure static `LanguageRegistry` (`classify_static(path)` — never reads project config). Host-gated classification (static registry × `ProjectCapabilitySnapshot`) is owned by `verter_session::framework::HostLanguageClassifier`; scheduler/workspace consumers reach it only through session-implemented trait objects (`SourceLoader::classify` / `WorkspaceAccess::classify_file`). The crate is a `verter_span`-only leaf (its design allowance — spans for the parse-artifact regions; strings stay crate-interned) and keeps a crate-local id-intern table: no lower crate exposes a reusable interning facility, and the id set is bounded by registered languages. It also owns the framework-neutral parse payload: `FrameworkParseArtifact` (typed `FrameworkParseCommon` — `ScriptRegion { span, source_type, kind }` / template / style regions, external links, `LanguageDiagnostic`s — plus a PRIVATE erased `Arc<dyn CarrierParse>`), with the raw downcast confined to each adapter's own bridge module (no capability token — a foreign artifact's erased payload is a DIFFERENT concrete `CarrierParse` type, so the `Any` downcast already fails structurally for it); the session's blessed accessors are `FrameworkAdapterCtx::carrier_for::<T>` (routed through each adapter's registered-projector opener, e.g. `open_vue_carrier`) and the Vue adapter's `vue_parse()`; the concrete `VueParseCarrier` + Vue producer live in `verter_compiler::framework_common::vue_bridge`.
  1899	- `verter_session` is the shared host/session/cache boundary for host-backed consumers.
  1900	- `verter_semantic` and `verter_compiler` own reusable semantics, lowering, and codegen.
  1901	- `verter_session::resolver_core` owns the host-backed resolver stack and type-resolution orchestration. Resolver-path methods receive `ctx: &dyn ResolverContext` (sealed super-trait at `resolver_core/resolver_context.rs`) — only `VerterHost` implements it, enforced by the `no_concrete_verter_host_in_seal_scope` arch-guard.
  1902	- `verter_protocol` owns transport-facing schema DTOs; `verter_ffi` stays a thin native/WASM adapter layer.
  1903	- Consumer packages and apps stay adapter-oriented: thin wrappers, public API shaping, transport glue, UX-specific behavior.
  1904	
  1905	Bug or slowdown in one surface → fix in shared substrate so other consumers benefit.
  1906	
  1907	## TypeScript Packages
  1908	
  1909	| Package | Purpose | Entry Point |
  1910	| ------- | ------- | ----------- |
  1911	| **`@verter/types`** | TypeScript utility types (`PatchHidden`, `ExtractHidden`, `EmitsToProps`, etc.). Has `/string` export with `$V_` prefixed types for LSP injection | `src/index.ts` |
  1912	| **`@verter/language-shared`** | Shared custom protocol types between VS Code client and Rust LSP binary | `src/index.ts` |
  1913	| **`@verter/typescript-plugin`** | TypeScript plugin resolving `.vue` imports in TS/JS files. Intercepts module resolution to return transformed TSX | `src/index.ts` |
  1914	| **`verter-vscode`** | VS Code extension. Launches Rust `verter-lsp` binary over stdio, bundles TS plugin, handles extension activation | `src/extension.ts` |
  1915	| **`@verter/unplugin`** | Universal bundler plugin (Vite, Rollup, webpack, esbuild, rspack, Rolldown, Farm). Compiles `.vue` files via `@verter/native`. Supports `preCompile` for build-start cache warming | `src/index.ts` |
  1916	
  1917	## Unplugin Configuration (`packages/unplugin/`)
  1918	
  1919	`@verter/unplugin` provides a `VerterPluginOptions` interface:
  1920	
  1921	| Option | Type | Default | Description |
  1922	| ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
  1923	| `componentId` | `(filename, source, isProd) => string` | hash-based | Custom component ID generator |
  1924	| `include` | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]` | `[/\.vue$/]` | File patterns to include |
  1925	| `preCompile` | `boolean` | `false` | Pre-compile all `.vue` files during `buildStart`. Scans project root, upserts files into host cache (including type dependencies for macros), and compiles them. When `transform()` later receives same content, host returns cached result instantly. `node_modules` excluded from scanning. |
  1926	| `crossFileOptimize` | `boolean` | `false` | Cross-file prop constness optimization. Requires `preCompile: true`. After pre-compilation, analyzes render tree to determine which props are always passed constant values, skipping dynamic tracking in compiled output. |
  1927	| `template` | `object` | — | Template compiler options (compat with `@vitejs/plugin-vue`) |
  1928	
  1929	**`preCompile` architecture:** During `buildStart()`, scans project root for `.vue` files (excluding `node_modules` and dot-directories). For each file: upserts into host, resolves external `src` attributes and macro type dependencies (e.g., `import type { Props } from './types'` used in `defineProps<Props>()`), then triggers compilation. When another plugin modifies the file before `transform()`, host detects content change via internal hashing and recompiles. Third-party `.vue` files in `node_modules` compile on-demand during `transform()` — no pre-compilation overhead.
  1930	
  1931	**Macro type resolution invariant:** cross-file macro type resolution must only follow imports reachable from the requested type's local declaration graph. Unrelated imports in the same file are out of scope; plain imports are not implicit re-exports.
  1932	
  1933	## CSS Analysis & Selector Matching (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/`)
  1934	
  1935	`verter_css_syntax` is the shared lossless token/event authority for CSS, SCSS, indented Sass, Less, and Stylus. `StyleSyntaxIrSink` and `LosslessCstSink` are peers over the same parser event stream. Semantic style analysis projects only complete, static selector nodes into selectors, classes, IDs, custom properties, and at-rules; interpolation, recovery, and evaluation-dependent selectors fail closed. Each `AnalyzedCssClass` carries `selector_index` (exact class → comma-part selector join) and each `AnalyzedSelector` carries `rule_body_span` (brace- or indentation-delimited body span). Vue's planner separately consumes trusted IR for authored-dialect `v-bind()` and post-preprocess plain-CSS module hashing/scoping; Svelte consumes the IR as a trust gate for its distinct plain-CSS matcher/scoper. Svelte's carrier/CSS parser remains the compatibility owner until exact Svelte 5.56.3 error-code, offset, and read-past-close parity is proven. Style `v-bind()` usage is discovered through the same dialect-aware planner IR, then OXC-derived `expr_roots`/`roots_complete` remain the liveness facts consumed by `mark_bindings_used_in_style` and compile-input assembly.
  1936	
  1937	`StyleSyntaxIr` retains positioned containment and balanced values without evaluating or compiling preprocessors. Imports, modules, plugins, guards, mixin/function arguments, and control expressions remain opaque-but-positioned.
  1938	
  1939	Stylesheet parser mode is deterministic by dialect and structural tokens. CSS always uses brace grammar. Sass and Stylus use the layout-capable grammar, which also recognizes explicit braced blocks. SCSS and Less use brace grammar whenever the lexer emits any plain `LeftBrace`; only a brace-free source with an actual deeper-indented line pair uses layout grammar. Closing-brace indentation and other incidental formatting never select the parser. Selector trust folds every component descendant and functional-pseudo selector list; class/ID collection descends those lists and gates each component independently, so complete literal class components may still publish from an otherwise evaluation-dependent selector such as `&.active` or `:global(.a .#{$x})`. A textually certain `:deep`/`:global`/`:slotted` kind publishes independently of argument trust, while every class inside its argument remains subject to the same per-component gate. Ambiguous optional-syntax statements remain locally typed and diagnosed without recovering intact ancestor rules. A declaration may own a retained `StyleBlock` (for example, an indented Sass nested-property namespace); the IR sink never discards such a block.
  1940	
  1941	**Module structure:**
  1942	
  1943	```
  1944	style.rs              # Semantic style projection types and specificity computation
  1945	style_syntax.rs       # Five-dialect syntax-to-semantic projection
  1946	selector_match.rs     # Three-valued selector matching against template elements
  1947	template.rs           # Template element analysis, dynamic class extraction, :style CSS var extraction
  1948	```
  1949	
  1950	**Key types:**
  1951	
  1952	| Type | Location | Purpose |
  1953	| ---- | -------- | ------- |
  1954	| `StructuredSelector` | `style.rs` | Parsed CSS selector (compounds + combinators) |
  1955	| `CompoundSelector` | `style.rs` | Single compound: element, classes, id, attributes, pseudo-classes |
  1956	| `SelectorCombinator` | `style.rs` | Descendant / Child / NextSibling / LaterSibling |
  1957	| `MatchResult` | `selector_match.rs` | Three-valued: `Matches`, `MaybeMatches`, `NoMatch` |
  1958	| `DomQueryCallSite` | `types.rs` | DOM query call with parsed selector and spans |
  1959	| `StyleBlockAnalysis` | `style.rs` | Per-`<style>` block analysis with nested `CssAnalysis` |
  1960	| `AnalyzedCustomProperty` | `style.rs` | CSS custom property with name/value spans, var references, selector index |
  1961	| `CssVarReference` | `style.rs` | `var()` call with name, span, optional fallback (recursive) |
  1962	| `AnalyzedVarUsage` | `style.rs` | Regular CSS property using `var()` with property name and selector index |
  1963	| `CssVarManipulation` | `types.rs` | Script-side CSS variable manipulation via DOM APIs |
  1964	| `DynamicStyleVar` | `template.rs` | CSS variable set via `:style` binding in template |
  1965	| `StaticStyleVar` | `template.rs` | CSS variable set via static `style` attribute in template |
  1966	| `CssVarFlow` | `project_index.rs` | Cross-component CSS variable flow (definitions + usages + manipulations) |
  1967	
  1968	**CSS Variable Analysis (three-block tracking):**
  1969	
  1970	- **Style**: the balanced component-value IR projects `AnalyzedCustomProperty` (definitions with values/spans) and `AnalyzedVarUsage` (var() references). `extract_var_references()` handles nested var() fallbacks without evaluating values.
  1971	- **Template**: `extract_dynamic_style_vars()` extracts CSS vars from `:style="{ '--color': val }"`. `extract_static_style_vars()` extracts from `style="--color: red"`.
  1972	- **Script**: `try_extract_css_var_manipulation()` detects `el.style.setProperty('--x', val)`, `getPropertyValue('--x')`, `removeProperty('--x')`.
  1973	- **Cross-component**: `ProjectIndex.css_var_flow(name)` and `VerterHost.css_var_flow(name)` return `CssVarFlow` with all files defining/referencing/manipulating a variable.
  1974	
  1975	**Selector matching algorithm** (`match_selector()`):
  1976	
  1977	1. Match rightmost compound against target element
  1978	2. Walk left through combinators: `Child` checks `parent_index`, `Descendant` walks ancestor chain
  1979	3. Dynamic `:class` or component types → `MaybeMatches` (can't determine statically)
  1980	4. `:not()` inverts, `:is()`/`:where()` takes best match across alternatives
  1981	
  1982	**Position encoding for CSS spans**: `CssAnalysis` spans (classes, IDs, selectors) are **SFC-absolute byte offsets**. `CssSource` is constructed with the style content origin, so syntax and projection spans are absolute from creation. Consumers use spans directly without adding any offset. `StyleBlockAnalysis.content_offset` is retained for documentation and slice operations.
  1983	
  1984	## Analysis MCP Server (`verter_mcp`)
  1985	
  1986	`verter-mcp` binary exposes Verter's full analysis, diagnostics, compilation, and scoring pipeline via MCP for AI agents. `VerterMcpServer` wraps `VerterHost` (with `AnalysisScope::LSP`), `Linter`, and `ActionEngine`. Tools auto-load via `ensure_loaded()`; template analysis triggers `ensure_template_analysis()` transparently. Cross-file tools iterate all loaded files (no `ProjectIndex` exposed from host). Scoring engine computes composite 0-100 quality scores from a11y, lint, template complexity, API surface, CSS health, and reactivity dimensions.
  1987	
  1988	Both binaries (`verter-mcp`, and the LSP-decoupling twin `verter-mcp-server`) run the one shared entry body `verter_mcp::run::run`. The HTTP transport binds before its initial scan and announces the real bound port as a one-line stdout readiness record (`verter_mcp::readiness`, mirrored by `packages/vue-vscode/src/mcpServer.ts`); `--client-pid` arms the same `ClientProcessGuard` containment as the LSP. The VS Code extension spawns this standalone binary per LSP start attempt (`createMcpServerLifecycle`: awaited replacement, bounded crash respawn, provider-registration teardown on death) — see `docs/contributing/lsp-mcp-decoupling.md`.
  1989	
  1990	## verter_semantic::analysis — Static Analysis Types
  1991	
  1992	`verter_semantic::analysis` is the shared static-analysis surface consumed by `verter_session`, diagnostics, and tooling. Compilation crate owns lowering and codegen; `verter_session` projects compiler and workspace state into these semantic snapshots.
  1993	
  1994	### AnalysisScope
  1995	
  1996	Bitflags (`u32`) controlling which analysis passes run during file upsert.
  1997	
  1998	**Script (bits 0-7)**
  1999	
  2000	| Flag | Bit | Description |
  2001	| ---- | --- | ----------- |
  2002	| `IMPORTS` | 0 | Import declarations |
  2003	| `BINDINGS` | 1 | Variable/function/class declarations |
  2004	| `REACTIVITY` | 2 | Ref/reactive/computed classification |
  2005	| `MACROS` | 3 | defineProps/Emits/Model/Slots/Expose |
  2006	| `MACRO_TYPE_DEPS` | 4 | Cross-file type references in macros |
  2007	| `VUE_API_USAGE` | 5 | Track provide/inject/lifecycle/watcher calls |
  2008	| `EXPORT_SIGNATURES` | 6 | Per-export hashes for smart invalidation |
  2009	| `FUNC_RETURNS` | 7 | Analyze function return reactivity (for composables) |
  2010	
  2011	**Template (bits 8-15)**
  2012	
  2013	| Flag | Bit | Description |
  2014	| ---- | --- | ----------- |
  2015	| `TPL_COMPONENTS` | 8 | Component usages + prop expressions |
  2016	| `TPL_BINDINGS` | 9 | Which script bindings are used in template |
  2017	| `TPL_SLOTS` | 10 | Slot definitions + usages |
  2018	| `TPL_REFS` | 11 | Template ref attributes |
  2019	| `TPL_EVENTS` | 12 | Event handler bindings |
  2020	| `TPL_CONSTNESS` | 13 | Prop constness classification |
  2021	
  2022	**Style (bits 16-19)**
  2023	
  2024	| Flag | Bit | Description |
  2025	| ---- | --- | ----------- |
  2026	| `STYLE_CSS` | 16 | Full CSS analysis (selectors, classes, IDs) |
  2027	| `STYLE_VBIND` | 17 | v-bind() in styles |
  2028	| `STYLE_SCOPED` | 18 | Scoped/module metadata |
  2029	| `STYLE_PSEUDOS` | 19 | :deep/:global/:slotted |
  2030	
  2031	**Cross-file (bits 24-26)**
  2032	
  2033	| Flag | Bit | Description |
  2034	| ---- | --- | ----------- |
  2035	| `CROSS_RENDER_TREE` | 24 | Build render tree from template analysis |
  2036	| `CROSS_PROVIDE` | 25 | Provide/inject chain validation |
  2037	| `CROSS_PROP_CONST` | 26 | Prop constness optimization |
  2038	
  2039	**Presets:**
  2040	
  2041	| Preset | Flags | Use Case |
  2042	| ------ | ----- | -------- |
  2043	| `BUILD` | IMPORTS, BINDINGS, MACROS, MACRO_TYPE_DEPS, EXPORT_SIGNATURES, STYLE_VBIND, STYLE_SCOPED | Minimal overhead for compilation + smart invalidation |
  2044	| `BUILD_OPTIMIZED` | BUILD + REACTIVITY, VUE_API_USAGE, TPL_COMPONENTS, TPL_BINDINGS, TPL_CONSTNESS, CROSS_RENDER_TREE, CROSS_PROVIDE, CROSS_PROP_CONST | Build with cross-file optimization |
  2045	| `LSP` | All flags | Full analysis for completions, hover, diagnostics |
  2046	| `LINTER` | IMPORTS, BINDINGS, REACTIVITY, MACROS, VUE_API_USAGE, TPL_COMPONENTS, TPL_BINDINGS, TPL_SLOTS, TPL_REFS, TPL_EVENTS | Script + template for lint rules |
  2047	| `ESSENTIAL` | IMPORTS, BINDINGS, MACROS, MACRO_TYPE_DEPS, EXPORT_SIGNATURES | Script-only (legacy compat) |
  2048	
  2049	### ScriptAnalysisSnapshot
  2050	
  2051	Primary output of `build_script_analysis()`. Produced by a single OXC parse + AST walk.
  2052	
  2053	| Field | Type | Description |
  2054	| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
  2055	| `imports` | `Vec<AnalyzedImport>` | All import declarations with source, bindings, spans |
  2056	| `bindings` | `Vec<AnalyzedBinding>` | Top-level variable/function/class declarations |
  2057	| `macros` | `Vec<AnalyzedMacro>` | Vue macro calls (defineProps, defineEmits, etc.) |
  2058	| `macro_type_deps` | `Vec<MacroTypeDep>` | Cross-file type references used by macros, tiered by structural position (`usage: MacroTypeDepUsage` — `Surface` = argument root / intersection-union arms / extends heritage / alias chains, missing ⇒ error; `Member` = top-level member annotation, missing ⇒ warning + `null` degrade). References nested deeper are never collected (runtime codegen does not need them) |
  2059	| `flags` | `AnalysisFlags` | Bitwise flags for O(1) queries |
  2060	| `exported_functions` | `Vec<AnalyzedExportedFunction>` | Non-SFC exported functions (composable analysis). Carries `name` / `is_default` / `params` / `is_async` / `composable` only. It carries NO return-type field: the declared return type's reactive-wrapper identity is a resolution decision answered at demand time from the lowered typed IR plus a package-backed route proof (`/type-resolution` → Reactive-wrapper demand), never from annotation text on this DTO |
  2061	
  2062	**ReactivityKind**: None | Ref | Computed | Reactive | MaybeRef | Mutable
  2063	
  2064	### TemplateAnalysisSnapshot
  2065	
  2066	Populated after compilation by converting `RawTemplateData` from `verter_compiler`.
  2067	
  2068	| Field | Type | Description |
  2069	| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
  2070	| `components` | `Vec<TemplateComponentUsage>` | Components used in template with props and slots |
  2071	| `binding_occurrences` | `Vec<TemplateBindingOccurrence>` | Script bindings referenced in template with spans |
  2072	| `defined_slots` | `Vec<DefinedSlot>` | `<slot>` elements defined in template |
  2073	| `template_refs` | `Vec<TemplateRef>` | `ref="foo"` attributes |
  2074	| `event_handlers` | `Vec<TemplateEventHandler>` | `@click`, `@input`, etc. |
  2075	| `elements` | `Vec<TemplateElement>` | Full element tree for linter traversal |
  2076	| `if_chains` | `Vec<IfChain>` | v-if/v-else-if chains for duplicate detection |
  2077	| `prop_definitions` | `Vec<AnalyzedPropDefinition>` | Props from defineProps |
  2078	| `emit_definitions` | `Vec<AnalyzedEmitDefinition>` | Emits from defineEmits |
  2079	| `comment_directives` | `Vec<CommentDirective>` | `@verter:disable`, `@verter:todo`, etc. |
  2080	
  2081	### ProjectIndex
  2082	
  2083	Aggregates file-level usage into project-wide indexes:
  2084	
  2085	- **provide_index**: provide key → files that call `provide(key)`
  2086	- **inject_index**: inject key → files that call `inject(key)`
  2087	- **component_graph**: file → components it uses (forward edges)
  2088	- **component_reverse_index**: component name → files that use it
  2089	- **class_index**: CSS class name → files that define it
  2090	- **v_bind_css_index**: v-bind CSS expression → files that use it
  2091	- **custom_property_index**: CSS custom property → files that define it
  2092	
  2093	### Data Flow
  2094	
  2095	```
  2096	Vue SFC Source
  2097	    |
  2098	    v
  2099	verter_compiler::compile()
  2100	    |-- ScriptAnalysisSnapshot (from OXC parse during compilation)
  2101	    |-- RawTemplateData (spans, binding refs, component tags)
  2102	    |-- CssParsed* (v-bind spans, pseudo spans)
  2103	    |
  2104	    v
  2105	verter_session (conversion layer)
  2106	    |-- RawTemplateData --> TemplateAnalysisSnapshot
  2107	    |-- CssParsed*      --> StyleBlockAnalysis
  2108	    |-- Resolves import paths, populates resolved_canonical_id
  2109	    |-- Updates ProjectIndex with file usage
  2110	    |
  2111	    v
  2112	Consumers (LSP, build, linter) query snapshots + ProjectIndex
  2113	```

  3048	    73	## Intent Contract
  3049	    74	
  3050	    75	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
  3051	    76	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
  3052	    77	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
  3053	    78	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
  3054	    79	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation), by omission (no lifecycle exists
  3055	    80	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), and by the wrong crate holding the kernel at all (a session-tier
  3056	    81	crate that already depends on the compiler, so nothing compiler-tier can embed it without a cycle) — not
  3057	    82	by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added
  3058	    83	without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
  3059	    84	
  3060	    85	**Required observable outcomes.**
  3061	    86	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
  3062	    87	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
  3063	    88	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
  3064	    89	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
  3065	    90	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
  3066	    91	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
  3067	    92	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer — for **every** non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/
  3068	    93	  `TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt, not a subset.
  3069	    94	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_workspace`,
  3070	    95	  `verter_session`, `verter_scheduler`, nor `verter_tsgo_api` on any target — this closes debt row A5-DD1
  3071	    96	  by *deleting* the exception, not widening it (`crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/
  3072	    97	  workspace_dependency_layers.rs:118-127`, the `ratified_upward_exceptions()` row keyed
  3073	    98	  `"verter_semantic"`).
  3074	    99	- `resolver_core`, `resolver_store`'s immutable observation types, `project_semantic_dispatch`, and
  3075	   100	  `ModuleResolverCore` (the relocated `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver`) physically live in
  3076	   101	  `verter_semantic`. `verter_compiler` can depend on the converged kernel directly — it already does
  3077	   102	  (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`, `verter_semantic = { path = "../verter_semantic" }`) — with no
  3078	   103	  new edge and no cycle.
  3079	   104	- A new capability-limited, immutable **observation interface**, defined inside `verter_semantic`, does
  3080	   105	  **not** extend today's `ResolverContext` and cannot name, hold, or return `VerterHost` or the
  3081	   106	  scheduler — not because a marker says so, but because `verter_semantic`'s crate dependency closure
  3082	   107	  makes those types structurally unnameable from inside it.
  3083	   108	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (relocated to `verter_semantic`) has exactly as many
  3084	   109	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct blocking lifecycles; a lifecycle that
  3085	   110	  cannot resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for

Per C1-AC-7 and the Authority/fallback order clause, the observation interface is the *only* surface an I/O-free (C2-shaped) caller can reach a non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation through — `ResolverContext` itself can call `ensure_loaded`/`wait_or_drive`, so it is not usable I/O-free. The trait is defined so every method returns `AttemptOutcome<T>` at the type level (never a bare `T`, `Result<T, _>`, or a call that can block) — a non-conforming method is a compile error at authoring time, not a gap a test could miss. Gate: one exhaustive test double (`impl <ObservationInterface> for TestDouble`) that must implement every trait method to compile; a method added later that does not return `AttemptOutcome<T>` fails to compile at the double, not at a sampled runtime assertion.   3183	   207	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract — full coverage (Fork 4)
  3184	   208	
  3185	   209	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
  3186	   210	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
  3187	   211	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
  3188	   212	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
  3189	   213	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
  3190	   214	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet" crates/`
  3191	   215	— zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
  3192	   216

  3291	   315	## Structural confinement
  3292	   316	
  3293	   317	Every invariant above is enforced structurally, matching the pattern the codebase already uses in this
  3294	   318	exact area — C1 extends that pattern, it does not invent scanner-based enforcement:
  3295	   319	
  3296	   320	- **The crate dependency firewall is the primary proof, not a marker.** Per the Fork 1/3 ruling, "prove
  3297	   321	  extractability without extracting" is not mechanically checkable — the existing structural graph guard
  3298	   322	  cannot see intra-crate direction (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:
  3299	   323	  182-189`). Once the kernel physically lives in `verter_semantic`, the **existing, landed**
  3300	   324	  Cargo-metadata closure guard (`crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs`) is
  3301	   325	  sufficient and requires no new guard: `verter_semantic` simply cannot name `VerterHost`, the scheduler,
  3302	   326	  or `verter_tsgo_api` types, because its production dependency closure does not reach them. That is what
  3303	   327	  makes the new observation interface's non-blocking, host-free guarantee real — not a marker trait
  3304	   328	  layered on top of a context that could still physically hold a host reference.
  3305	   329	- **Sealed-trait lifecycle closure.** `ResolverContext: sealed::Sealed` (relocated with the trait) already
  3306	   330	  makes "some fourth, unregistered lifecycle adapter" a compile error. C1 preserves the seal and, if the
  3307	   331	  bare-host rail is deleted (see above), tightens `RequestBoundResolverContext` from "narrower than
  3308	   332	  `ResolverContext`" to "identical to it" — a resolver-tier function taking `&dyn ResolverContext` becomes
  3309	   333	  provably request-bound by construction, not by convention. The new observation interface is a *separate*
  3310	   334	  sealed trait, not a subtrait of `ResolverContext` — per the ruling, a subtrait inherits
  3311	   335	  `ensure_loaded`/the host escape hatch and proves nothing.
  3312	   336	- **`StoreView`/`HostStoreView` immutability is already structural**, not a convention: `HostStoreView`

  3314	   338	  (a live host reference smuggled into the struct) is a visible field addition a reviewer catches at the
  3315	   339	  type definition, not a runtime behavior to detect. This is one of the value types that relocates into

  3328	   352	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
  3329	   353	
  3330	   354	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
  3331	   355	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
  3332	   356	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
  3333	   357	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
  3334	   358	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
  3335	   359	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges (now physically in
  3336	   360	`verter_semantic`) remains the single authority `D1` integrates against behind its private non-production
  3337	   360	`verter_semantic`) remains the single authority `D1` integrates against behind its private non-production
  3338	   361	test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later extends without needing a second relation/name
  3339	   362	authority (`program.md:253`). The full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` threading touches the *calling
  3340	   363	convention* around `execute_relate` (per Fork 4) but never the relation algorithm itself.
  3341	   364	
  3342	   365	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
  3343	   366	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
  3344	   367	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
  3345	   368	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
  3346	   369	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is now concretely: a converged kernel
  3347	   370	physically resident in `verter_semantic` that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be
  3348	   371	driven from an I/O-free observation interface and returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking across its
  3349	   372	**full** operation surface, and (c) is constructible without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/
  3350	   373	`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery *by construction of the crate graph*, so C2's compiler-facing
  3351	   374	facade embeds `verter_semantic` the same way `verter_compiler` already does today

  3470	   213	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
  3471	   214	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet" crates/`
  3472	   215	— zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.

  3588	    84	# C1 — Converge `ModuleResolverCore` and non-flow `TypeInfoCore`
  3589	    85	
  3590	    86	**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** Foundational
  3591	    87	(`program-dag.toml:162`). **Predecessors:** `A6`, `B1`, `B2` (`program-dag.toml:163`).
  3592	    88	
  3593	    89	C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
  3594	    90	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and the TypeScript-style resolver living in
  3595	    91	`verter_workspace::resolver` — into the two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a
  3596	    92	`ModuleResolverCore` that owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow
  3597	    93	`TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution,
  3598	    94	relation/inference, effective typing, recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and
  3599	    95	exactness/completeness propagation. Neither target type exists in code today; both names describe roles
  3600	    96	the current tree already plays under different names and in the wrong crate. C1 does not invent new
  3601	    97	resolution semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be
  3602	    98	identical to today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code, how many
  3603	    99	duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform I/O
  3604	   100	directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
  3605	   101	
  3606	   102	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
  3607	   103	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
  3608	   104	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
  3609	   105	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions. It owns
  3610	   106	convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, and the addition of a batched,
  3611	   107	resumable load-outcome so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume the same kernel a blocking lifecycle
  3612	   108	consumes today.
  3613	   109	
  3614	   110	## Intent Contract
  3615	   111	
  3616	   112	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
  3617	   113	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
  3618	   114	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
  3619	   115	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
  3620	   116	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation) and by omission (no lifecycle exists
  3621	   117	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), not by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits
  3622	   118	a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
  3623	   119	
  3624	   120	**Required observable outcomes.**
  3625	   121	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
  3626	   122	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
  3627	   123	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
  3628	   124	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
  3629	   125	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
  3630	   126	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
  3631	   127	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer.
  3632	   128	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_scheduler` nor
  3633	   129	  `verter_tsgo_api` on any target (closes debt row A5-DD1, `evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:158-176`).
  3634	   130	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (`resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:161`) has exactly as many
  3635	   131	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct lifecycles; a lifecycle that cannot
  3636	   132	  resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
  3637	   133	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
  3638	   134	
  3639	   135	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
  3640	   136	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
  3641	   137	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
  3642	   138	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832` — C1 preserves this unchanged).
  3643	   139	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
  3644	   140	  observation views").
  3645	   141	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
  3646	   142	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext` implementor served it, for
  3647	   143	  identical inputs.
  3648	   144	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
  3649	   145	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
  3650	   146	
  3651	   147	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
  3652	   148	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
  3653	   149	point). `ResolverContext` implementors are lifecycle *adapters* over that one authority, never alternate
  3654	   150	authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed
  3655	   151	non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s `CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split,
  3656	   152	`.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) — C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken
  3657	   153	it while adding the `NeedInputs` outcome alongside it.

  3714	   210	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract
  3715	   211	
  3716	   212	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
  3717	   213	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
  3718	   214	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
  3719	   215	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
  3720	   216	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
  3721	   217	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet"
  3722	   218	crates/` — zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
  3723	   219	
  3724	   220	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
  3725	   221	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
  3726	   222	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
  3727	   223	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
  3728	   224	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
  3729	   225	C1's obligation ends at: one resolver-tier operation, one immutable snapshot, one typed outcome. C2's
  3730	   226	obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay
  3731	   227	tokens.
  3732	   228	
  3733	   229	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
  3734	   230	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
  3735	   231	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
  3736	   232	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome so a *new* I/O-free lifecycle can reuse the same resolution
  3737	   233	logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every existing call site to stop blocking.
  3738	   234

  3835	     2	//!
  3836	     3	//! Binds [`SemanticQueryKey`] variants onto the shared
  3837	     4	//! [`SemanticGraphStore`](crate::semantic_query_memo::SemanticGraphStore) memo
  3838	     5	//! and routes them to the existing resolver/solver entry points. This is the
  3839	     6	//! single dispatch site every reusable type-resolution operation flows
  3840	     7	//! through, regardless of which higher-level request initiated it.
  3841	     8	//!
  3842	     9	//! ## Scope of this landing
  3843	    10	//!
  3844	    11	//! Every [`SemanticQueryKey`] variant dispatches through this module:
  3845	    12	//!
  3846	    13	//! - `ResolveDecl` — returns a structural node sourced from the shallow state
  3847	    14	//!   (an `Object` surface when the declaration carries member signatures,
  3848	    15	//!   otherwise a `Primitive(Never)` anchor that memoizes the declaration's
  3849	    16	//!   scope/name identity).
  3850	    17	//! - `Instantiate` — identity-preserving alias anchored to the base node.
  3851	    18	//!   Memoizing the key is the dedup guarantee; the richer instantiation
  3852	    19	//!   shape is produced on demand by the solver once the caller walks
  3853	    20	//!   into it. Mode-free per the lazy-materialisation rule.
  3854	    21	//! - `ProjectPath` — path-precise projection rooted at `base` walking each
  3855	    22	//!   [`PathSegment`]. The empty-path form is the canonical shape of
  3856	    23	//!   "expand the whole surface" and supersedes the retired `Expand`
  3857	    24	//!   variant. `ProjectMember { base, member, mode }` and
  3858	    25	//!   `IndexedAccess { base, index, mode }` admission-canonicalise to the
  3859	    26	//!   length-1 `ProjectPath` form **before** memo hashing so sugar and
  3860	    27	//!   canonical share one warm entry and one in-flight wait graph.
  3861	    28	//! - `NormalizeUnion` / `NormalizeIntersection` — structural dedup over the
  3862	    29	//!   supplied members with stable ordering.
  3863	    30	//! - `KeyOf` / `MappedType` / `Conditional` — navigation operations that
  3864	    31	//!   walk the base node's shared-graph payload. Paths that do not reach a
  3865	    32	//!   concrete node fall through to a recorded `Opaque(Miss)` entry — this
  3866	    33	//!   is distinct from a dispatch miss because the warm entry observes the
  3867	    34	//!   base node identity and therefore dedups repeated asks.
  3868	    35	//! - `TypeOf` — mirrors `ResolveDecl` but routes through the shallow
  3869	    36	//!   value-symbol space.
  3870	    37	//!
  3871	    38	//! Every variant observes a dep-signature fragment (at minimum the project
  3872	    39	//! generation; additional file hashes flow in from the base nodes' origin
  3873	    40	//! scopes where the dispatcher can observe them). Dep-signature propagation
  3874	    41	//! is what the publish-side completion-fence revalidation relies on for
  3875	    42	//! transitive final-result validation.
  3876	    43	//!
  3877	    44	//! ## Design rules
  3878	    45	//!
  3879	    46	//! - Navigators stay non-owning: new semantic nodes must enter through
  3880	    47	//!   [`SemanticQueryApi::execute`], not through ad-hoc helpers on the
  3881	    48	//!   dispatcher.
  3882	    49	//! - Errors, partial results, and recursion sentinels never promote to warm
  3883	    50	//!   memo entries — the underlying [`SemanticGraphStore`] enforces this
  3884	    51	//!   invariant at publish time.
  3885	    52	//! - Dep-signatures returned from warm hits must fold into the caller's
  3886	    53	//!   dependency-fact set so the publish-side completion-fence
  3887	    54	//!   revalidation stays transitive.

  4227	   800	
  4228	   801	## 10.1 Separation of concerns
  4229	   802	
  4230	   803	```text
  4231	   804	API demand
  4232	   805	-> QueryRuntime
  4233	   806	   -> validated hit: return inline
  4234	   807	   -> compatible running FlightCell: join
  4235	   808	   -> new cold FlightCell
  4236	   809	      -> cheap dependent work: inline

  4238	   811	      -> owner-affine work: owner call/inline
  4239	   812	```
  4240	   813

  4244	   817

  4255	   828	## 10.3 Flight classes and compatibility
  4256	   829	
  4257	   830	Two default flight scopes exist:
  4258	     1	# ADR-001 — One Semantic Authority, Justified Derived Projections
  4259	     2	
  4260	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
  4261	     4	**Decision owner:** TypeInfo/effective-flow architecture
  4262	     5	
  4263	     6	## Context
  4264	     7	
  4265	     8	`FunctionFlowGraph` must be the one structural flow authority, but efficient solving may need dominators, loop forests, SCCs, def-use overlays, capture summaries, reverse adjacency, or compact execution schedules. Forbidding every graph-derived structure would either bloat the canonical graph or repeat topology work. Allowing independent query-specific CFGs recreates the current dual-authority defect.
  4266	     9	
  4267	    10	## Decision
  4268	    11	
  4269	    12	`FunctionFlowGraph` is the canonical structural authority. A derived structure is allowed only when it:
  4270	    13	
  4271	    14	- is keyed by one exact graph/body identity and any interpretation-affecting semantic profile;
  4272	    15	- is deterministic and fully reproducible from the graph and accepted kernel rules;
  4273	    16	- cannot add facts, define transfer/join semantics, mark coverage complete, or publish a semantic result;
  4274	    17	- is request-local by default and independently weighted/evicted if retention is proven valuable;
  4275	    18	- can be replaced without changing observable semantics.
  4276	    19	
  4277	    20	## Consequences
  4278	    21	
  4279	    22	The solver may use efficient layouts without creating a second semantic or control authority. Review checks authority and construction rights, not superficial data-structure count.
  4280	    23	
  4281	    24	## Rejected alternatives
  4282	    25	
  4283	    26	- exactly one physical graph-like object;
  4284	    27	- independent syntax-shaped/query-specific CFGs;
  4285	    28	- projections that own relation, completion, capture, or coverage decisions.
  4286	     1	# ADR-006 — Flow Uses Demand-Selected Abstract Domains
  4287	     2	
  4288	     3	**Status:** Accepted
  4289	     4	
  4290	     5	## Context
  4291	     6	
  4292	     7	One binding-based solver is required, but one always-maximal state would make every operation pay for narrowing, completion, definite assignment, freshness, capture/effects, and coverage.
  4293	     8	
  4294	     9	## Decision
  4295	    10	
  4296	    11	Use one solver framework and one authoritative transfer/join implementation per closed flow domain. `FlowDemandPlan` activates the transitive prerequisite closure required by the result contract. Fixed points run only over the selected obligation frontier.
  4297	    12	
  4298	    13	Structural authored-return collection is independent of endpoint completion. A private obligation ledger and finalizer construct complete results; a query cannot omit required domains manually.
  4299	    14	
  4300	    15	## Consequences
  4301	    16	
  4302	    17	Narrow queries stay narrow without introducing a second evaluator. Domains are independently testable while completeness remains global to the requested result.
  4303	    18	
  4304	    19	## Rejected alternatives
  4305	    20

  4309	     1	# ADR-014 — Flow Replaces the Legacy Evaluator in One Atomic Public Cutover
  4310	     2	
  4311	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
  4312	     4	**Decision owner:** flow migration and cache admission  
  4313	     5	**Reopen only if:** a release obligation explicitly requires two semantics paths, which would require a new architecture decision and bounded compatibility window.
  4314	     6	
  4315	     7	## Context
  4316	     8	
  4317	     9	Building graph/domain features across many accepted merges while the old syntax-shaped evaluator remains selectable creates two production authorities. Deleting the old path only after full parity pressures implementors to copy the legacy model into the replacement.
  4318	    10	
  4319	    11	## Decision
  4320	    12	
  4321	    13	1. Build the minimum new graph/domain/obligation/coverage foundation behind a private non-production test boundary on the bounded cutover branch; it may be reviewed as a checkpoint but never merged or released independently.
  4322	    14	2. In one public cutover, route all effective-flow operations to the new solver and delete the old evaluator and its state/caches/tasks/flags.
  4323	    15	3. Unsupported mechanisms return typed non-admissible gaps; temporary reduction from guessed success to honest partial is allowed only for rows not ratified Supported/Stable, or through a separate reviewed breaking product decision.
  4324	    16	4. Later semantic blocks only expand the sole solver.
  4325	    17	5. A private obligation ledger and finalizer make complete-result construction impossible unless all required closed-domain obligations are discharged.
  4326	    18	
  4327	    19	No runtime flag, compatibility shim, shadow evaluator, or compare-in-production path survives the accepted cutover.
  4328	    20	
  4329	    21	## Consequences
  4330	    22	
  4331	    23	- one production semantic authority at all times after `D2`;
  4332	    24	- completeness proof is architectural rather than a convention;
  4333	    25	- parity can expand without preserving guessed legacy behavior.
  4334	    26	
  4335	    27	## Rejected alternatives
  4336	    28	
  4337	    29	- **Long-running dual evaluators:** divergent semantics and cache risk.
  4338	    30	- **Wait for full parity before deletion:** encourages porting the second authority intact.

  4806	   402	    /// The stack index of `identity` when that tagged obligation is already

  4820	   416	    /// Push a fresh RELATION frame for `(key, occurrence)` with the pending
  4821	   417	    /// ledger's current length as its drain watermark; returns its stack
  4822	   418	    /// index.
  4823	   419	    pub(crate) fn push_relate(
  4824	   420	        &mut self,
  4825	   421	        key: RelateMemoKey,
  4826	   422	        occurrence: InferenceOccurrence,
  4827	   423	        pending_watermark: usize,
  4828	   424	    ) -> usize {
  4829	   425	        let identity = ObligationIdentity::Relate { key, occurrence };
  4830	   426	        let idx = self.frames.len();
  4831	   427	        self.frames.push(ObligationFrame {
  4832	   428	            identity: identity.clone(),
  4833	   429	            assumption_targets: Vec::new(),
  4834	   430	            min_open_target: None,
  4835	   540	    /// own callee gate records those).
  4836	   541	    pub(crate) fn record_nearest_flow_hold(&mut self, hold: ReturnObligationIdentity) -> bool {
  4837	   542	        if matches!(hold, ReturnObligationIdentity::FlowReturn(_)) {
  4838	   543	            return false;
  4839	   544	        }
  4840	   545	        let Some(state) = self
  4841	   546	            .frames
  4842	   547	            .iter_mut()
  4843	   548	            .rev()
  4844	   549	            .find_map(|frame| match &mut frame.domain {
  4845	   550	                ObligationFrameDomain::FlowReturn(state) => Some(state),
  4846	   551	                ObligationFrameDomain::Relate(_) | ObligationFrameDomain::ResolveCall(_) => None,
  4847	   552	            })
  4848	   553	        else {
  4849	   554	            return false;
  4850	   555	        };
  4851	   556	        if !state.holds.contains(&hold) {
  4852	   557	            state.holds.push(hold);
  4853	   558	        }
  4854	   559	        true
  4855	   560	    }
  4856	   561	}

  8742	### Editor-Liveness Provider-Sync Invariant (CRITICAL)
  8743	
  8744	Open-document provider-sync state is an editor-liveness invariant. An OPEN `.vue` document must keep a usable IDE TSX (`{src}.vue.tsx` / `.jsx`) live in the type provider so hover / completion / diagnostics keep working — regardless of ownership. Every `.vue` IDE/API provider sync, in every context (snapshot drain, aliased-import resync, barrel Vue-dependency pass, foreground `ensure_current_file_synced`, debounced `SyncCoordinator`, background API twin, workspace scanner), obeys the same discipline:
  8745	
  8746	- **Ownership None / ambiguous never removes an open `.vue`'s state nor closes its IDE TSX.** A ready snapshot that resolves no owner for an OPEN document converts the committed state to `Unresolved` (preserving the owner-independent IDE TSX) and keeps the file QUEUED for a future owner — it does NOT clear state or close the TSX. Only a genuinely non-open import is removed + closed.
  8747	- **Owner transitions sync-new → commit → close-stale, per kind (never close-before-sync).** On an owner change the new paths are opened/updated FIRST; only after a kind's replacement sync succeeds is its genuinely-stale path closed (`genuinely_stale_after_sync` gates on synced-kind AND non-active). A kind whose replacement sync FAILS reverts to its previous live path (`revert_unsynced_kinds`) and that path stays open — a failed reconciliation leaves the prior path alive. On total failure nothing is committed or closed.
  8748	- **Owner mismatch / loss forces reconciliation, not only `is_unresolved()`.** A previously-`Owned` open `.vue` whose owner changed or disappeared must be reconciled even when its IDE is already synced (`committed_binding_matches_current` / `current_owner_binding_for_source`); a fully-loaded import is only short-circuited when its committed binding still matches the live resolution. The owned→unowned conversion drops the owner-derived `.vue.ts` API path AND closes it (`dropped_api_path_on_unowned_conversion`) — that path is invalid once unowned — while never closing the IDE TSX.
  8749	- **Partial sync stays queued for retry.** A drain pass that syncs one kind but fails another returns `SyncOutcome::Partial`; the drain dequeues only on `FullyReconciled`, so a failed kind is retried rather than permanently suppressed.
  8750	- **`active_ide_path_for_uri` is state-backed only.** Interactive routing reads the committed `ProviderSyncState`, never re-derives a path from ownership at request time.
  8751	
  8752	**Guards**: `vue_sync_functions_never_inline_close_the_stale_set` + `guard_detector_discriminates_inline_close_from_delegation` + `vue_sync_functions_never_delegate_raw_stale_close` + `delegated_close_detector_discriminates_vue_evasion_from_approved_and_non_vue` (the static `editor_liveness_guards` architecture guard — source-scans every LSP provider-sync file and FAILS if any function other than the approved leaf close-dispatch primitives contains an inline provider-close loop, OR if any `.vue`-syncing function delegates a raw transition stale set to a close helper before syncing; the delegated-close detector uses fixed-point `let`-taint propagation + recursive close-arg inspection to catch wrapper/`.clone()`/by-value/multi-hop-alias/`Vec`-collect evasions). The per-kind close-after-sync helpers (`revert_unsynced_kinds`, `genuinely_stale_after_sync`, `dropped_api_path_on_unowned_conversion`, `committed_binding_matches_current`) and their integration paths are pinned by the discriminating drain / aliased-resync / barrel / foreground regression tests in `provider_sync.rs` + `server_tests.rs`.
