 10525	   408	# 5. Input authority and snapshots
 10526	   409	
 10527	   410	## 5.1 One committed input authority
 10528	   411	
 10529	   412	The managed system has exactly one authority for committed sources, overlays, project topology, and configuration. `InputStore` is the logical role; Revision 11 does not require inventing a new type when the current registered-source/VFS/`PublishedRoot` machinery already owns the invariant and can be converged in place.
 10530	   413	
 10531	   414	The required invariant is:
 10532	   415	
 10533	   416	> A reader observes one coherent source/project/configuration state before a commit or after it, never independently sampled roots from different commits.
 10534	   417	
 10535	   418	An immutable/persistent root published through a short atomic commit is preferred. Equivalent implementations are allowed only if they preserve coherent capture, ordered document mutation, conditional commit, short writer critical sections, bounded memory, and deterministic snapshot identity.
 10536	   419	
 10537	   420	No parse, compile, TypeInfo, provider, index, cache validation, or external I/O runs inside the input write critical section.
 10538	   421	
 10539	   422	Before managed QueryRuntime/cache convergence, the current input/VFS/publication owner is classified and its snapshot/fact API is locked. Query infrastructure must not be built around a transitional or independently sampled source view.
 10540	   423	
 10541	   424	## 5.2 Ordered document mutation
 10542	   425	
 10543	   426	For each document:
 10544	   427	
 10545	   428	- accepted incremental edits are applied in order;
 10546	   429	- incarnation and document version are validated;
 10547	   430	- edits are never dropped or coalesced before source application;
 10548	   431	- derived work may be cancelled/coalesced after commit;
 10549	   432	- an invalid range/version gap enters an explicit unsynchronized state;
 10550	   433	- a later range is never applied to unproven text.
 10551	   434	
 10552	   435	## 5.3 Lazy input loading
 10553	   436	
 10554	   437	Reusable semantic/compiler computation performs no unversioned filesystem, network, package-manager, or process read behind a snapshot. Missing information is resolved by the deterministic state machine in `contracts/input-loading.md`.
 10555	   438	
 10556	   439	At a high level:
 10557	   440	
 10558	   441	```text
 10559	   442	Attempt(snapshot, accumulated observations, resource budget)
 10560	   443	  -> Complete(result)
 10561	   444	  -> NeedInputs(normalized LoadSet)
 10562	   445	  -> TerminalFailure
 10563	   446	```
 10564	   447	
 10565	   448	For `NeedInputs`:
 10566	   449	
 10567	   450	1. normalize, sort, and deduplicate the complete discovered set for the attempt;
 10568	   451	2. compute `delta = requested - previously_requested`;
 10569	   452	3. fail with typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` when `delta` is empty and no observed basis changed;
 10570	   453	4. enforce total unique-input, byte, dependency-depth, retry, and churn budgets;
 10571	   454	5. load `delta` through same-key I/O flights owned outside the semantic kernel;
 10572	   455	6. conditionally commit successful and stable negative observations as one coherent batch when the project/configuration basis is still current;
 10573	   456	7. capture a new snapshot and restart the whole semantic attempt;
 10574	   457	8. never splice newly loaded data into an in-progress derivation.
 10575	   458	
 10576	   459	A basis change may justify a retry even with the same symbolic dependency, but it consumes the configured churn/restart budget. Partial load success, stable missing observations, and transient loader failures have distinct typed outcomes.
 10577	   460	
 10578	   461	`TypeInfoEnvironment` is an immutable/data-only observation view. Public/external environments provide bytes and typed metadata, not authoritative semantic fingerprints: Verter validates key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints at the capture boundary. A caller-supplied digest is a hint unless it was minted by a sealed first-party snapshot authority and carries its validity basis. A direct project session returns `NeedInputs` to its caller; a managed embedding may run the outer load/commit/retry loop. The compiler and semantic kernel remain I/O-free.

 10594	   564	# 7. Direct compiler, plans, and compile projections
 10595	   565	
 10596	   566	## 7.1 Direct compiler boundary
 10597	   567	
 10598	   568	The direct compiler is a separate product boundary, not an `Engine` mode. It exposes borrowed-source one-shot compilation, explicit prepared reuse, and staged batch planning/emission. It owns no workspace, committed input store, QueryRuntime, provider lifecycle, durable cache set, audit database, or background scheduler.
 10599	   569	
 10600	   570	No public `dyn CompileTypeInfo`, open resolver trait, `Engine`, `VerterHost`, provider state, or ambient filesystem handle enters the direct compiler.
 10601	   571	
 10602	   572	## 7.2 Typed operation plan
 10603	   573	
 10604	   574	The compiler consumes the final compositional request and derives the smallest acyclic prerequisite closure. A cold request plans once by default. Deliberate replanning is allowed only when benchmark evidence shows it is cheaper in total CPU, allocation, retained memory, and complexity than carrying the first plan.
 10605	   575	
 10606	   576	Unsupported product combinations fail before expensive work. No projection demands means zero TypeInfo construction/call and zero project read.
 10607	   577	
 10608	   578	## 7.3 Resumable projection protocol
 10609	   579	
 10610	   580	Project-aware compilation follows:
 10611	   581	
 10612	   582	```text
 10613	   583	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
 10614	   584	```
 10615	   585	
 10616	   586	Conceptually:
 10617	   587	
 10618	   588	```rust
 10619	   589	let mut prepared = compiler.prepare(source_id, source, parse_options)?;
 10620	   590	let plan = prepared.plan(request)?;
 10621	   591	
 10622	   592	loop {
 10623	   593	    match type_info.project(plan.projection_batch())? {
 10624	   594	        ProjectionOutcome::Complete(facts) => {
 10625	   595	            plan.validate_facts(&facts)?;
 10626	   596	            break prepared.emit(plan, facts);
 10627	   597	        }
 10628	   598	        ProjectionOutcome::NeedInputs(load_set) => {
 10629	   599	            return CompileAttempt::NeedInputs {
 10630	   600	                prepared,
 10631	   601	                plan,
 10632	   602	                load_set,
 10633	   603	            };
 10634	   604	        }
 10635	   605	    }
 10636	   606	}
 10637	   607	```
 10638	   608	
 10639	   609	The exact Rust API may use separate types/builders. The invariants are binding:
 10640	   610	
 10641	   611	- `CompileProjectionBatch` is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
 10642	   612	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized per-product request to the retained prepared root for anti-replay;
 10643	   613	- the plan also contains narrower deterministic `ProjectionPlanToken`, product-subplan tokens, and terminal-subplan tokens, so a terminal-only change does not invalidate unchanged semantic/code artifacts;
 10644	   614	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, and completeness—not to unrelated presentation or serialization fields;
 10645	   615	- stale, replayed, mismatched, or injected facts are rejected before emission;
 10646	   616	- no AST borrow, arena pointer, or unvalidated locator crosses external I/O;
 10647	   617	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome, not a generic internal error;
 10648	   618	- the outer caller may extend a captured project view and retry under the load-wave/no-progress contract;
 10649	   619	- a project/configuration basis change invalidates/replans as specified by the token rather than silently reusing facts.
 10650	   620	
 10651	   621	One-shot convenience APIs may orchestrate local-only semantics synchronously. Project-capable convenience orchestration must remain explicit about loading and retry; compute itself stays I/O-free.
 10652	   622	
 10653	   623	## 7.4 Sealed `CompileTypeInfo`
 10654	   624	
 10655	   625	```rust
 10656	   626	pub struct CompileTypeInfo<'env> {
 10657	   627	    inner: CompileTypeInfoInner<'env>,
 10658	   628	}
 10659	   629	```

 10661	   631	All first-party local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes execute one `TypeInfoCore`, one `ModuleResolverCore`, and one profile-parameterized relation/inference implementation.  10662	   632	
 10663	   633	No blanket `Send + Sync` applies. Parallel batches use staged prepare/plan, one TypeInfo owner with internal parallelism or explicit first-party per-worker sessions, and parallel emit when legal.
 10664	   634	
 10665	   635	Validated precomputed facts are optional and accepted only after domain/profile/toolchain/source/dependency/completeness/integrity/size and anti-replay validation. Callers cannot mint arbitrary resolved facts.

 10667	   637	## 7.5 Closed framework projections
 10668	   638	
 10669	   639	The compiler discovers exact closed projection demands. Vue runtime macro projection contains only facts runtime generation consumes: prop/model identity, optional/required/default association, ordered broad runtime constructors, `skip_check`/typed degradation, provenance anchor, and exact dependency/profile basis.

 10675	   645	# 8. TypeInfo semantic kernel and public API
 10676	   646	
 10677	   647	## 8.1 One implementation
 10678	   648	
 10679	   649	`TypeInfoCore` owns:
 10680	   650	
 10681	   651	- authored-node traversal;
 10682	   652	- binder/name/reference semantics;
 10683	   653	- substitution;
 10684	   654	- relation/inference;
 10685	   655	- effective typing;
 10686	   656	- recursion/work budgets;
 10687	   657	- query-specific projection;

 10689	   659	
 10690	   660	`ModuleResolverCore` owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution. Environments supply observations; they do not implement semantics.
 10691	   661	
 10692	   662	Direct local, direct project, in-memory, managed, compile projection, component metadata, effective type, and framework surface operations share these kernels. Lifecycle adapters differ only in data access, concurrency, and retention.

 10694	   664	## 8.2 No final general `TypeExpr`, with ordered cutover

 10821	    13	## Objective
 10822	    14	
 10823	    15	Land dependency-neutral types and canonical encodings needed by later blocks without creating
 10824	    16	service owners or migrating semantic behavior.
 10825	    17	
 10826	    18	## Required final state
 10827	    19	
 10828	    20	Carried unchanged from the template:
 10829	    21

 10831	    23	- canonical encoding golden vectors shared by native/WASM where applicable;
 10832	    24	- `StableEntityId` and `SessionHandle` non-interchangeable;
 10833	    25	- `QueryIdentity` distinct from `SemanticFlightKey` and `InputBasisId`;

 10869	    61	### Dependency-direction test (the block's own exit criterion)
 10870	    62	
 10871	    63	The strategy is **locked** by [`evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md`](../evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md).
 10872	    64	B1 implements it; B1 does not redesign it. Binding points:
 10873	    65	
 10874	    66	- **One `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features` forbidden-edge test over the whole
 10875	    67	  workspace graph**, modelled on `crates/verter_macro_dto/tests/cases/dependency_closure_guard.rs`.
 10876	    68	  **No new source-text scanner** — `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only rule forbids a name-keyed file scanner
 10877	    69	  as landed enforcement, and three of the four current mechanisms are exactly that grandfathered form.
 10878	    70	- Edges: normal + build, transitive; dev edges excluded and the exclusion stated.
 10879	    71	- Assertion form: **closure-based, not direct-edge-based**. A direct-edge test passes while a two-hop
 10880	    72	  violation walks straight through it, and §4 of the A5 artifact shows that is not hypothetical.
 10881	    73	- Exceptions: **equality-pinned, never subset-checked**, each with a recorded rationale and a named
 10882	    74	  removal gate.
 10883	    75	- Discrimination: the test must FAIL when a forbidden edge is added. Prove it by adding one to a
 10884	    76	  scratch manifest and observing the failure, and prove the mutation was actually applied
 10885	    77	  (`CLAUDE.md` → *Verification Must Prove Execution*: a plant that fails to apply reports a pass).

 10888	    80	  justification there.

 10899	    91	
 10900	    92	**A5-DD1, maintainer-ratified.** `verter_semantic -> verter_workspace` (and
 10901	    93	`verter_diagnostics -> verter_workspace`) are recorded as an **equality-pinned exception** with `C1`
 10902	    94	as the removal gate.

 10905	    97	declared differently in `crates/verter_workspace/Cargo.toml`:
 10906	    98	
 10907	    99	| dep | declaration | reach |
 10908	   100	|---|---|---|

 10990	    26	## 2. The locked strategy
 10991	    27	
 10992	    28	**One `cargo metadata`-driven forbidden-edge test over the whole workspace graph, modelled
 10993	    29	exactly on `verter_macro_dto`'s `dependency_closure_guard`. No new source-text scanner.**
 10994	    30	
 10995	    31	This is not a stylistic preference; it follows from `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only rule: *landed*
 10996	    32	enforcement is compiler/type-system/tool-based and never a name/text/grep scanner over the source
 10997	    33	tree. Three of the four mechanisms above are exactly the scanner form that rule grandfathers but
 10998	    34	forbids extending. The fourth is the model to generalise, and it is already the better test on the
 10999	    35	merits:
 11000	    36	
 11001	    37	- it reads what cargo actually links, so a forbidden edge added **behind any feature**, or
 11002	    38	  arriving **transitively**, fails — a manifest scan sees none of those;
 11003	    39	- it distinguishes production edges (normal + build) from dev-dependencies, so a guard's own
 11004	    40	  tooling dev-deps cannot self-trip it;
 11005	    41	- it pins its sanctioned exception by **equality** against a structurally computed set, so an
 11006	    42	  upstream release that grows the exception is a re-audit gate rather than a silent grant.
 11007	    43	
 11008	    44	Naming crates in a layer matrix is not the scanner failure mode the rule forbids. The rule's
 11009	    45	target is text matching over source; a resolve-graph walk over cargo's own output is the
 11010	    46	"real used tool" form it prescribes. The matrix is data for a graph query, not a grep pattern.
 11011	    47	
 11012	    48	### 2.1 Required properties of the `B1` test
 11013	    49	
 11014	    50	1. **Input** — `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`, the resolve cargo builds from.
 11015	    51	2. **Edges** — normal + build, transitive. Dev edges excluded and that exclusion stated.
 11016	    52	3. **Assertion form** — for each crate, its production closure must not reach any crate in a
 11017	    53	   strictly higher layer. Closure-based, not direct-edge-based: a direct-edge test passes while a
 11018	    54	   two-hop violation walks straight through it (§4 shows this is not hypothetical).
 11019	    55	4. **Exceptions** — equality-pinned, never subset-checked, each with a recorded rationale.
 11020	    56	5. **Discrimination** — the test must FAIL when a forbidden edge is added. `B1` proves it by
 11021	    57	   adding one to a scratch manifest and observing the failure, and the proof must show the
 11022	    58	   mutation was actually applied (`CLAUDE.md` → Verification Must Prove Execution: a plant that
 11023	    59	   fails to apply reports a pass).
 11024	    60	6. **Supersession, with one residue that must be decided rather than assumed.** Landing the
 11025	    61	   closure test deletes `verter_audit_no_upward_deps` and both tests in `no_session_dep.rs`:
 11026	    62	   their invariants are strictly implied by the walk (`verter_audit` closure ⊆
 11027	    63	   {`verter_audit`, `verter_span`}; `verter_scheduler` closure excludes `verter_session`), and
 11028	    64	   a source path reference to a non-dependency crate does not compile, so the source-scan half
 11029	    65	   adds nothing a closure walk misses. Keeping them would be a second authority for one rule,
 11030	    66	   and deleting them in the same accepted candidate is `CLAUDE.md`'s clean-cutover requirement.
 11031	    67	
 11032	    68	   `audit_substrate_isolation` is **not** fully implied, and `B1` must not delete it on the
 11033	    69	   assumption that it is. Its *dependency* half is implied. Its residue is a **naming** rule: it
 11034	    70	   rejects any `verter_*` token on a non-comment line in `crates/verter_audit/src`, including
 11035	    71	   ones that are not dependencies at all — that is exactly what it caught during A4, when the
 11036	    72	   scope macro's local binding `_verter_attribution_scope` tripped it. A closure walk cannot see
 11037	    73	   a local variable name. So `B1` decides explicitly: either the naming rule is worth keeping as
 11038	    74	   a separate, named, grandfathered guard, or it is dropped as coverage the program does not
 11039	    75	   need. Silently deleting it and calling the closure test a superset would lose real coverage.

 11066	   102	## 4. The two upward edges in the current tree
 11067	   103	
 11068	   104	Running the proposed matrix over the resolved graph yields **exactly two** production edges that
 11069	   105	point upward:
 11070	   106	
 11071	   107	```text
 11072	   108	L3 verter_semantic     ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
 11073	   109	L3 verter_diagnostics  ->  L5 verter_workspace   (normal)
 11074	   110	```
 11075	   111	
 11076	   112	`verter_semantic` uses `verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead` (6 sites), `resolver`, `types`,
 11077	   113	`fact_registry`, and `FilesystemWorkspace`.
 11078	   114	
 11079	   115	**This is not repairable by re-layering.** The tempting fix — move `verter_workspace` down to
 11080	   116	layer 2 — fails, because `verter_workspace` itself depends on `verter_scheduler` and
 11081	   117	`verter_tsgo_api`. The two are declared differently, and `B1` must not conflate them
 11082	   118	(`crates/verter_workspace/Cargo.toml`):
 11083	   119	
 11084	   120	| dep | declaration | reach |
 11085	   121	|---|---|---|
 11086	   122	| `verter_scheduler` | `[dependencies]`, line 37 | unconditional — every target |
 11087	   123	| `verter_tsgo_api` | `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`, line 49 | native only; absent from a `wasm32` build |
 11088	   124	
 11089	   125	So the edge is real on every target, and its consequence is measurable — but the `verter_tsgo_api`
 11090	   126	half of that consequence is **native-only**:
 11091	   127	
 11092	   128	```text
 11093	   129	verter_semantic's production closure (--all-features, normal+build, transitive):
 11094	   130	  verter_audit  verter_css_syntax  verter_ecma  verter_language
 11095	   131	  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_parser
 11096	   132	  verter_scheduler  verter_span  verter_tsgo_api  verter_type_expr
 11097	   133	  verter_type_expr_oxc  verter_workspace
 11098	   134	```
 11099	   135	
 11100	   136	That closure is the `--all-features` **native** resolve, which is what `cargo metadata` reports by
 11101	   137	default and what the closure test will read.
 11102	   138	
 11103	   139	**The semantic kernel's production closure reaches the task scheduler unconditionally, and the
 11104	   140	external tsgo API on native targets.** ADR-015's stated consequence — "semantic kernel remains
 11105	   141	reusable across lifecycles" — does not hold today: linking the kernel links a task scheduler on
 11106	   142	every target, and additionally an out-of-process tool client on everything but `wasm32`. The
 11107	   143	platform split narrows the second half of the violation; it does not repair either half, because a
 11108	   144	`wasm32`-only firewall is not a firewall.
 11109	   145	
 11110	   146	Compare the crates that *do* satisfy their firewall:
 11111	   147	
 11112	   148	```text
 11113	   149	verter_audit      -> verter_audit  verter_span
 11114	   150	verter_macro_dto  -> verter_macro_dto  verter_no_storedspan(+_derive)  verter_no_typeexpr(+_derive)  verter_span
 11115	   151	```
 11116	   152	
 11117	   153	Reproduce all three with the closure walk over `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features`,
 11118	   154	following `resolve.nodes[].deps` and skipping deps whose `dep_kinds` are all `dev`.

 11121	   157	
 11122	   158	```text
 11123	   159	DEBT A5-DD1  Disposition: DEFER
 11124	   160	  Finding:          verter_semantic (and verter_diagnostics) depend on verter_workspace, so the
 11125	   161	                    semantic kernel's production closure reaches verter_scheduler (unconditional)
 11126	   162	                    and verter_tsgo_api (native only — declared under
 11127	   163	                    cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32")) in verter_workspace/Cargo.toml),
 11128	   164	                    contradicting ADR-015's reusability consequence
 11129	   165	  Durable owner:    C1 (converge ModuleResolverCore / non-flow TypeInfoCore — the block that
 11130	   166	                    decides what the kernel's input surface is), with B1 owning the test that
 11131	   167	                    makes the violation fail rather than be reviewed for
 11132	   168	  Resolution gate:  C1 accepted candidate. B1 MAY land its test with this pair as a recorded,
 11133	   169	                    equality-pinned exception; it MUST NOT land it as a subset-checked allowance,
 11134	   170	                    and the exception must name C1 as its removal gate.
 11135	   171	  Acceptance:       verter_semantic's closure contains neither verter_scheduler nor

 11137	   173	                    B1's equality-pinned exception must therefore record the target condition

 11142	   178	The `B1`-may-land-with-exception clause matters: without it, `B1` either cannot land its own exit
 11143	   179	criterion or is tempted to weaken the test to green. The equality pin plus a named removal gate is
 11144	   180	what keeps a temporary exception from becoming permanent.

 11146	   182	## 5. What the strategy deliberately does not cover
 11147	   183	
 11148	   184	- **Intra-crate direction.** The closure walk sees crates. `verter_session` is 5 of the 6 layers
 11149	   185	  by volume, and the module-level direction inside it is not testable this way. ADR-015 is
 11150	   186	  explicit that "logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until
 11151	   187	  a real dependency firewall … exists" — so intra-crate direction is held by the type system
 11152	   188	  (privacy, sealed traits, the `NoTypeExpr` marker) and by review, not by this test. `K3` is the
 11153	   189	  block that turns the module boundaries that matter into crate boundaries.
 11154	   190	- **Trait-object back-edges.** A closure walk cannot see a callback that inverts control without
 11155	   191	  inverting the dependency. ADR-015 rejects "mutual compiler/semantic callbacks" for this reason;
 11156	   192	  detecting them is a review mandate, not a graph query.

 12335	     1	# C1 — Converge `ModuleResolverCore` and non-flow `TypeInfoCore`
 12336	     2	
 12337	     3	**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** Foundational
 12338	     4	(`program-dag.toml:162`). **Predecessors:** `A6`, `B1`, `B2` (`program-dag.toml:163`).
 12339	     5	
 12340	     6	C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
 12341	     7	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and the TypeScript-style resolver living in
 12342	     8	`verter_workspace::resolver` — into the two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a
 12343	     9	`ModuleResolverCore` that owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow
 12344	    10	`TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution,
 12345	    11	relation/inference, effective typing, recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and
 12346	    12	exactness/completeness propagation. Neither target type exists in code today; both names describe roles
 12347	    13	the current tree already plays under different names and in the wrong crate. C1 does not invent new
 12348	    14	resolution semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be
 12349	    15	identical to today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code, how many
 12350	    16	duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform I/O
 12351	    17	directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
 12352	    18	
 12353	    19	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
 12354	    20	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
 12355	    21	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
 12356	    22	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions. It owns
 12357	    23	convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, and the addition of a batched,
 12358	    24	resumable load-outcome so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume the same kernel a blocking lifecycle
 12359	    25	consumes today.
 12360	    26	
 12361	    27	## Intent Contract
 12362	    28	
 12363	    29	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
 12364	    30	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
 12365	    31	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
 12366	    32	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
 12367	    33	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation) and by omission (no lifecycle exists
 12368	    34	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), not by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits
 12369	    35	a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
 12370	    36	
 12371	    37	**Required observable outcomes.**
 12372	    38	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
 12373	    39	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
 12374	    40	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
 12375	    41	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
 12376	    42	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
 12377	    43	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
 12378	    44	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer.
 12379	    45	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_scheduler` nor
 12380	    46	  `verter_tsgo_api` on any target (closes debt row A5-DD1, `evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:158-176`).
 12381	    47	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (`resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:161`) has exactly as many
 12382	    48	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct lifecycles; a lifecycle that cannot
 12383	    49	  resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
 12384	    50	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
 12385	    51	
 12386	    52	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
 12387	    53	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
 12388	    54	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
 12389	    55	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832` — C1 preserves this unchanged).
 12390	    56	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
 12391	    57	  observation views").
 12392	    58	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
 12393	    59	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext` implementor served it, for
 12394	    60	  identical inputs.
 12395	    61	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
 12396	    62	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
 12397	    63	
 12398	    64	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
 12399	    65	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
 12400	    66	point). `ResolverContext` implementors are lifecycle *adapters* over that one authority, never alternate
 12401	    67	authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed
 12402	    68	non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s `CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split,
 12403	    69	`.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) — C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken
 12404	    70	it while adding the `NeedInputs` outcome alongside it.

 12461	   127	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract
 12462	   128	
 12463	   129	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
 12464	   130	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
 12465	   131	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
 12466	   132	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
 12467	   133	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
 12468	   134	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet"
 12469	   135	crates/` — zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
 12470	   136	
 12471	   137	**C1 does not own** the outer staged transaction. `contracts/input-loading.md` §5: "A direct/project
 12472	   138	`CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns
 12473	   139	`NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry." That caller — the
 12474	   140	prepare/plan/project/emit loop, `CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, and the
 12475	   141	load/commit/retry orchestration across *multiple* kernel attempts — is `C2` (`program.md:242-247`, ADR-011).
 12476	   142	C1's obligation ends at: one resolver-tier operation, one immutable snapshot, one typed outcome. C2's
 12477	   143	obligation starts at: drive repeated C1 attempts, own the snapshot-extend/retry loop, own the anti-replay
 12478	   144	tokens.
 12479	   145	
 12480	   146	The existing blocking behavior is **not deleted**: the host-backed LSP session and the session-overlay
 12481	   147	lifecycle are permitted, documented lifecycles that legitimately block a cooperating thread
 12482	   148	(`decl_body_memo.rs:21`, `store_view_manager_tests.rs:2399` — "in-flight work block cooperatively, never
 12483	   149	busy-spin"). C1 adds the alternative outcome so a *new* I/O-free lifecycle can reuse the same resolution
 12484	   150	logic without being forced to block; it does not retrofit every existing call site to stop blocking.
 12485	   151

 12521	   187	## Structural confinement
 12522	   188	
 12523	   189	Every invariant above is enforced structurally, matching the pattern the codebase already uses in this
 12524	   190	exact area — C1 extends that pattern, it does not invent scanner-based enforcement:
 12525	   191	
 12526	   192	- **Sealed-trait lifecycle closure.** `ResolverContext: sealed::Sealed` (`resolver_context.rs:82-98,161`)
 12527	   193	  already makes "some fourth, unregistered lifecycle adapter" a compile error. C1 preserves the seal and,
 12528	   194	  if the bare-host rail is deleted (see above), tightens `RequestBoundResolverContext`
 12529	   195	  (`resolver_context.rs:780-815`, `static_assertions::assert_obj_safe!`) from "narrower than
 12530	   196	  `ResolverContext`" to "identical to it" — a resolver-tier function taking `&dyn ResolverContext` becomes
 12531	   197	  provably request-bound by construction, not by convention.
 12532	   198	- **`StoreView`/`HostStoreView` immutability is already structural**, not a convention: `HostStoreView`
 12533	   199	  (`resolver_store.rs:1462-1525`) has no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<..>>` field, only `Arc`-shared by-value
 12534	   200	  snapshot data; a future violation (a live host reference smuggled into the struct) is a visible field
 12535	   201	  addition a reviewer catches at the type definition, not a runtime behavior to detect.
 12536	   202	- **The Authority-uniqueness contract** (`.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:826-832`: no second
 12537	   203	  `SemanticQueryApi` impl, no second `execute_relate`, no second `shallow_lower_type_expr`, no second
 12538	   204	  `RelationMemo` owner, no second semantic-node-map owner) is enforced today partly by a `syn`-AST content
 12539	   205	  scanner (`crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs:3384` `mod resolver_context_seal`,
 12540	   206	  reached from `no_concrete_verter_host_in_seal_scope` at `:3703-3712`) and partly by grandfathered
 12541	   207	  string-content assertions (e.g. `resolver_store_view_returns_store_view_read` at `:16454-16469`). Per
 12542	   208	  `CLAUDE.md`'s forward-only landed-scanner rule, these are **grandfathered, not a template**: C1 must not
 12543	   209	  add a new name-keyed source scanner for any *new* invariant it introduces (the deleted bare-host rail,
 12544	   210	  the collapsed duplication, the new `AttemptOutcome`). New confinement is type-level: privacy, the
 12545	   211	  existing seal, a marker type for "I/O-free context" analogous to `RequestBoundResolverContext`, or a
 12546	   212	  `NoTypeExpr`-style content-free marker if `AttemptOutcome<T>` needs one. C1 may *extend* the existing
 12547	   213	  grandfathered scanners' checked assertions if a change under review genuinely regresses what they
 12548	   214	  already check; it may not add a new standalone scanner test.
 12549	   215	- **`NeedInputs` non-blocking guarantee.** The cleanest structural proof available is a marker type on the
 12550	   216	  I/O-free context (e.g. an `IoFreeResolverContext` sealed subtrait, mirroring
 12551	   217	  `RequestBoundResolverContext`'s shape) that is never implemented for any type holding a `&VerterHost`
 12552	   218	  capable of reaching the scheduler — so a resolver-tier function generic over that marker cannot call
 12553	   219	  `ensure_loaded` even if someone tries, because the trait bound does not expose it. This is a design
 12554	   220	  recommendation, not a locked mechanism; see Open Questions.

 12556	   222	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
 12557	   223	
 12558	   224	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
 12559	   225	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
 12560	   226	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
 12561	   227	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
 12562	   228	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
 12563	   229	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges remains the single authority `D1`
 12564	   230	integrates against behind its private non-production test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later
 12565	   231	extends without needing a second relation/name authority (`program.md:253`: "No flow-private relation/name
 12566	   232	authority may exist after `D2`"). If convergence work touches `project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`,
 12567	   233	`relation_txn.rs`, or the `RelationMemo` at all, it is confined to lifecycle/context plumbing around the
 12568	   234	call, never the relation algorithm itself.
 12569	   235	
 12570	   236	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
 12571	   237	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
 12572	   238	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
 12573	   239	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
 12574	   240	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is: a `ResolverContext`-shaped kernel
 12575	   241	(or its post-extraction equivalent) that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be driven
 12576	   242	from an I/O-free environment and returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking, and (c) can be constructed
 12577	   243	without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery, so C2's compiler-facing
 12578	   244	facade does not have to depend on the whole `verter_session` crate to embed it.
 12579	   245

 12612	   277	## Open questions requiring maintainer/architecture ruling
 12613	   278	
 12614	   279	These are gaps this research could not close from the code and evidence tree alone. Do not dispatch
 12615	   280	implementation against them without a ruling — each is a real design fork, not a detail:
 12616	   281	
 12617	   282	1. **Crate placement.** `resolver_core`/`resolver_store` are today private modules inside `verter_session`
 12618	   283	   with no crate boundary between them (confirmed: `lib.rs:341-344`, plain `use crate::resolver_store::…`
 12619	   284	   intra-crate references throughout). `architecture.md` §18.1 places "semantic kernel/module
 12620	   285	   resolver/relation/flow" *below* "compiler" and far below "managed engine/session" in the inward
 12621	   286	   dependency chain, which today's placement inverts. Whether C1 must physically extract the converged
 12622	   287	   kernel into a new crate (and if so, its name, its exact member boundary, and whether extraction happens
 12623	   288	   inside C1 or is staged into a follow-up block C1 merely proves is possible) is the single largest open
 12624	   289	   design question in this charter. I did not find an existing target crate name or extraction plan in
 12625	   290	   `architecture.md`, the ADRs, or `program-dag.toml` — this needs an explicit pre-implementation
 12626	   291	   architecture challenge (governance.md's Foundational-class requirement), not a decision made inside
 12627	   292	   the charter.
 12628	   293	2. **A5-DD1's harder half.** `verter_semantic/src/analysis/routes.rs`'s `&dyn verter_workspace::WorkspaceRead`
 12629	   294	   parameter (6 call sites) is a genuine functional dependency, not a re-export. Closing the
 12630	   295	   `verter_semantic → verter_workspace` edge requires either relocating `WorkspaceRead` to a lower neutral
 12631	   296	   layer or moving route-extraction logic upward to where `WorkspaceRead` already lives — I could not
 12632	   297	   determine from the code which is correct without risking a guess that contradicts `F1`'s
 12633	   298	   not-yet-written committed-input-authority design. Flagged, not resolved, in Legacy Deletions above.
 12634	   299	3. **Whether `NeedInputs` needs a structural (marker-type) non-blocking guarantee or an accepted
 12635	   300	   review-enforced one.** I recommend a sealed `IoFreeResolverContext`-shaped marker (mirroring
 12636	   301	   `RequestBoundResolverContext`) so a resolver-tier function generic over it cannot reach
 12637	   302	   `ensure_loaded`/the scheduler even by accident, but this is materially more invasive than a
 12638	   303	   review-enforced convention and its cost/benefit was not evaluated against a real implementation attempt.
 12639	   304	   This should be settled at the same pre-implementation architecture challenge as (1), since the answer
 12640	   305	   likely depends on it (a marker type is far cheaper to add correctly if the extraction in (1) happens
 12641	   306	   first, because the I/O-free context would then live outside `verter_session` entirely and could not
 12642	   307	   physically hold a `&VerterHost`).
 12643	   308	4. **Scope of "AttemptOutcome" coverage.** `program.md:196` says "return batched `NeedInputs`" without
 12644	   309	   qualifying which resolver-tier operations. This charter scopes it to the load points already reached
 12645	   310	   through `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` (the only synchronous-blocking-on-I/O sites this
 12646	   311	   research found). Whether C2 needs *every* resolver-core query to support the outcome on day one, or
 12647	   312	   whether a narrower first cut (module/import resolution only, deferring full type-query coverage) is
 12648	   313	   acceptable, is a scope call for whoever authors C1's pre-implementation brief — I have not sized the
 12649	   314	   full-coverage option against the fan-out of `resolver_core`'s ~37 files.

 13209	     1	# Snapshot-Consistent Batched Input Loading Contract
 13210	     2	
 13211	     3	**Status:** Normative outer-orchestration contract.
 13212	     4	
 13213	     5	# 1. Kernel rule
 13214	     6	
 13215	     7	The compiler, resolver, TypeInfo, flow, and reusable query kernels consume one immutable observation view per attempt and perform no hidden filesystem/network/process/package-manager I/O.
 13216	     8	
 13217	     9	# 2. Outcome
 13218	    10	
 13219	    11	```rust
 13220	    12	enum AttemptOutcome<T> {
 13221	    13	    Complete(T),
 13222	    14	    NeedInputs(LoadSet),
 13223	    15	    Terminal(AttemptFailure),
 13224	    16	}
 13225	    17	```
 13226	    18	
 13227	    19	`LoadSet` is normalized, sorted, deduplicated, and includes the resolution basis needed to load/commit safely. The kernel discovers all independently reachable missing observations it can identify without fabricating semantic answers.
 13228	    20	
 13229	    21	# 3. Orchestration state
 13230	    22	
 13231	    23	```text
 13232	    24	attempt number
 13233	    25	current snapshot identity
 13234	    26	accumulated requested InputKeys
 13235	    27	accumulated stable positive/negative observations
 13236	    28	unique input count
 13237	    29	loaded byte count
 13238	    30	dependency depth/frontier
 13239	    31	basis-change/churn count
 13240	    32	```
 13241	    33	
 13242	    34	# 4. Algorithm
 13243	    35	
 13244	    36	1. Run the whole operation against snapshot `S`.
 13245	    37	2. On `Complete`, validate observed facts against `S` and return/admit according to the query contract.
 13246	    38	3. On `Terminal`, return typed failure and never admit complete state.
 13247	    39	4. On `NeedInputs(L)`, normalize `L` and calculate `delta = L.keys - accumulated_requested`.
 13248	    40	5. If `delta` is empty and neither the resolution basis nor any previously observed fact changed, return `InputResolutionNoProgress` with the unresolved set.
 13249	    41	6. Check configured limits before I/O: attempts, unique keys, bytes, dependency depth, and basis-change/churn count.
 13250	    42	7. Load `delta` through embedding-owned same-key I/O flights. Each result is `Present`, stable `Missing`, or transient `LoadFailure`, with typed metadata and basis. Public/external loader digests are hints: the committing authority verifies key/basis consistency and computes or verifies content/configuration fingerprints from captured data before publication.
 13251	    43	8. Conditionally publish all validated commit-eligible observations as one coherent input batch only if the project/configuration basis remains compatible.
 13252	    44	9. If conditional commit loses a race or the basis changed, capture the new coherent snapshot, increment churn budget, and restart. Do not splice data into the old attempt.
 13253	    45	10. If committed, capture the new snapshot and restart from step 1.
 13254	    46	
 13255	    47	# 5. Direct project mode
 13256	    48	
 13257	    49	A direct/project `CompileTypeInfo` over an immutable caller environment does not own commits or I/O. It returns `NeedInputs`; the caller may rebuild/extend the environment and retry. The same no-progress/resource rules apply to convenience orchestration APIs.
 13258	    50	
 13259	    51	# 6. Observation trust boundary
 13260	    52	
 13261	    53	- public environments/loaders cannot mint authoritative `ContentId`, `InputBasisId`, semantic read facts, or completeness evidence;
 13262	    54	- source bytes, declared language/source type, canonical source identity, package/config metadata, lengths, and supplied digests are consistency-checked at capture/commit;
 13263	    55	- the authoritative owner hashes/normalizes once per committed revision and reuses the typed IDs thereafter;
 13264	    56	- a sealed first-party `EngineSnapshot` may carry prevalidated IDs because the same authority minted them;
 13265	    57	- mismatched key/bytes/profile/basis is a typed integrity failure and is never cached as stable missing or complete.
 13266	    58	
 13267	    59	# 7. Negative facts
 13268	    60	
 13269	    61	A stable missing module/package/file may be observed and cached only with the complete resolution basis: parent/package boundaries, conditions, path/case/symlink/workspace policy, and relevant configuration. Transient permission/network/process/provider failure is not a stable negative semantic fact.
 13270	    62	
 13271	    63	# 8. Resource failures
 13272	    64	
 13273	    65	Distinct failures include:
 13274	    66	
 13275	    67	```text
 13276	    68	InputResolutionNoProgress
 13277	    69	InputResolutionAttemptLimit
 13278	    70	InputResolutionUniqueKeyLimit
 13279	    71	InputResolutionByteLimit
 13280	    72	InputResolutionDepthLimit
 13281	    73	InputResolutionChurnLimit
 13282	    74	InputLoadUnavailable
 13283	    75	InputCommitConflictExceeded
 13284	    76	```
 13285	    77	
 13286	    78	They carry unresolved keys and consumed budget without exposing sensitive ambient paths beyond the product's diagnostic policy.
 13287	    79	
 13288	    80	# 9. Tests
 13289	    81	
 13290	    82	- multiple missing siblings loaded in one batch;
 13291	    83	- transitive dependency waves;
 13292	    84	- stable missing negative fact;
 13293	    85	- dependency appears between attempts;
 13294	    86	- project/config changes during load;
 13295	    87	- repeated same `LoadSet` no progress;
 13296	    88	- loader partial/transient failure;
 13297	    89	- unique key/byte/depth/retry/churn limits;
 13298	    90	- external observation digest/key mismatch rejected before commit;
 13299	    91	- no semantic kernel I/O instrumentation;
 13300	    92	- final result equals an equivalent fully preloaded clean run.
 13301	     1	# Staged Compile Transaction and Anti-Replay Contract
 13302	     2	
 13303	     3	**Status:** Normative direct/prepared/project-aware compiler protocol.
 13304	     4	
 13305	     5	# 1. Stages
 13306	     6	
 13307	     7	```text
 13308	     8	prepare(source, parse options)
 13309	     9	  -> PreparedCarrier
 13310	    10	plan(prepared, CompileRequest)
 13311	    11	  -> CompilePlan
 13312	    12	project(plan.projection_batch, CompileTypeInfo)
 13313	    13	  -> CompleteFacts | NeedInputs(LoadSet) | TerminalFailure
 13314	    14	emit(prepared, plan, complete facts)
 13315	    15	  -> CompileResult
 13316	    16	```
 13317	    17	
 13318	    18	Planning discovers the complete product prerequisite closure and closed semantic projection batch before projection. Emission does not discover new project-semantic demands. A new demand requires a new plan.
 13319	    19	
 13320	    20	# 2. Binding tokens
 13321	    21	
 13322	    22	`CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay. The plan additionally owns narrower deterministic tokens:
 13323	    23	
 13324	    24	```text
 13325	    25	ProjectionPlanToken   root + semantic profile + closed demand batch + kernel/projection domains
 13326	    26	ProductSubplanToken   root + framework/product + output profile + required product mapping contract
 13327	    27	TerminalSubplanToken  exact typed result/product + requested presentation/provenance/encoding profile
 13328	    28	```
 13329	    29	
 13330	    30	The whole `CompilePlanToken` binds at least:
 13331	    31	
 13332	    32	- prepared root/source/unit identities;
 13333	    33	- parse key/domain and relevant generation;
 13334	    34	- normalized canonical typed product-request collection;
 13335	    35	- shared semantic profile when observed;
 13336	    36	- each product's output and requested terminal presentation/mapping/provenance/serialization profiles;
 13337	    37	- framework/compiler compatibility identity;
 13338	    38	- projection schema/domain;
 13339	    39	- plan algorithm compatibility domain;
 13340	    40	- deterministic demand ordering and digest.
 13341	    41	
 13342	    42	The plan contains independently keyed subplans/artifact identities. A presentation-, map-encoding-, provenance-, or serialization-only change may create a new terminal subplan without invalidating an unchanged semantic projection or code-generation subplan. `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete request for anti-replay; it does not force every subartifact to use that whole token as its cache key.
 13343	    43	
 13344	    44	`CompileFactsBatch` binds:
 13345	    45	
 13346	    46	- exact `ProjectionPlanToken` and demand digest referenced by the containing plan;
 13347	    47	- semantic profile and kernel compatibility domain;
 13348	    48	- input basis and observed dependency fingerprints;
 13349	    49	- one typed result for every demand;
 13350	    50	- exactness/completeness/degradation;
 13351	    51	- integrity and size limits when decoded or transferred.
 13352	    52	
 13353	    53	Emission first validates the whole `CompilePlanToken`, then validates that the facts satisfy the exact `ProjectionPlanToken` referenced by that plan. It rejects missing, extra, duplicated, reordered without canonical identity, stale, wrong-profile, wrong-projection-plan, wrong-root, wrong-domain, or insufficient facts before output construction.
 13354	    54	
 13355	    55	# 3. Zero-demand behavior
 13356	    56	
 13357	    57	When the plan has no semantic projection demands:
 13358	    58	
 13359	    59	- no `CompileTypeInfo` session is constructed;
 13360	    60	- no module resolver or TypeInfo index/graph/flow work runs;
 13361	    61	- projection stage is represented as an empty complete batch bound to the plan;
 13362	    62	- Svelte current runtime compilation must prove zero Vue/native projection demand unless its capability contract changes.
 13363	    63	
 13364	    64	# 4. `NeedInputs`
 13365	    65	
 13366	    66	`NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a resumable orchestration outcome. It does not mutate the current plan or prepared value with unversioned ambient data. The outer orchestrator loads and publishes/rebuilds a coherent input view according to `input-loading.md`, then reruns projection with the same plan only when the plan’s source/request/profile basis remains valid. Otherwise it replans.
 13367	    67	
 13368	    68	# 5. Direct and managed modes
 13369	    69	
 13370	    70	- local direct mode may project from the retained root only;
 13371	    71	- direct project mode consumes an immutable caller-provided observation view and returns `NeedInputs` to the caller;
 13372	    72	- managed mode consumes one `EngineSnapshot`/`InputBasisId` per attempt and uses the outer commit/retry loop;
 13373	    73	- all modes execute one semantic kernel and the same closed framework projector;
 13374	    74	- lifecycle, retention, and orchestration differ; semantics do not.
 13375	    75	
 13376	    76	# 6. Error taxonomy
 13377	    77	
 13378	    78	Distinct failures include parse/preparation failure, unsupported product combination, unavailable semantic capability, `NeedInputs`, no progress, projection gap, unresolved dependency, stale plan/facts, profile/domain mismatch, size/integrity failure, cancellation, budget exhaustion, and internal failure.
 13379	    79	
 13380	    80	# 7. Required tests
 13381	    81	
 13382	    82	- plan once and emit multiple requested products without rediscovery;
 13383	    83	- simultaneous product combinations equal separately requested products where contracts declare composability;
 13384	    84	- different per-product output profiles coexist without a global-profile collision;
 13385	    85	- presentation/serialization-only changes reuse unchanged semantic and code subplans;
 13386	    86	- irrelevant product/profile fields are rejected or normalized away before identity construction;
 13387	    87	- zero-demand zero-initialization;
 13388	    88	- local and imported projection batches;
 13389	    89	- batched shared-root deduplication;
 13390	    90	- stale/wrong-whole-plan/wrong-projection-plan/wrong-profile/extra/missing facts rejected;
 13391	    91	- facts from a terminal-only sibling plan are accepted only when their `ProjectionPlanToken` is exactly equal;
 13392	    92	- `NeedInputs` waves and no-progress behavior;
 13393	    93	- basis change forces retry/replan as appropriate;
 13394	    94	- direct/prepared/managed output equality for equal product/profile/input contracts;
 13395	    95	- cancelled/superseded attempts do not terminally materialize output.

 13417	     1	# ADR-003 — Compile Semantics Use a Concrete Sealed Facade
 13418	     2	
 13419	     3	**Status:** Accepted
 13420	     4	
 13421	     5	## Context
 13422	     6	
 13423	     7	The compiler needs optional project-aware semantic projections. An open trait would permit alternate module/type/runtime-classification semantics and create a second engine.
 13424	     8	
 13425	     9	## Decision
 13426	    10	
 13427	    11	The compiler accepts only a concrete Verter-owned `CompileTypeInfo<'_>` facade. Lifecycle variants are private/sealed first-party constructions. External integrations may supply captured observations through a data-only environment; they cannot implement semantic behavior.
 13428	    12	
 13429	    13	All construction modes execute one profile-parameterized semantic kernel and one module resolver. The facade has no blanket `Send + Sync`; ownership/concurrency is a lifecycle policy.
 13430	    14	
 13431	    15	## Consequences
 13432	    16	
 13433	    17	Direct local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed modes remain possible without opening semantics or coupling the compiler to `Engine`.
 13434	    18	
 13435	    19	## Rejected alternatives
 13436	    20	
 13437	    21	- public semantic trait object;
 13438	    22	- compiler receives host/Engine/provider state;
 13439	    23	- framework/compiler-local resolver fallback.
 13440	     1	# ADR-011 — Project-Aware Compile Uses a Resumable I/O-Free Transaction
 13441	     2	
 13442	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13443	     4	**Decision owner:** direct compiler/project TypeInfo integration  
 13444	     5	**Reopen only if:** a future compiler mode explicitly embeds I/O and accepts a separate architecture boundary.
 13445	     6	
 13446	     7	## Context
 13447	     8	
 13448	     9	A compile API that may need project inputs cannot safely hide I/O or retain OXC borrows across asynchronous loading. Projection facts must be proven to belong to the exact plan that consumes them.
 13449	    10	
 13450	    11	## Decision
 13451	    12	
 13452	    13	Project-aware compile follows:
 13453	    14	
 13454	    15	```text
 13455	    16	prepare -> plan -> project -> emit
 13456	    17	```
 13457	    18	
 13458	    19	- prepared syntax remains owned/borrowed by one retained owner;
 13459	    20	- the projection batch is compact, owned, and OXC-free;
 13460	    21	- `CompilePlanToken` binds the complete normalized request to the prepared root; the plan contains narrower deterministic projection/product/terminal subplan tokens;
 13461	    22	- `CompileFactsBatch` binds to the exact `ProjectionPlanToken`, semantic profile, dependency/input basis, projection schema, and demand digest, so terminal-only sibling plans may reuse facts only when that projection token is exactly equal;
 13462	    23	- `NeedInputs(LoadSet)` is a first-class resumable outcome;
 13463	    24	- external loading occurs outside compiler/semantic compute;
 13464	    25	- no syntax borrow or unvalidated locator crosses the loading boundary;
 13465	    26	- each attempt reports the maximal sound missing observation set discovered;
 13466	    27	- retries use a monotonic progress ledger, bounded waves/resources, and deterministic no-progress failure;
 13467	    28	- stale or replayed facts are rejected before emission.
 13468	    29	
 13469	    30	## Consequences
 13470	    31	
 13471	    32	The same semantic kernel supports local, captured-project, in-memory, and managed-snapshot modes without hidden filesystem authority.
 13472	    33	
 13473	    34	## Rejected alternatives
 13474	    35	
 13475	    36	- **Synchronous hidden filesystem callbacks:** break hermeticity and coherent snapshots.
 13476	    37	- **Reparse/replan implicitly after every missing input:** can amplify work and consume mismatched facts.
 13477	     1	# ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free
 13478	     2	
 13479	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13480	     4	**Decision owner:** crate/module ownership  
 13481	     5	**Reopen only if:** a new stable boundary cannot be represented without a cycle and an alternative decomposition has been disproven.
 13482	     6	
 13483	     7	## Context
 13484	     8	
 13485	     9	Where `CompileTypeInfo`, framework projection DTOs, and request contracts live can accidentally create compiler↔semantic or compiler↔session cycles, forcing traits, erasure, and shared ownership.
 13486	    10	
 13487	    11	## Decision
 13488	    12	
 13489	    13	Binding direction is:
 13490	    14	
 13491	    15	```text
 13492	    16	identity/span/language/contracts
 13493	    17	-> shared syntax frontends and dependency-neutral DTOs
 13494	    18	-> semantic kernel/module resolver/relation/flow
 13495	    19	-> compiler
 13496	    20	-> managed engine/session
 13497	    21	-> LSP/provider/MCP/NAPI/WASM/CLI adapters
 13498	    22	```
 13499	    23	
 13500	    24	Rules:
 13501	    25	
 13502	    26	- syntax/contracts do not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
 13503	    27	- semantic kernel does not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
 13504	    28	- compiler may depend on syntax, sealed semantic facade, and neutral closed DTOs;
 13505	    29	- managed engine depends on compiler/semantic, never the reverse;
 13506	    30	- provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel;
 13507	    31	- adapters depend inward only;
 13508	    32	- durable build tests reject crate dependency cycles and forbidden edges.
 13509	    33	
 13510	    34	Logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until a real dependency firewall or multi-consumer stable contract exists.
 13511	    35	
 13512	    36	## Consequences
 13513	    37	
 13514	    38	- direct compiler cannot become a session mode;
 13515	    39	- semantic kernel remains reusable across lifecycles;
 13516	    40	- fewer traits, erased bags, and `Arc` workarounds are required.
 13517	    41	
 13518	    42	## Rejected alternatives
 13519	    43	
 13520	    44	- **Mutual compiler/semantic callbacks:** creates cycles and alternate behavior.
 13521	    45	- **Everything in session/host crate:** preserves catch-all ownership.
 13522	     1	# ADR-001 — One Semantic Authority, Justified Derived Projections
 13523	     2	
 13524	     3	**Status:** Accepted  
 13525	     4	**Decision owner:** TypeInfo/effective-flow architecture
 13526	     5	
 13527	     6	## Context
 13528	     7	
 13529	     8	`FunctionFlowGraph` must be the one structural flow authority, but efficient solving may need dominators, loop forests, SCCs, def-use overlays, capture summaries, reverse adjacency, or compact execution schedules. Forbidding every graph-derived structure would either bloat the canonical graph or repeat topology work. Allowing independent query-specific CFGs recreates the current dual-authority defect.
 13530	     9	
 13531	    10	## Decision
 13532	    11	
 13533	    12	`FunctionFlowGraph` is the canonical structural authority. A derived structure is allowed only when it:
 13534	    13	
 13535	    14	- is keyed by one exact graph/body identity and any interpretation-affecting semantic profile;
 13536	    15	- is deterministic and fully reproducible from the graph and accepted kernel rules;
 13537	    16	- cannot add facts, define transfer/join semantics, mark coverage complete, or publish a semantic result;
 13538	    17	- is request-local by default and independently weighted/evicted if retention is proven valuable;
 13539	    18	- can be replaced without changing observable semantics.
 13540	    19	
 13541	    20	## Consequences
 13542	    21	
 13543	    22	The solver may use efficient layouts without creating a second semantic or control authority. Review checks authority and construction rights, not superficial data-structure count.
 13544	    23	
 13545	    24	## Rejected alternatives
 13546	    25	
 13547	    26	- exactly one physical graph-like object;
 13548	    27	- independent syntax-shaped/query-specific CFGs;
 13549	    28	- projections that own relation, completion, capture, or coverage decisions.

 13757	   475	### Verification Must Prove Execution (MANDATORY)
 13758	   476	
 13759	   477	A required gate passes only on fresh, input-bound evidence that: every applicable required job was eligible and ran; the intended tree-derived surface was owned and independently discovered; selectors matched non-zero work; required source, build, and fixture prerequisites matched the tested tree; executed work was non-zero; unexpected prerequisite skips were zero; child deadlines were strictly below their parent killer; and a terminal summary completed. **Exit status 0 alone, a self-declared test universe, or a missing required-job result is FAIL.** Every tracked test or guard has exactly one declared primary gate; a hand-maintained filename list may not define the primary universe unless generated from independent discovery and parity-checked.
 13760	   478	
 13761	   479	Attestation alone is insufficient — a receipt faithfully attests whatever incomplete universe the runner defines for itself. The durable design needs all three: fresh execution attestation; independently tree-derived inventory/discovery parity; and per-surface negative-control mutation through the exact canonical entry point. A single global canary cannot detect an omitted unrelated spec.
 13762	   480	
 13763	   481	**The negative control must itself be proven to have applied.** A plant that fails to apply reports a pass: `perl`/`sed`/`grep` exit 0 on a non-match, so a mutation's exit code is never proof it landed, and a verification search hitting a PRE-EXISTING occurrence of the planted string is a false positive. Prove the mutation is present, unique, and new in the source before trusting the run; a green planted run means the plant failed until proven otherwise. A discrimination check that cannot distinguish "the plant did not apply" from "the code is correct" is not a discrimination check.
 13764	   482	
 13765	   483	Planned guard: `gate_contract_integrity` — one registered suite exercising the canonical entry point against independent inventory plus per-surface negative controls covering missing summary, disabled or missing job, invalid timeout nesting, zero selection, stale or missing build, missing fixture or unexpected skip, omitted or unowned test, and a mutation that silently fails to apply. Until that guard, its attesting driver, and the required-job aggregator land, this rule is held only by §1a and confirm judgment.

So the gap is named rather than hidden — the deferral, its owner (the gate-integrity block), its resolution gate (that block's landing), and the live in-tree instances are recorded in [`docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md`](docs/arch/gate-integrity-ledger.md).  13779	528:**Intent before mechanism.** Before mechanism design for a block that changes observable behavior, authority, or fallback, record a ratified intent contract: the actor/problem and why the capability should exist; required and forbidden observable outcomes; authority/fallback order; a planned test or gate for each stable acceptance ID; and material cold, warm, allocation, fan-out, and latency bounds. An internal substrate block may reference its parent contract but must state the invariant and performance contribution it owns. Ratification comes from the approved plan or product authority; no implementation brief is dispatched without it. Enforcement is judgment — exercised at decomposition and again immediately before implementation dispatch.

 13781	534:**One-pass execution applies only while the approved design remains valid.** The second-REOPEN circuit breaker lapses approval for the affected design: pause implementation, obtain and record the required architecture/product ruling, and resume only once the design is ratified again. This is not a checkpoint — one-pass governs *executing an approved design*, and the breaker fires when *approval itself has lapsed*, which is a different event and precisely why execution must stop rather than grind on. STOP, failed verification, rule conflict, and verified plan-invalidating discoveries pause at their prescribed evidence gate without creating a discretionary user checkpoint. Breadth, breakage, effort, or migration size never lapses approval; approved scope changes only through the recorded ruling or explicit user re-scope. See `/mom-cto-orchestration` → Decision Admission.

 14363	All four proposed positions fail. Forks 1 and 3 are one coupled decision.
 14364	
 14365	First, the draft is factually wrong that both modules are private: `resolver_core` is `pub mod`; only `resolver_store` is private (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:341-342`). That does not rescue in-place convergence.
 14366	
 14367	### Fork 1 — VIOLATES
 14368	
 14369	Invariant: inward, cycle-free dependency direction; compiler may depend on the semantic kernel, never on session (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/architecture.md:1110-1130`, `decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:24-34`).
 14370	
 14371	A `pub(crate)` session facade is unusable by C2. Making it public would require `verter_compiler -> verter_session`, while session already depends on compiler (`crates/verter_session/Cargo.toml:117`), creating a cycle. Compiler already depends on the ratified layer-3 kernel crate, `verter_semantic` (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`; `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs:44-47`).
 14372	
 14373	“Prove extractability without extracting” is not mechanically enforceable inside this crate. The existing structural graph guard explicitly cannot see intra-crate direction (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:182-189`). A facade controls exposure, not what its implementation imports. The current context directly names scheduler state and `VerterHost` (`resolver_context.rs:183-196,700-717`).
 14374	
 14375	Ruling: **EXTRACT-NOW into existing crate `verter_semantic`**, not a new `verter_typeinfo` crate. Exact boundary:
 14376	
 14377	- `verter_semantic`: `ModuleResolverCore`, non-flow `TypeInfoCore`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, relation/node algorithms, dependency-neutral semantic store/value types, immutable observation contracts, and `AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`.
 14378	- `verter_workspace`/`verter_session`: observation capture, committed-store implementations, `VerterHost`, scheduler, I/O flights, cache-retention policy, and outer retry/commit orchestration.
 14379	- `verter_compiler`: C2’s concrete `CompileTypeInfo`, plans, facts, and anti-replay tokens.
 14380	
 14381	The kernel closure must contain only layers 1–3 and exclude compiler/workspace/session/scheduler/provider. The existing Cargo-metadata closure guard is the landed structural enforcement (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:1-18,316-350`).
 14382	
 14383	### Fork 2 — VIOLATES
 14384	
 14385	Invariant: environments provide immutable data observations, not resolution semantics or live I/O (`architecture.md:461,631,660-662`).

 12153	   132	
 12154	   133	Legal modes:
 12155	   134	
 12156	   135	- **Bottom-up:** land only the lowest `LANDABLE` layer. Then invalidate/restack every remaining upper layer on the actual accepted base and issue a successor snapshot. If one layer remains, continue as an ordinary single PR.

 12272	    43	## 3.2 `ATOMIC_REVIEW`
 12273	    44	
 12274	    45	Use when several review-sized diffs collectively form one indivisible clean cutover.
 12275	    46	
 12276	    47	Rules:
 12277	    48	
 12278	    49	- top-level `acceptance_block_id` names the sole program block that may become accepted/landed from this window;
 12279	    50	- all layers belong to that atomic acceptance unit and have unique `layer_id` values;
 12280	    51	- private layers may repeat the acceptance block's `block_id` as internal checkpoints, or name an explicit `foundational-private-checkpoint` predecessor such as `D1`;
 12281	    52	- intermediate layers target a private integration branch, remain draft, are marked `NON_MERGEABLE_PRIVATE_LAYER`, and are unreachable from production entry points;
 12282	    53	- no intermediate layer is released, merged to trunk, or recorded as an accepted program predecessor, except an explicit program checkpoint such as D1 whose `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT` state is valid only for the final acceptance block;
 12283	    54	- exactly one final mergeable layer routes every consumer, deletes the displaced path/support machinery, and becomes the reviewed candidate;
 12284	    55	- the complete combined tip receives the block's required conformance, architecture, and adversarial/performance review;
 12285	    56	- landing preserves the exact reviewed candidate delta on the recorded landing base.
 12286	    57	
 12287	    58	`D1`/`D2` is the canonical case: D1 is a private checkpoint; D2 is the sole acceptance and landing unit.
 12288	    59	
 12289	    60	## 3.3 Parallel disjoint work
 12290	    61	
 12291	    62	Parallelism is represented by separate `LANDABLE` or `ATOMIC_REVIEW` windows, not one artificial stack. Each window declares shared owners/files/generated artifacts and integration tests. A newly discovered ownership overlap stops or serializes the affected work.

 14378	- `verter_workspace`/`verter_session`: observation capture, committed-store implementations, `VerterHost`, scheduler, I/O flights, cache-retention policy, and outer retry/commit orchestration.

 14384	
 14385	Invariant: environments provide immutable data observations, not resolution semantics or live I/O (`architecture.md:461,631,660-662`).

Moving that interface downward would preserve live workspace authority inside the kernel and let environments continue implementing resolution semantics.

     1	# C1 architecture addendum — three execution gaps
     2	
     3	**Source:** bounded architecture challenge, read-only, run against `program/architecture-lock`
     4	at `8c2189389`. Commissioned by the maintainer when C1 was held before ratification, scoped to
     5	exactly three discovered execution gaps and forbidden from re-scoping C1 smaller.
     6	
     7	**Baseline preserved:** the C1 charter, its research, and all four prior architecture rulings
     8	(`ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS`) remain binding and were not reopened.
     9	
    10	**Amendment determination:** no accepted ADR, no DAG edge, and no program outcome changes under any
    11	of the three gap resolutions, so no AMD is required. The extraction into `verter_semantic` and full
    12	behavioural `AttemptOutcome` coverage both remain required.
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## GAP 1 — Cross-crate trait sealing
    17	
    18	Use the repository’s existing idiom exactly:
    19	
    20	```rust
    21	// verter_semantic/src/type_info/observations.rs
    22	mod sealed {
    23	    pub trait Sealed {}
    24	}
    25	
    26	pub trait ObservationRead: sealed::Sealed {
    27	    fn lookup(&self, key: &ObservationKey) -> ObservationValueRef<'_>;
    28	}
    29	
    30	impl sealed::Sealed for ObservationSnapshot {}
    31	impl ObservationRead for ObservationSnapshot { /* ... */ }
    32	```
    33	
    34	The private module is the sealing token. Only code inside `verter_semantic` can name `sealed::Sealed`; a foreign `impl ObservationRead for CompileTypeInfo` fails because `CompileTypeInfo: sealed::Sealed` cannot be satisfied, and attempting the marker impl fails with private-module error E0603. This is the same shape used by:
    35	
    36	- `ResolverContext`: private marker at `crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/resolver_context.rs:82`, supertrait at `:161`, sanctioned marker impls at `:745`.
    37	- Public cross-crate `AttachOwnership`: `crates/verter_tsgo_api/src/attach.rs:85`, `:98`, `:113`.
    38	- `NegativeEvidence`: `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/framework_facts/mod.rs:35`, `:45`; its sanctioned implementation is at `framework_facts/svelte.rs:178`.
    39	- The existing foreign-implementation compile failure: `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/compile-fail/deferred_callable_is_sealed_to_its_two_consumers.rs:21-38`.
    40	
    41	Therefore the legal implementors are semantic-owned types only: production `ObservationSnapshot`, and—if useful—a test-only type whose implementations are written inside `observations.rs`. `verter_compiler`, `verter_session`, integration tests, and external mocks consume an `ObservationSnapshot`; they do not implement the trait. They construct it through a semantic-owned builder from immutable data. No callbacks, closures, host references, or trait objects belong in the snapshot.
    42	
    43	`CompileTypeInfo` must compose an `ObservationSnapshot` and call the kernel. If it genuinely must implement the interface, the interface cannot remain sealed: Rust has no friend-crate exception. The same applies to external test doubles. An exhaustive external double and a private-supertrait seal are directly incompatible.
    44	
    45	This also falsifies C1-AC-4’s proposed relocated `ResolverContext`: `VerterHost` being local makes the foreign-trait impl orphan-legal, but it cannot implement the foreign trait’s private semantic supertrait (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:149`). Keep the lifecycle `ResolverContext`/`RequestBoundResolverContext` seal and its adapters in `verter_session`; extract their semantic operations behind the semantic-owned snapshot/gateway. This changes the charter’s file-level split at `C1.md:186`, not the kernel extraction or C1 outcome.
    46	
    47	Mechanical gates:
    48	
    49	- A compile-fail fixture in `verter_semantic/tests/compile-fail/` attempts both foreign marker and observation-interface impls.
    50	- `rg 'impl (sealed::Sealed|ObservationRead)' crates/verter_semantic/src/type_info` has only the sanctioned implementations.
    51	- Compiler/session tests use the public builder or semantic-owned test fixture, never a foreign `impl`.
