    96	## GAP 3 — Full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` proof
    97	
    98	The charter’s exhaustive-`impl` mechanism is invalid.
    99	
   100	- Adding a required method makes an existing impl incomplete, but adding a defaulted method does not. The repo demonstrates this directly: `ResolverContext::is_request_bound` has a default at `resolver_context.rs:179-181`, while the large `impl ResolverContext for VerterHost` beginning at `:817` omits it and compiles.
   101	- Even a required method proves only that the double supplies a body. A new method returning bare `T` can be added, implemented with bare `T`, and the exhaustive impl compiles. The impl does not constrain the trait author’s return type.
   102	- Generic methods, associated output types, and `async fn` do not improve this. They may make the trait non-dyn-compatible—the current code separately pins that at `resolver_context.rs:805-815`—but they do not force `AttemptOutcome`. An associated type can resolve to any type.
   103	- A Rust type alias to `AttemptOutcome<T>` is type-identical and therefore valid. It only defeats textual/name-based checking, not Rust type equality.
   104	- A foreign exhaustive double is forbidden by GAP 1’s seal. Only an in-module semantic test type can implement it, and it still suffers the default/return-shape defects above.
   105	- “Sole entry surface” is currently false: ProjectResolver uses `WorkspaceRead` directly (`resolver.rs:321-365`), component-meta reaches the host/scheduler (`component_meta/mod.rs:251-288`), and dispatch lowering calls host materialization (`lower.rs:403-418`).
   106	
   107	Replace the operation trait with one closed, non-overridable inherent gateway:
   108	
   109	```rust
   110	pub enum NonFlowOperation { /* every C2-reachable operation */ }
   111	pub enum NonFlowValue { /* heterogeneous results */ }
   112	
   113	impl TypeInfoCore {
   114	    pub fn attempt(
   115	        &self,
   116	        observations: &ObservationSnapshot,
   117	        operation: NonFlowOperation,
   118	    ) -> AttemptOutcome<NonFlowValue>;
   119	}
   120	```
   121	
   122	Keep the implementation modules and fields private. Match `NonFlowOperation` exhaustively with no wildcard. Adding a variant then forces the dispatcher to change, while every cross-crate operation necessarily returns the one inherent method’s `AttemptOutcome`. Compile-fail fixtures prove foreign code cannot implement a query/observation trait or access an alternate kernel operation. This is a mechanically valid proof of the closed cross-crate entry surface and its return shape.
   123	
   124	It is not—and stable Rust cannot make it—a complete proof that every internal helper is I/O-free. `verter_semantic` can still compile `std::fs`, `std::net`, a blocking primitive, a global/TLS read, or an I/O-capable callback without naming `VerterHost` or scheduler. Cargo’s crate firewall cannot observe those effects. A dedicated `#![no_std]` capability crate could strengthen that proof, but the binding ruling requires the existing `verter_semantic` crate.
   125	
   126	The honest mechanically checkable criterion is therefore:
   127	
   128	- Every external C2 operation is a `NonFlowOperation` and enters through `TypeInfoCore::attempt`.
   129	- All kernel internals are private to that module tree.
   130	- The semantic Cargo closure contains only layers 1–3.
   131	- Compile-fail tests pin sealing and private-entry unreachability.
   132	- Exhaustive all-missing-observation tests cover every enum variant and require `NeedInputs` or `Terminal`, never blocking.
   133	- Internal absence of direct I/O/blocking remains an audited/linted source invariant, not a type-system proof.
   134	
   135	Accepted ADR: unchanged by all three gap resolutions.
   136	
   137	Program DAG edge: unchanged; the planned dependency inversion remains higher layers → `verter_semantic`.
   138	
   139	Program outcome: unchanged; full non-flow extraction and full behavioral `AttemptOutcome` coverage remain required.
   140	
   141	GAP 1 VERDICT — Current cross-crate sealing design is impossible; seal semantic-owned snapshots and require compiler/session composition, not foreign implementations.
   142	
   143	GAP 2 VERDICT — The proposed files do not close below layer 4 as-is; C1 is executable only through the listed splits, cuts, and capture inversions.
   144	
   145	GAP 3 VERDICT — The exhaustive-`impl` proof is false; a closed inherent gateway proves boundary shape, but total internal I/O-freedom has no mechanically valid proof under the preserved existing-crate architecture.

   307	   because compiler already depends on semantic (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:51-59`).

   310	   protocol's existing semantic dependency (`crates/verter_protocol/Cargo.toml:12-20`) creates a direct

   313	   at `resolver_core/component_meta/mod.rs:251-288`; native props calls a host projection at
   314	   `component_meta/native_props.rs:113-139`; `ResolverContext` names scheduler cancellation at
   315	   `resolver_context.rs:188-196`. All three are cut; captured language, prepared-declaration, surface,
   316	   and cancellation-state observations replace them, delivered through `ObservationSnapshot`. This is
   317	   why `component_meta/` cannot move as an unmodified wildcard (see the convergence map above).
   318	4. **Store and cache infrastructure.** `HostStoreView` is not a dependency-neutral value — see the
   319	   convergence-map row above. `HostStoreView`, its `StoreViewRoots`, and its manager stay in
   320	   `verter_session`; only `StoreViewValidationToken`-shaped scalar DTOs and the new `ObservationSnapshot`
   321	   move down.
   322	5. **Workspace fact vocabulary.** `resolver_core/fact_read_set.rs:1-5`, `resolver_core/reuse.rs:46-51`,
   323	   `resolver_core/request_store_view.rs:81-94`, and `resolver_core/mod.rs:669-672` import workspace-owned
   324	   fact/cache types. Move the neutral fact identities, read-set values, populations, and
   325	   validation-result vocabulary into semantic; workspace and session then import them downward. Live
   326	   fact registries, published roots, transactions, and generation capture remain workspace/session.
   327	6. **`ProjectResolver`.** Its pure algorithm depends on workspace DTOs and membership
   328	   (`verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs:11-17,74-114`), but its resolution entry accepts live
   329	   `WorkspaceRead` (`:321-365`), path resolution calls `probe_path`/`realpath` (`:1251-1267`), and
   330	   package resolution calls live manifest reads (`:1654-1663`). Move the algorithm, request/result/
   331	   manifest DTOs, and immutable membership predicate into semantic. Replace `WorkspaceRead` with
   332	   snapshot lookups whose missing keys produce `NeedInputs`. Keep `resolve_tracked`,
   333	   `TrackedResolutionCapability`, and `TransactionReader` in workspace (`:354-384`).

   340	   reach (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:108-126`).

   343	   cache/project-store machinery (`flow_return.rs:2016-2078`). Its architectural home is genuinely

   345	   preserve the stated member scope: move the flow query/value types and pure evaluation code unchanged;
   346	   leave cache-node admission, retention, audit, and capture in `verter_session`. Flow remains exempt

   348	   flow" below).

   365	
   366	## Batched `NeedInputs` contract — full coverage (Fork 4)
   367	
   368	C1 owns the **kernel-level** attempt outcome: a resolver-core operation run under an I/O-free environment
   369	returns `AttemptOutcome::{Complete(T), NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal(AttemptFailure)}` per
   370	`contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4, instead of calling `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   371	synchronously. `LoadSet` is normalized/sorted/deduplicated; `NeedInputs` on an empty delta with no basis
   372	change is the typed `InputResolutionNoProgress` failure (§4.3-4.5 of that contract), never a silent retry
   373	loop. This capability does not exist anywhere in the tree today (`grep -rn "NeedInputs\|LoadSet" crates/`
   374	— zero hits) and is new work, not a refactor of an existing batching mechanism.
   375	
   376	**Coverage is full, per the Fork 4 ruling — not "module/import resolution only."** Every non-flow
   377	`ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
   378	outcome: module/import resolution, decl-body lowering, relation/inference queries driven through
   379	`execute_relate`'s plumbing (the algorithm itself stays `Preserve`; only the calling convention around it
   380	changes), and the member/JSDoc-hydration path that already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`
   381	(`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`) today. `contracts/input-loading.md:5-19`
   382	is unqualified across compiler/resolver/TypeInfo kernels, and ADR-011:19-28 requires each attempt to
   383	report the maximal sound missing-observation set — a partial cut would leave C2 unable to plan its
   384	complete semantic demand closure before projection (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:18,44-53`) for
   385	whichever operations were left out. Internally, `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` may still
   386	become the two central observation-or-demand choke points every covered operation funnels through — that
   387	is an implementation strategy, not a scope carve-out. Acceptance is never "one real load point exercised
   388	by a test harness"; it is every reachable operation covered, expressed at the type level as a closed
   389	`NonFlowOperation` variant matched exhaustively by `TypeInfoCore::attempt` (GAP 3).
   390	
   520	  entirely in `verter_session`, so nothing about the crate move weakens it. C1 preserves the seal and, if
   521	  the bare-host rail is deleted (see above), tightens `RequestBoundResolverContext` from "narrower than
   522	  `ResolverContext`" to "identical to it." `ObservationRead` is a *separate*, independently sealed trait
   523	  in `verter_semantic` — not a subtrait of `ResolverContext` — per the ruling, a subtrait would inherit
   524	  `ensure_loaded`/the host escape hatch and prove nothing.
   525	- **`StoreView`/`HostStoreView` immutability is already structural**, not a convention: `HostStoreView`
   526	  has no `&VerterHost`/`Arc<Mutex<..>>` field, only `Arc`-shared by-value snapshot data. Per GAP 2 item 4
   527	  this type does **not** relocate — it stays in `verter_session` alongside its roots and manager, exactly
   528	  because its `StoreViewRoots` field retains live store handles that are not dependency-neutral. The
   529	  dependency-neutral value that does relocate is the new `ObservationSnapshot`, a distinct, narrower type
   530	  built specifically to exclude those handles.

   534	  forward-only landed-scanner rule, these are **grandfathered, not a template**. Because the scanned file
   535	  physically moves to `verter_semantic`, this grandfathered scanner's target path must be updated to keep
   536	  scanning the relocated file — that is "extending the existing grandfathered scanner's checked
   537	  assertions" (permitted) tracking a genuine regression risk from the move, not authoring a new
   538	  standalone scanner (forbidden). C1 must not add a new name-keyed source scanner for any new invariant it
   539	  introduces (the deleted bare-host rail, the collapsed duplication, the new `AttemptOutcome`, the new
   540	  `ObservationSnapshot`/`TypeInfoCore::attempt` gateway) — new confinement here is type-level and
   541	  crate-boundary-level only.
   542	
   543	**Residual limit — not mechanically provable, stated plainly (GAP 3).** None of the above proves every
   544	internal helper inside the extracted kernel is I/O-free. `verter_semantic` can still compile `std::fs`,
   545	`std::net`, a blocking primitive, a global/TLS read, or an I/O-capable callback without naming
   546	`VerterHost` or the scheduler anywhere — Cargo's crate firewall cannot observe those effects, because
   547	they never touch a crate-graph edge. A dedicated `#![no_std]` capability crate could strengthen this
   548	proof, but the binding ruling requires reusing the existing `verter_semantic` crate, so that stronger
   549	proof is out of scope for C1. This is accepted, disclosed residue, not a defect the charter is hiding:
   550	internal absence of direct I/O/blocking inside the kernel is an **audited/linted source invariant** —
   551	code review discipline plus a `clippy`-level disallowed-import/disallowed-method lint over
   552	`verter_semantic/src/type_info/**` and the relocated `resolver_core`/`resolver_store` trees, checked at
   553	review time and re-checked whenever new internal helpers are added — never claimed as a type-system
   554	guarantee. The mechanically checkable claim stops at boundary shape: every external operation is a
   555	`NonFlowOperation` entering through `TypeInfoCore::attempt`; all kernel internals are private; the
   556	semantic Cargo closure contains only layers 1–3; compile-fail tests pin sealing and private-entry
   557	unreachability; exhaustive all-missing-observation tests cover every `NonFlowOperation` variant and
   558	require `NeedInputs` or `Terminal`, never blocking.
   559	
   560	## Boundary against flow (D-track) and against C2
   561	
   562	**Flow exclusion.** C1 converges the relation/inference authority (`execute_relate`,
   563	`project_semantic_dispatch/relation.rs`) exactly as it stands today — `Preserve`, not `Converge`. It adds
   564	no flow-specific relation classifier, no binding-slot integration, no nominal-identity/unique-symbol
   565	comparability extension. Those are `D3`'s stated job: "Extend the already-shared relation authority with
   566	nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability" (`program.md:249-253`). C1's only
   567	obligation to the flow track is that the relation authority it converges (now physically in
   568	`verter_semantic`) remains the single authority `D1` integrates against behind its private non-production
   569	test boundary (`program.md:229`) and that `D3` later extends without needing a second relation/name
   570	authority (`program.md:253`). The full-coverage `AttemptOutcome` threading touches the *calling
   571	convention* around `execute_relate` (per Fork 4) but never the relation algorithm itself. Per GAP 2 item
   572	8, `flow_return`'s ambiguous placement resolves the same way: its query/value types and pure evaluation
   573	code relocate into `verter_semantic` unchanged (they must, since the shared dispatcher they route through
   574	relocates), while its cache-node admission, retention, audit, and capture stay in `verter_session`; flow
   575	stays exempt from the `AttemptOutcome` conversion in both halves.
   576	
   577	**C2 boundary.** C2 owns the staged compile transaction: `prepare → plan → project → emit`,
   578	`CompilePlanToken`/`ProjectionPlanToken` anti-replay, `CompileFactsBatch`, the concrete sealed
   579	`CompileTypeInfo`, and the outer load/commit/retry loop over C1's `NeedInputs` outcome (ADR-011,
   580	`program.md:242-247`). C1 must not build any of that — no plan token, no fact batch, no staged
   581	prepare/plan/project/emit state machine. C1's deliverable to C2 is now concretely: a converged kernel
   582	physically resident in `verter_semantic` that (a) gives identical answers across lifecycles, (b) can be
   583	driven from an I/O-free `ObservationSnapshot` through the closed `TypeInfoCore::attempt` gateway and
   584	returns `NeedInputs` instead of blocking across its **full** operation surface, and (c) is constructible
   585	without pulling in `verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api`/LSP-facing machinery *by construction of the crate
   586	graph*, so C2's compiler-facing facade embeds `verter_semantic` the same way `verter_compiler` already
   587	does today (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`) with no cycle risk. `CompileTypeInfo` composes an
   588	`ObservationSnapshot`; per GAP 1 it never implements `ObservationRead`.
   589	
   590	## Required exit
   591	
   592	Per `program.md:196`: **lifecycle differs; module/name/type/relation meaning does not.** Concretely: the
   593	converged kernel (`ModuleResolverCore`, non-flow `TypeInfoCore`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, relation/node
   594	algorithms, dependency-neutral value types, `ObservationSnapshot`, `TypeInfoCore::attempt`,
   595	`AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`) lives in `verter_semantic`; `ResolverContext`/`RequestBoundResolverContext`
   596	and their two concrete adapters stay in `verter_session`, unmoved, now composing `ObservationSnapshot`
   597	internally; the three (or more, once a future I/O-free lifecycle exists) lifecycle implementors give
   598	bit-identical resolved answers for identical inputs; the duplicated boilerplate between
   599	`HostResolverContext` and `SessionResolverContext` is gone; `verter_semantic`'s production closure
   600	excludes `verter_workspace`, `verter_session`, `verter_scheduler`, and `verter_tsgo_api` on every target
   601	with the A5-DD1 exception row deleted, not recorded as still-permitted; `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)`
   602	exists and covers every non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2
   603	projection attempt, exercised by an I/O-free test harness that never touches the scheduler; the
   604	Authority-uniqueness contract's five rows still hold; no `TypeExpr`-general transit, flow semantics, or
   605	C2-owned staged-transaction machinery was introduced; and the residual limit on internal I/O-freedom
   606	(GAP 3) is recorded as an audited/linted source invariant in the owning skill docs, not silently dropped.
   607

     1	//! Demand-sliced flow content — the OWNED, arena-free content lowering
     2	//! of exactly one planned flow slice.
     3	//!
     4	//! The [`FunctionProgramIndex`](verter_semantic::analysis::function_program::FunctionProgramIndex)
     5	//! is the eager STRUCTURAL inventory (identities + locators, no lowered
     6	//! types), and the flow-slice substrate (`verter_semantic::analysis::flow`)
     7	//! plans the demanded slice as graph reachability and lowers it into the
     8	//! content-free `FlowSliceIR`. THIS module is the content half: on the
     9	//! cold path of one flow evaluation it reborrows the retained parse
    10	//! snapshot ONCE (through the memo's lease-only run, exactly like every

    91	    /// Binding-identifier spans of the slice's VALUE-selected slots —

   122	        self.value_slot_spans.contains(&span)
   123	    }

   721	Dominator indexes, loop forests, SCC indexes, reverse adjacency, def-use overlays, capture summaries, and compact schedules are permitted only as deterministic projections of one exact graph/profile identity. They cannot introduce semantic facts, are request-local by default, and have independent weight/eviction when retained.
   722	
   723	## 9.3 Demand plan and closed domain registry
   724	
   725	A product operation names semantic obligations. The solver computes the transitive closure through one static domain registry before evaluation. Candidate domains include declared/reaching type, narrowing, relation, completion, definite assignment, capture freshness/invalidation, effect, and coverage.
   726	
   727	A `FlowDemandPlan` selects only nodes/edges/domains needed by the result. A fixed point runs only on selected obligations that require convergence. A missing registered prerequisite makes the plan invalid and cannot produce a complete result.
   728	
   729	## 9.4 Binding and relation authority
   730	
   731	Flow state is keyed by stable binding/slot identity, never by string names. Declaration authority exists for annotated and inferred bindings. Joins, substitution, and nominal `unique symbol` overlap/comparability use the shared semantic relation/inference implementation; flow owns no private relation classifier.
   732	
   733	## 9.5 Structural returns and completion
   734	
   735	For return inference:
   736	
   737	```text
   738	result = union(effective_type(return_expr_i, program_point_i)
   739	               for every authored return statement i)
   740	       + (endpoint_reachable ? undefined : nothing)
   741	```
   742	
   743	Authored return membership is structural. Reachability does not delete a return contributor. Endpoint reachability is a separate completion question.
   744	
   745	Completion uses one algebra:
   746	
   747	```rust
   748	enum CompletionKind {
   749	    Normal,
   750	    Return,
   751	    Throw,
   752	    Break(LabelId),
   753	    Continue(LabelId),
   754	}
   755	```
   756	
   757	Blocks, conditions, loops, labels, `switch`, `try`, `catch`, and `finally` transform/join completion sets. Suffix booleans, “guarantees return,” and pending-break flags are prohibited.
   758	
   759	## 9.6 Closure and effects
   760	
   761	The structural producer retains nested capture reads and writes. Summaries include direct/transitive reads, writes, escapes, creation point, freshness, and invalidating-write information.
   762	
   763	Effects use one expression-position-independent mechanism. No IIFE/capture hook is specialized to statement, initializer, condition, argument, return, sequence, literal, or another parent position. Compatibility results match the selected semantic profile; extra analysis may decide whether answering is safe but may not publish a different compatibility answer.
   764	
   765	## 9.7 Obligation ledger and proof-carrying completeness
   766	
   767	Each solve owns a private obligation ledger. Every selected graph/domain/fixed-point/semantic operation finishes as one of:
   768	
   769	```text
   770	Discharged
   771	CoverageGap
   772	Unsupported
   773	Cancelled
   774	BudgetExceeded
   775	Stale
   776	InternalFailure
   777	```

   779	Only a private finalizer can construct `CompleteFlowResult`, and only when every required obligation is `Discharged` under the exact graph, demand, profile, input basis, and result contract. Rich audit evidence is optional/request-scoped; the production proof token is compact.
   780	
   781	Partial/gap results may be returned but remain non-admissible unless a separate query contract proves partial admission. Authored `any` is distinct from unmodelled semantics.

     1	# ADR-001 — One Semantic Authority, Justified Derived Projections
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** TypeInfo/effective-flow architecture
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	`FunctionFlowGraph` must be the one structural flow authority, but efficient solving may need dominators, loop forests, SCCs, def-use overlays, capture summaries, reverse adjacency, or compact execution schedules. Forbidding every graph-derived structure would either bloat the canonical graph or repeat topology work. Allowing independent query-specific CFGs recreates the current dual-authority defect.
     9	
    10	## Decision
    11	
    12	`FunctionFlowGraph` is the canonical structural authority. A derived structure is allowed only when it:
    13	
    14	- is keyed by one exact graph/body identity and any interpretation-affecting semantic profile;
    15	- is deterministic and fully reproducible from the graph and accepted kernel rules;
    16	- cannot add facts, define transfer/join semantics, mark coverage complete, or publish a semantic result;
    17	- is request-local by default and independently weighted/evicted if retention is proven valuable;
    18	- can be replaced without changing observable semantics.
    19	
    20	## Consequences
    21	
    22	The solver may use efficient layouts without creating a second semantic or control authority. Review checks authority and construction rights, not superficial data-structure count.
    23	
    24	## Rejected alternatives
    25	
    26	- exactly one physical graph-like object;
    27	- independent syntax-shaped/query-specific CFGs;
    28	- projections that own relation, completion, capture, or coverage decisions.
     1	# ADR-014 — Flow Replaces the Legacy Evaluator in One Atomic Public Cutover
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** flow migration and cache admission  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a release obligation explicitly requires two semantics paths, which would require a new architecture decision and bounded compatibility window.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	Building graph/domain features across many accepted merges while the old syntax-shaped evaluator remains selectable creates two production authorities. Deleting the old path only after full parity pressures implementors to copy the legacy model into the replacement.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	1. Build the minimum new graph/domain/obligation/coverage foundation behind a private non-production test boundary on the bounded cutover branch; it may be reviewed as a checkpoint but never merged or released independently.
    14	2. In one public cutover, route all effective-flow operations to the new solver and delete the old evaluator and its state/caches/tasks/flags.
    15	3. Unsupported mechanisms return typed non-admissible gaps; temporary reduction from guessed success to honest partial is allowed only for rows not ratified Supported/Stable, or through a separate reviewed breaking product decision.
    16	4. Later semantic blocks only expand the sole solver.
    17	5. A private obligation ledger and finalizer make complete-result construction impossible unless all required closed-domain obligations are discharged.
    18	
    19	No runtime flag, compatibility shim, shadow evaluator, or compare-in-production path survives the accepted cutover.
    20	
    21	## Consequences
    22	
    23	- one production semantic authority at all times after `D2`;
    24	- completeness proof is architectural rather than a convention;
    25	- parity can expand without preserving guessed legacy behavior.
    26	
    27	## Rejected alternatives
    28	
    29	- **Long-running dual evaluators:** divergent semantics and cache risk.
    30	- **Wait for full parity before deletion:** encourages porting the second authority intact.
     1	# ADR-015 — Core Dependency Direction Is Inward and Cycle-Free
     2	
     3	**Status:** Accepted  
     4	**Decision owner:** crate/module ownership  
     5	**Reopen only if:** a new stable boundary cannot be represented without a cycle and an alternative decomposition has been disproven.
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	Where `CompileTypeInfo`, framework projection DTOs, and request contracts live can accidentally create compiler↔semantic or compiler↔session cycles, forcing traits, erasure, and shared ownership.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	Binding direction is:
    14	
    15	```text
    16	identity/span/language/contracts
    17	-> shared syntax frontends and dependency-neutral DTOs
    18	-> semantic kernel/module resolver/relation/flow
    19	-> compiler
    20	-> managed engine/session
    21	-> LSP/provider/MCP/NAPI/WASM/CLI adapters
    22	```
    23	
    24	Rules:
    25	
    26	- syntax/contracts do not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    27	- semantic kernel does not depend on compiler, session, provider, or LSP;
    28	- compiler may depend on syntax, sealed semantic facade, and neutral closed DTOs;
    29	- managed engine depends on compiler/semantic, never the reverse;
    30	- provider lifecycle never enters direct compiler or semantic kernel;
    31	- adapters depend inward only;
    32	- durable build tests reject crate dependency cycles and forbidden edges.
    33	
    34	Logical owners do not automatically require crates; use modules/functions until a real dependency firewall or multi-consumer stable contract exists.
    35	
    36	## Consequences
    37	
    38	- direct compiler cannot become a session mode;
    39	- semantic kernel remains reusable across lifecycles;
    40	- fewer traits, erased bags, and `Arc` workarounds are required.
    41	
    42	## Rejected alternatives
    43	
    44	- **Mutual compiler/semantic callbacks:** creates cycles and alternate behavior.
    45	- **Everything in session/host crate:** preserves catch-all ownership.

   501	        site: SliceCallSite,

   503	    ) -> SignatureCall {

   505	        let Some(data) = graph.node_data(function_node) else {
   506	            return SignatureCall::NotCallable;

   509	            return_type,
   510	            type_parameters,
   511	            params,
   512	            ..

   527	                        site,
   528	                        dispatch.first_signature_param_occurrence(&params, decl.name.as_ref()),
   529	                    );

   531	                        Arc::clone(&decl.name),
   532	                        site,
   533	                        inference,
   534	                        || Some(default),

   538	                        // already-resolved node, so this arm is
   539	                        // unreachable today; it stays a typed outcome
   540	                        // rather than an `unwrap` so a future producer

   553	            Some(SemanticNodeData::Opaque(QueryError::Miss))

   375	        identity: &verter_type_expr::facts::FlowFunctionReturnIdentity,
   376	        demand: crate::semantic_query::ReturnProjectionDemand,
   377	    ) -> FlowReturnKey {
   378	        FlowReturnKey {
   379	            function: self.flow_function_slot_for(
   380	                Arc::clone(&identity.anchor.canonical_id),
   381	                identity.anchor.owner,
   382	                Arc::clone(&identity.anchor.symbol),
   383	                identity.function_part.clone(),
   384	                identity.overload_ordinal,
   385	            ),
   386	            normalized_type_args: Arc::from(Vec::new().into_boxed_slice()),
   387	            context: self.flow_return_context_for(identity.anchor.canonical_id.as_ref()),
   388	            demand,
   389	            input: crate::semantic_query::FlowInputContext::empty(),
   390	        }
   391	    }

   393	    /// The instantiation half of the ONE construction point: call
   394	    /// resolution demands the callee's flow return under the call's
   395	    /// FINAL ordered type-argument mapping and substitution — the same
   396	    /// env-bearing slot and context derivation, with the demand and
   397	    /// input axes at the canonical production point.
   398	    pub(crate) fn flow_return_key_for_instantiation(
   399	        &self,
   400	        identity: &verter_type_expr::facts::FlowFunctionReturnIdentity,
   401	        normalized_type_args: Arc<[SemanticNodeId]>,
   402	        substitution: crate::semantic_query::CanonicalTypeSubstitution,
   403	    ) -> FlowReturnKey {
   404	        let mut key = self.flow_return_key_with_demand(
   405	            identity,
   406	            crate::semantic_query::ReturnProjectionDemand::whole_return(),
   407	        );
   408	        key.normalized_type_args = normalized_type_args;
   409	        key.context.type_substitution = substitution;
   410	        key
   411	    }

   413	    /// Full live context for an indexed semantic call at `canonical`:
   414	    /// the same `P R T L J` env derivation [`Self::flow_return_context_for`]
   415	    /// owns, with the empty type substitution.
   416	    pub(crate) fn resolve_call_context_for(
   417	        &self,
   418	        canonical: &str,
   419	    ) -> crate::semantic_query::ResolveCallContext {
   420	        let host = self.ctx.host_for_fact_tracer_install();
   421	        let env = host.host_view_env_hashes_for(canonical);
   422	        crate::semantic_query::ResolveCallContext {
   423	            parse_env_hash: env.parse_env_hash,
   424	            resolve_env_hash: env.resolve_env_hash,
   425	            type_env_hash: env.type_env_hash,
   426	            lib_env_hash: env.lib_env_hash,
   427	            project_identity: host.host_view_project_identity().0,
   428	            substitution: crate::semantic_query::CanonicalTypeSubstitution::empty(),
   429	        }
   430	    }

   432	    /// Execute one indexed semantic call and return only a complete admitted
   433	    /// selected or genuine-dynamic value node.
   434	    pub(crate) fn execute_indexed_resolve_call(
   435	        &self,
   436	        key: crate::semantic_query::ResolveCallKey,
   437	    ) -> Option<crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId> {
   438	        self.execute_indexed_resolve_call_with_flow_hold(key, false)
   439	            .0
   440	    }
   441	
   442	    /// The flow-aware half of [`Self::execute_indexed_resolve_call`]: when
   443	    /// `hold_flow_result` is set, a complete or held call whose result a
   444	    /// surrounding FlowReturn evaluation depends on is recorded as a
   445	    /// tagged hold on the nearest active flow frame instead of serving a
   446	    /// provisional value — the frame's SCC close joins the admitted
   447	    /// result through its return equation.
   448	    pub(crate) fn execute_indexed_resolve_call_with_flow_hold(
   449	        &self,
   450	        key: crate::semantic_query::ResolveCallKey,
   451	        hold_flow_result: bool,
   452	    ) -> (Option<crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId>, bool) {
   453	        match self.execute_resolve_call(key.clone()) {
   454	            super::call_resolve::ResolveCallStep::Complete(result) => {
   455	                let return_type = super::return_equation::resolved_call_return_type(&result);
   456	                let held_by_flow = hold_flow_result
   457	                    && self
   458	                        .dispatch_txn
   459	                        .borrow_mut()
   460	                        .reentry_mut()
   461	                        .record_nearest_flow_hold(
   462	                            super::dispatch_txn::ReturnObligationIdentity::ResolveCall(key),
   463	                        );
   464	                if held_by_flow {
   465	                    (None, true)
   466	                } else {
   467	                    (Some(return_type), false)
   468	                }
   469	            }
   470	            super::call_resolve::ResolveCallStep::Hold(target) => {
   471	                let held_by_flow = hold_flow_result
   472	                    && self
   473	                        .dispatch_txn
   474	                        .borrow_mut()
   475	                        .reentry_mut()
   476	                        .record_nearest_flow_hold(
   477	                            super::dispatch_txn::ReturnObligationIdentity::ResolveCall(*target),
   478	                        );
   479	                (None, held_by_flow)
   480	            }
   481	            super::call_resolve::ResolveCallStep::Degraded(_) => (None, false),
   482	        }
   483	    }
   484	
   485	    /// Evaluate parsed indexed expression IR directly to a semantic node.
   486	    /// Calls route only through `ResolveCall`; a non-result is a typed miss
   487	    /// without a scanner/raw-expression fallback.
   488	    pub(crate) fn evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node(
   489	        &self,
   490	        canonical: &str,
   491	        owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   492	        expression: &verter_type_expr::IndexedValueExpression,
   493	    ) -> Option<crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId> {
   494	        self.evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node_inner(canonical, owner, expression, true)
   495	    }
   496	
   497	    pub(crate) fn evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node_inner(
   498	        &self,
   499	        canonical: &str,
   500	        owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   501	        expression: &verter_type_expr::IndexedValueExpression,
   502	        hold_flow_result: bool,
   503	    ) -> Option<crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId> {
   504	        use verter_type_expr::{IndexedValueCallKind, IndexedValueExpression};
   505	        match expression {
   506	            IndexedValueExpression::Value(value) => self.lower_type_expr_in_owner_scope_with_mode(
   507	                canonical,
   508	                owner,
   509	                value,
   510	                crate::semantic_query::ProjectionMode::Navigate,
   511	            ),
   512	            IndexedValueExpression::UnsupportedCall { .. } => {
   513	                crate::request_context::mark_request_result_partial();
   514	                None
   515	            }
   516	            IndexedValueExpression::Call(call) => {
   517	                let callee = self.evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node_inner(
   518	                    canonical,
   519	                    owner,
   520	                    &call.callee,
   521	                    false,
   522	                )?;
   523	                let receiver = call.receiver.as_deref().and_then(|receiver| {
   524	                    self.evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node_inner(
   525	                        canonical, owner, receiver, false,
   526	                    )
   527	                });
   528	                let mut args = Vec::with_capacity(call.args.len());
   529	                for argument in call.args.iter() {
   530	                    let ty = self.evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node_inner(
   531	                        canonical,
   532	                        owner,
   533	                        &argument.expression,
   534	                        false,
   535	                    )?;
   536	                    args.push(crate::semantic_query::CallArgKey::Eager {
   537	                        ty,
   538	                        spread: argument.spread,
   539	                        context_sensitive: argument.context_sensitive,
   540	                        literal_mode: match argument.literal_mode {
   541	                            verter_type_expr::IndexedValueLiteralMode::Widened => {
   542	                                crate::semantic_query::ArgumentLiteralMode::Widened
   543	                            }
   544	                            verter_type_expr::IndexedValueLiteralMode::Literal => {
   545	                                crate::semantic_query::ArgumentLiteralMode::Literal
   546	                            }
   547	                        },
   548	                    });
   549	                }
   550	                let explicit_type_args = call
   551	                    .explicit_type_args
   552	                    .iter()
   553	                    .map(|argument| {
   554	                        self.lower_type_expr_in_owner_scope_with_mode(
   555	                            canonical,
   556	                            owner,
   557	                            argument,
   558	                            crate::semantic_query::ProjectionMode::Navigate,
   559	                        )
   560	                    })
   561	                    .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
   562	                let (result, held) = self.execute_indexed_resolve_call_with_flow_hold(
   563	                    crate::semantic_query::ResolveCallKey {
   564	                        point: crate::semantic_query::ProgramPointId {
   565	                            canonical_id: Arc::from(canonical),
   566	                            offset: call.point,
   567	                        },
   568	                        callee,
   569	                        kind: match call.kind {
   570	                            IndexedValueCallKind::Call => crate::semantic_query::CallKind::Call,
   571	                            IndexedValueCallKind::Construct => {
   572	                                crate::semantic_query::CallKind::Construct
   573	                            }
   574	                        },
   575	                        receiver,
   576	                        args: Arc::from(args.into_boxed_slice()),
   577	                        explicit_type_args: Arc::from(explicit_type_args.into_boxed_slice()),
   578	                        flow: crate::semantic_query::FlowNarrowingKey::empty(),
   579	                        context: self.resolve_call_context_for(canonical),
   580	                    },
   581	                    hold_flow_result,
   582	                );
   583	                if result.is_none() && !held {
   584	                    crate::request_context::mark_request_result_partial();
   585	                }
   586	                result
   587	            }
   588	        }
   589	    }
   590	
   591	    /// Consume an inferred declaration's indexed semantic expression source.
   592	    pub(crate) fn execute_semantic_expression_source(
   593	        &self,
   594	        source: &verter_type_expr::facts::SemanticExpressionSource,
   595	        owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   596	    ) -> Option<crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId> {
   597	        match source {
   598	            verter_type_expr::facts::SemanticExpressionSource::FunctionReturn(source) => {
   599	                let canonical = match source {
   600	                    verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Declared(locator) => {
   601	                        locator.slot().anchor.canonical_id.as_ref()
   602	                    }
   603	                    verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Flow(identity) => {
   604	                        identity.anchor.canonical_id.as_ref()
   605	                    }
   606	                    verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Absent => return None,
   607	                };
   608	                match self.execute_function_return_source(source, canonical) {
   609	                    FunctionReturnNode::Declared(node) => Some(node.node()),
   610	                    FunctionReturnNode::Flow(result) => Some(result.return_type()),
   611	                    FunctionReturnNode::DeclaredMiss
   612	                    | FunctionReturnNode::NoValue(_)
   613	                    | FunctionReturnNode::Absent => None,
   614	                }
   615	            }
   616	            verter_type_expr::facts::SemanticExpressionSource::ProgramExpression(point) => {
   617	                let serve = self
   618	                    .ctx
   619	                    .ensure_indexed_ready_serve(point.canonical_id.as_ref())?;
   620	                let indexed = serve.indexed;
   621	                let memo = indexed.shallow_state.decl_bodies();
   622	                let index = memo.function_program_index();
   623	                let record = index.expression(point)?;
   624	                match &record.source {
   625	                    verter_semantic::analysis::function_program::ProgramExpressionSource::FunctionReturn(source) => {
   626	                        match self.execute_function_return_source(source, point.canonical_id.as_ref()) {
   627	                            FunctionReturnNode::Declared(node) => Some(node.node()),
   628	                            FunctionReturnNode::Flow(result) => Some(result.return_type()),
   629	                            FunctionReturnNode::DeclaredMiss
   630	                            | FunctionReturnNode::NoValue(_)
   631	                            | FunctionReturnNode::Absent => None,
   632	                        }
   633	                    }
   634	                    verter_semantic::analysis::function_program::ProgramExpressionSource::UnsupportedCall => {
   635	                        crate::request_context::mark_request_result_partial();
   636	                        None
   637	                    }
   638	                    verter_semantic::analysis::function_program::ProgramExpressionSource::Value
   639	                    | verter_semantic::analysis::function_program::ProgramExpressionSource::SemanticCall { .. } => {
   640	                        let expression = memo.indexed_program_expression_ir(record)?;
   641	                        self.evaluate_indexed_value_expression_node(
   642	                            point.canonical_id.as_ref(),
   643	                            owner,
   644	                            expression.as_ref(),
   645	                        )
   646	                    }
   647	                }
   648	            }
   649	        }
   650	    }
   651	
   652	    /// The ONE sealed function-return consumer entry: routes the fact's
   653	    /// [`verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource`] to its producer.
   654	    /// `Declared` lowers through the memoized locator rail; `Flow`
   655	    /// constructs and executes the [`FlowReturnKey`] through
   656	    /// [`Self::flow_return_key_for`] (never the `None → miss_node` arm);
   657	    /// `Absent` reports the absent carrier.
   658	    pub(crate) fn execute_function_return_source(
   659	        &self,
   660	        source: &verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource,
   661	        scope_canonical_id: &str,
   662	    ) -> FunctionReturnNode {
   663	        match source {
   664	            verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Declared(locator) => {
   665	                match self
   666	                    .raise_body_slot(locator.slot(), scope_canonical_id)
   667	                    .at_optional_boundary()
   668	                {
   669	                    Some(hot) => FunctionReturnNode::Declared(hot),
   670	                    None => FunctionReturnNode::DeclaredMiss,
   671	                }
   672	            }
   673	            verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Flow(identity) => {
   674	                let node = match self.execute_flow_return(self.flow_return_key_for(identity)) {
   675	                    // A DEGRADED SUCCESS stays usable — the consumer keeps
   676	                    // the value (interning a miss would be the opposite
   677	                    // collapse).
   678	                    FlowReturnStep::Complete(result) => FunctionReturnNode::Flow(result),
   679	                    FlowReturnStep::NoValue(failure) => FunctionReturnNode::NoValue(failure),
   680	                    // A hold surfacing at a consumer is a demand reentering
   681	                    // its own in-flight component: undecided here, ReturnOnly.
   682	                    FlowReturnStep::Hold(_) => {
   683	                        FunctionReturnNode::NoValue(FlowReturnFailure::Unresolved)
   684	                    }
   685	                };
   686	                // THE cache-read fold — ONE call site, EVERY non-clean arm,
   687	                // no `degradation.is_some()` condition at THAT entry. (The
   688	                // bit is still read for questions that are not the
   689	                // consumer's fold: this module's own admission gate,
   690	                // `scc_publish`'s component-wide publication gate, and the
   691	                // TSC projection's inferred-class-member row.)
   692	                //
   693	                // `build_flow_return` sets `cache_suppress` on the
   694	                // `FlowReturn` query's OWN output. That says nothing about
   695	                // the ENCLOSING composition, and the four consumers each
   696	                // turn a no-value failure into `Opaque(Miss)` / `miss_node`
   697	                // — two of them with no taint at all. So a failure was
   698	                // laundered into a warm-admitted enclosing result exactly
   699	                // as a degraded success was before the success arm was
   700	                // folded; the asymmetry was never a decision.
   701	                //
   702	                // Which RAILS fold is a per-arm FACT, not a per-call-site
   703	                // condition, so it is decided once by the exhaustive
   704	                // [`FunctionReturnNode::consumer_fold`] classification.
   705	                match node.consumer_fold() {
   706	                    ConsumerFold::Clean => {}
   707	                    ConsumerFold::Partial(reasons) => self.fold_flow_return_consumer_rails(reasons),
   708	                }
   709	                node
   710	            }
   711	            verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Absent => FunctionReturnNode::Absent,
   712	        }
   713	    }
   714	
   715	    /// The `ReturnType<typeof callee>` MEMBER-HOP admission: the
   716	    /// path-precise projector demand rail. Given the argument node of a
   717	    /// builtin `ReturnType` instantiation carrier and the pending walk
   718	    /// segment, resolve the callee to its served function slot and — when
   719	    /// the callee is a FUNCTION VALUE whose return is body-derived
   720	    /// (`FunctionReturnSource::Flow`) — dispatch
   721	    /// `SemanticQueryKey::FlowReturn` with the single-member
   722	    /// `ReturnProjectionDemand`, returning the demanded member's node.
   723	    ///
   724	    /// `None` is the structured fall-through: a declared-return callee, a
   725	    /// non-`typeof` argument, an overload group, a computed segment, or a
   726	    /// degraded/held member evaluation all fall back to the generic
   727	    /// `Instantiate` unwrap (the pre-existing whole-return route through
   728	    /// this same dispatch) — never a fabricated member and never a
   729	    /// second resolver.
   730	    /// The typed `ReturnType<typeof callee>` CALLEE detection: `arg` is
   731	    /// the bare `typeof callee` carrier (no member path) of a
   732	    /// single-signature FUNCTION VALUE whose return is body-derived
   733	    /// (`FunctionReturnSource::Flow`), resolved through the prepared
   734	    /// value registry — identity only, no body lowering, no execution.
   735	    /// `None` for a declared-return callee, an overload group, a dotted
   736	    /// `typeof` path, or a non-`typeof` argument.
   737	    pub(super) fn flow_return_callee_for_typeof_arg(
   738	        &self,
   739	        callee_arg: SemanticNodeId,
   740	    ) -> Option<verter_type_expr::facts::FlowFunctionReturnIdentity> {
   741	        let data = crate::project_semantic_dispatch::node_data_for(self.ctx, callee_arg)?;
   742	        let (value_root, typeof_path) = data.typeof_head()?;
   743	        if !typeof_path.is_empty() {
   744	            return None;
   745	        }
   746	        let scope_canonical = Arc::clone(&value_root.scope.canonical_id);
   747	        let scope_owner = value_root.scope.owner;
   748	        let value_name = Arc::clone(&value_root.name);
   749	        drop(data);
   750	        let prepared =
   751	            self.ctx
   752	                .prepared_value_decl(scope_canonical.as_ref(), scope_owner, &value_name)?;
   753	        let [signature] = prepared.signatures.as_slice() else {
   754	            return None;
   755	        };
   756	        let verter_type_expr::facts::FunctionReturnSource::Flow(identity) =
   757	            &signature.return_source
   758	        else {
   759	            return None;
   760	        };
   761	        // Anchor fill mirrors the signature-composition consumers: the
   762	        // extractor stamps the declaration name; canonical / owner come
   763	        // from the serving scope.
   764	        let mut identity = identity.clone();
   765	        identity.anchor.canonical_id = scope_canonical;
   766	        identity.anchor.owner = scope_owner;
   767	        Some(identity)
   768	    }
   769	
   770	    /// Whether `node` is the builtin `ReturnType<typeof callee>`
   771	    /// instantiation carrier over a body-derived (flow-return) callee —
   772	    /// the shape whose MEMBER projection routes through the
   773	    /// single-member `FlowReturn` demand instead of a whole-signature
   774	    /// composition.
   775	    pub(super) fn is_flow_return_type_member_base(&self, node: SemanticNodeId) -> bool {
   776	        match crate::project_semantic_dispatch::node_data_for(self.ctx, node) {
   777	            Some(data) => self.is_flow_return_type_member_base_data(&data),
   778	            None => false,
   779	        }
   780	    }
   781	
   782	    /// The node-data half of [`Self::is_flow_return_type_member_base`].
   783	    /// Matches BOTH carrier stages: the resolved builtin
   784	    /// `InstantiationRef` and the still-unresolved authored
   785	    /// `BareRef("ReturnType", [arg])` (whose head the dispatch's
   786	    /// carrier-subject normalization resolves shadowing-aware — a
   787	    /// userland `ReturnType` shadow settles to its own declaration
   788	    /// there and never enters the flow member rail).
   789	    pub(super) fn is_flow_return_type_member_base_data(&self, data: &SemanticNodeData) -> bool {
   790	        if let SemanticNodeData::InstantiationRef { base, args } = data {
   791	            return base.canonical_id.as_ref() == "__builtin__"
   792	                && base.decl_name.as_ref() == "ReturnType"
   793	                && args.len() == 1
   794	                && self.flow_return_callee_for_typeof_arg(args[0]).is_some();
   795	        }
   796	        if let Some((name, _scope)) = data.bare_ref_head() {
   797	            let args = data.carrier_type_args();
   798	            return name.as_ref() == "ReturnType"
   799	                && args.len() == 1
   800	                && self.flow_return_callee_for_typeof_arg(args[0]).is_some();
   801	        }
   802	        false
   803	    }
   804	
   805	    pub(super) fn flow_return_member_projection(
   806	        &self,
   807	        callee_arg: SemanticNodeId,
   808	        segment: &crate::semantic_query::PathSegment,
   809	    ) -> Option<SemanticNodeId> {
   810	        // The demanded member must be a statically-named key.
   811	        let member_name: Arc<str> = match segment {
   812	            crate::semantic_query::PathSegment::Member(key) => Arc::from(key.as_string()?),
   813	            crate::semantic_query::PathSegment::Index(crate::semantic_query::IndexKey::String(
   814	                value,
   815	            )) => Arc::clone(value),
   816	            crate::semantic_query::PathSegment::Index(_) => return None,
   817	        };
   818	        let identity = self.flow_return_callee_for_typeof_arg(callee_arg)?;
   819	        let demand = crate::semantic_query::ReturnProjectionDemand {
   820	            point: crate::semantic_query::demand::Demand::navigate(
   821	                crate::semantic_query::demand::ProjectionPath::from_segments([
   822	                    crate::semantic_query::PathSegment::Member(
   823	                        crate::semantic_query::PropertyKey::identifier(Arc::clone(&member_name)),
   824	                    ),
   825	                ]),
   826	            ),
   827	        };
   828	        let key = self.flow_return_key_with_demand(&identity, demand);
   829	        match self.execute_flow_return(key) {
   830	            FlowReturnStep::Complete(result) if result.degradation().is_none() => {
   831	                // `ReturnType<…>` is a signature UTILITY, not a call: it
   832	                // has no call site to be argument-free at, so every free
   833	                // clause parameter instantiates at `unknown` and a
   834	                // declared default never applies (`ReturnType<typeof
   835	                // id>` over `id<T = number>(x: T)` is `{ … unknown … }`,
   836	                // not `number`). That is precisely the policy the
   837	                // WHOLE-return route applies through
   838	                // `instantiate_free_signature_params_at_unknown`; this
   839	                // route is the same utility over the same callee one
   840	                // path segment longer, so it applies the same policy —
   841	                // returning the flow return's raw member position would
   842	                // publish the CALLEE's own binder as the consumer's
   843	                // value, and the two routes would disagree about one
   844	                // callee.
   845	                //
   846	                // The clause NAMES come from the shallow function-program
   847	                // fact rather than from composing the callee's signature,
   848	                // so the member demand stays as narrow as it was: a
   849	                // whole-signature composition here would materialise
   850	                // exactly the sibling members this rail exists to leave
   851	                // cold.
   852	                self.instantiate_callee_clause_at_unknown(&identity, result.return_type())
   853	            }
   854	            // Degraded success / typed failure / in-flight hold: the
   855	            // generic unwrap route decides (it already owns these
   856	            // shapes for every other consumer).
   857	            _ => None,
   858	        }
   859	    }
   860	
   861	    /// Instantiate the served callee's OWN type-parameter clause at
   862	    /// `unknown` over a value taken from its body-derived return — the
   863	    /// signature-UTILITY policy, applied without composing a signature.
   864	    ///
   865	    /// A clause the route could not READ is a MISS (`None`), never "the
   866	    /// callee declares none". The two were the same value here — a
   867	    /// failed read returned the callee's return UNTOUCHED, its own
   868	    /// binders intact and warm-admissible — while the CALL-site route
   869	    /// degraded on the identical miss. The clause reader is now shared

   702	impl ResolveCallSelection {

   705	    pub(crate) fn fresh_literal_returns(&self) -> &[SemanticNodeId] {

   715	    pub(crate) fn with_return_type(

   725	                fresh_literal_returns,
   726	            } => ResolvedCallResult::Selected {

   732	                        .intern_node(callable.clone().into_general_signature(return_type)),

   734	                substitution: substitution.clone(),
   735	                return_type,
   736	                fresh_literal_return: fresh_literal_returns.contains(&return_type),
   737	            },
   738	            Self::UnionSelected { arms } => ResolvedCallResult::UnionSelected {
   739	                selections: Arc::from(

   741	                        .map(|arm| crate::semantic_query::ResolvedUnionArm {

   744	                            substitution: arm.substitution.clone(),
   745	                        })
   746	                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   747	                        .into_boxed_slice(),
   748	                ),
   749	                return_type,
   750	            },
   751	            Self::DynamicAny => ResolvedCallResult::DynamicAny { return_type },
   752	        }
   753	    }
   754	}

The authoritative boundary is capability-based, not directory-based: dependency-neutral semantic compute moves to `verter_semantic`; live host observation, cache admission, retention, publication, audit, and I/O remain in `verter_session` ([ADR-015:16-32](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:16), [C1 revised:341-348](<<SESSION_SCRATCH>/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/C1-CHARTER-REVISED.md:341>)).

- `flow_slice_content.rs` — MOVES whole. Its complete surface—`FlowSliceSelection`, every `Slice*`/`Gated*`/`FrameShadowedName` type, `SignatureScope`, `Lowerer`, `build_function_type_param_clause`, `build_flow_slice_content`, and all lowering helpers—is owned, arena-free semantic IR/lowering over OXC and semantic/type-expression inputs; it contains no host, store, scheduler, cache, audit, or I/O authority ([flow_slice_content.rs:53-79](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:53), [flow_slice_content.rs:81-159](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:81), [flow_slice_content.rs:1471-1489](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:1471)). Its being a sibling module is irrelevant to architectural ownership.

- `flow_return_callee.rs` — MOVES whole. `ReturnOrigin`, `ClauseParamInference`, `CalleeClauseParam`, `CalleeClause`, `CalleeClauseLookup`, `CallValue`, `SignatureCall`, `HeldCallee`, and `unmodeled_position_marker` are pure semantic transfer/evaluation machinery. The file depends only on the relocating semantic dispatcher/query vocabulary and function-program facts ([flow_return_callee.rs:84-91](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:84), [flow_return_callee.rs:112-248](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:112), [flow_return_callee.rs:436-733](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:436)).

- `dispatch_txn.rs` — SPLITS; it does not move whole. The semantic transaction symbols move: `SessionId`, `InferenceOccurrence`, `StrictFamilyConfig`, `RelationStep`, `RelationAssumptionEvidence`, `ObligationIdentity`, the frame/pending/SCC topology, `ObligationReentryStack`, `ObligationPendingLedger`, `Provisional*`, `ObligationRuntime`, inference-session machinery, `SessionAdmissionLedger`, return-equation state, and their algorithms ([dispatch_txn.rs:78-265](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:78), [dispatch_txn.rs:396-561](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:396), [dispatch_txn.rs:795-959](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:795)). Session retains `InlineRelationFlight`/`InlineFlowReturnFlight`/`InlineResolveCallFlight`, `ObservedGraphSelfRoot`, `CompletedSccMember`, `CompletedFlowReturnMember`, `CompletedResolveCallMember`, and completed-member publication queues ([dispatch_txn.rs:269-314](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:269), [dispatch_txn.rs:1763-1904](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:1763)). Consequently `RelationFrameState`, `FlowReturnFrameState`, `ResolveCallFrameState`, the three `*PendingState` types, the three `*DomainRuntime` types, and `CheckerDispatchTransaction` split internally: semantic state moves; flight/root/publication fields stay in a session wrapper.

- `flow_return.rs` — SPLITS. Move the result/value and evaluator authority: `FunctionReturnNode`, `ConsumerFold`, `FlowRootClose`, `FlowEvaluationOutcome`, `FlowFramePop`, `MemberDemandFilter`, `FlowBinderEnv`, `GuardNarrowing`, `NodeDisjointness`, `FlowEvaluator`, `FlowContribution`, `FlowBreakExit`, `ScopeShadow`, `FlowLayerState`, `Positional`, all pure helper functions, SCC/fixed-point computation, narrowing/join logic, and the `FlowEvaluator` algorithms ([flow_return.rs:42-297](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:42), [flow_return.rs:1594-1809](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:1594), [flow_return.rs:2559-3200](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:2559)). Session retains the live-capture/admission portions of `flow_return_context_for`, `resolve_call_context_for`, `execute_semantic_expression_source`, `execute_function_return_source`, `served_callee_clause`, `execute_flow_return`, `execute_flow_return_root`, `execute_flow_return_cold_build`, `flow_return_drain_completed_members`, and `build_flow_return` ([flow_return.rs:302-428](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:302), [flow_return.rs:592-713](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:592), [flow_return.rs:900-1137](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:900)). The mixed `evaluate_flow_return` symbol must decompose: immutable demand/evaluation logic moves, while indexed serving, fact capture, flow-slice store lookup, audit, and content reacquisition at lines 1971-2113 stay above ([flow_return.rs:1921-2113](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:1921)). Likewise, inline-flight claims/abort/publication inside `flow_frame_open`/`flow_frame_pop` stay in session while the frame/SCC transition math moves. `FlowEvaluator::direct_callee_clause` and `eval_call_via_resolve_call` move only after their live `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` calls are replaced by captured immutable observations ([flow_return.rs:7238-7254](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:7238), [flow_return.rs:7781-7790](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:7781)).

There is no cross-block ownership problem around `ObligationRuntime`. C1 relocates/separates the existing authority; D1, whose predecessor is C1, then extends that same semantic-owned symbol—never a peer ledger ([program.md:225-231](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:225), [dispatch_txn.rs:879-959](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:879)). D1 remains inseparable from D2 under ADR-014 ([ADR-014:13-19](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-014-atomic-flow-cutover-and-obligation-proof.md:13)).

This changes no accepted ADR, DAG edge, or program outcome. Structural enforcement remains the crate dependency firewall and sealed/capability-limited boundaries, never a new name-keyed scanner ([C1 revised:362-364](<<SESSION_SCRATCH>/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/C1-CHARTER-REVISED.md:362>)).

```text
flow_return.rs         | SPLITS | semantic values/evaluator/SCC math → verter_semantic; capture/cache/admission/audit → verter_session
flow_return_callee.rs  | MOVES  | entire file → verter_semantic
dispatch_txn.rs        | SPLITS | ObligationRuntime + semantic transaction state → verter_semantic; flight/root/publication carriers → verter_session
flow_slice_content.rs  | MOVES  | entire file → verter_semantic
```
